  site observer `Frame : J2000` (the state computed in `Frame.ICRF`, which equals the frame asked), and so did the
  orientation of a kernel-backed spacecraft; `frame-converter`, `orbital-parameters` and the orbital parameters of
  `propagate` rewrote it as `J2000`. Every command now resolves its frame arguments by one rule (internal
  `Helpers.ResolveFrame`): ICRF or J2000, in any case, is `Frame.ICRF`, labelled `J2000` on every path; any other name
  is `new Frame(name)`, which the library routes by its name (TEME, GCRF, CIRS, TIRS, #656). The numbers are unchanged
  (`EphemerisTests.IcrfIsLabelledJ2000_OnTheSpiceAndTheSitePaths`, ICRF, icrf and j2000 red on a85098d; the expected
  labels of `EphemerisTests` and `SpacecraftKernelsTests` updated). The output: Changed below.
- **The element conversions of `SpiceAPI` read the data provider under the SPICE lock** ([#664](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/664)).
  `ConvertStateVectorToConicOrbitalElement`, `ConvertEquinoctialElementsToStateVector`, `ConvertConicElementsToStateVector`
  and `Propagate2Bodies` (every overload) built the observer of their result, `new CelestialBody(id)`, inside
  `lock (lockObject)`: 9 calls of the data provider under the lock about the Earth (the information of 399, 3, 0, 10 and 0,
  four states), about 80 µs held for a native call of 1.8 µs (the issue's measure, 016237bd), and a custom `IDataProvider`
  ran under the lock. Only the native call, its check and the reading of SPICE's message now run under the lock, and the
  result carries the caller's observer (#725, under Changed), so no call reads the provider at all
  (`ColdStartTests.ElementConversions_ReadNoProviderUnderTheSpiceLock`, a child process on a probe provider that counts
  the calls made while the thread holds the lock: 9 of 9 for each of the ten overloads on a85098d, 0 of 0 now).
- **`SpiceAPI.ConvertEquinoctialElementsToStateVector` gave the state of another point of the orbit** ([#450](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/450)).
  `ProfilesConfiguration.Convert` passed the true longitude L0 to `eqncpv_c`, whose fourth element is the mean longitude
  (NAIF's documentation of `eqncpv_c`: "the mean longitude (mean0+argp+node) at the epoch of the elements"): every orbit
  whose mean and true longitudes differ came back off, 0.18 |r| for a LEO of e = 0.1 and 7.6 |r| at e = 0.89 (measured on
  a85098d; the issue's 1029 km and 27 900 km on 732bcc3). It now passes `MeanLongitude()`, right on every branch since
  #469, circular elements of f = −0.0 and equatorial ones included (#450's comment), and the unused reverse converter,
  which read the mean longitude as a true one and took p = a / (1 − e²), is removed. Against the 60-digit closed form of
  `tools/equinoctial_elements/equinoctial_reference.py` (the cases of #450 added under `eqncpv`, and every reference case
  within the domain of EQNCPV and a turn of its true longitude, 79 cases) the worst relative error is 1.0e-15 in position
  and velocity (`SpiceApiElementConversionTests.EquinoctialToState_MatchesTheReference`; 7.6 and 0.94 on a85098d).
  The domain checks of #711 are unchanged.
- **`SpiceAPI.WriteEphemeris` and `WriteOrientation` enumerated the caller's states under the SPICE lock** ([#661](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/661)).
  Both materialized the caller's `IEnumerable` inside `lock (lockObject)` (`WriteEphemeris` twice on 016237bd, when the
  issue was filed, once on a85098d), so a lazy sequence ran under the lock, and one that read `PlanetsAndMoons`, `Stars` or
  `Barycenters` for the first time could wait for a thread waiting for the lock (#623); the release note only warned the
  caller to pass an array. Each writer now materializes the sequence once, before the lock, with its checks on the array
  (empty, three states or more, one frame, the category of the centres; the names of the centres are still read from
  SPICE under the lock) and the conversion to the native records; only the unload of a replaced file and the native
  call run under the lock (`SpiceApiWriterEnumerationTests`: a sequence that counts its enumerations, records whether
  the thread holds the lock at each item, and has another thread take the lock during its first item: on a85098d one
  enumeration, all 10 items under the lock and the other thread blocked for its 60 s, both writers; now one enumeration,
  none under the lock, the lock taken). An array writes the same file, byte for byte.
- **The body information of a site identifier gave the Sun as centre** ([#651](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/651)).
  Both layers classed every identifier above 1000 as an asteroid, so `SpiceAPI.GetCelestialBodyInfo` of DSS-13 (399013),
  DSS-14 and DSS-65 gave the centre 10 and the barycentre 0 (measured on a85098d), where SPICE's SPK of the stations
  (`earthstns_itrf93_201023.bsp`) has their segments about the Earth (399, spiceypy `spksfs`), and
  `CelestialItem.IsAsteroid` was true for them. A site identifier (body × 1000 + site, the body a planet or a moon, the
  rule of `Site.NaifId`, internal `SpiceAPI.IsSiteId`) of a body SPICE names (internal `SpiceAPI.IsSiteOfNamedBody`, the
  body's name read under the SPICE lock) now has its body as centre and its body's barycentre as barycentre, in the
  record (`SpiceAPI` corrects the native record, the C++ layer unchanged) and in
  `CelestialItem.FindCenterOfMotionId`/`FindBarycenterOfMotionId`, and is no asteroid. SPICE's built-in NOTO (398989)
  and NEW NORCIA (398990), ESA stations whose identifiers have the form of a site of 398, a body SPICE does not name
  (spiceypy 8.4.0 `bodc2n`), keep 10 and 0 and stay asteroids, as before (`SiteIdentifierCentreTests`: the three
  stations against SPICE, red on a85098d, the Moon and the Earth as controls, sites of the Moon and Mars by the rule, and
  an asteroid, a comet, 391001, 399000, NOTO, NEW NORCIA and 101001, not sites, unchanged).
- **NOTO and NEW NORCIA as observers threw for a body 398** ([#750](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/750)).
  SPICE's built-in NOTO (398989) and NEW NORCIA (398990) have the form of a site of 398, a body SPICE does not name,
  which #651 kept out of `IsSiteOfNamedBody`, but four call sites still tested `IsSiteId` and built them as a site of the
  body 398 (`new CelestialBody(398)`): the observer of `SpiceAPI.ReadEphemeris` by identifiers (both overloads), the
  centre of a frame on the reference-body path, and the objects of the CLI's `ephemeris` and `sub-point`. Each threw
  `ArgumentException` "The NAIF identifier 398 has no name in SPICE" (`naifId`), an identifier the caller never gave
  (measured on f70ee32). They now test `IsSiteOfNamedBody`; an identifier of the form of a site whose body SPICE does not
  name is an object of the kernels read by its identifier (internal `Body.KernelObject`, a `CelestialItem` named as SPICE
  names it), so the read is `spkezr_c`'s: the state with its SPK loaded, SPICE's missing-data error
  (`InvalidOperationException`) otherwise; a frame centre of that form is read from SPICE by its identifier
  (`KernelObjectObserverTests`, with an SPK of NOTO the test writes: NOTO as observer the negation of NOTO as target,
  bit for bit, and `spkezr_c`'s read with "NOTO" as observer for the nine corrections in J2000 and ITRF93, bit for bit
  (Validation); the window read; NEW NORCIA without its SPK SPICE's error; the Moon in a TK frame centred on NOTO from a
  site built from coordinates against its closed form; the CLI's `ephemeris` from NOTO and its `sub-point`,
  `EphemerisTests.Ephemeris_FromNoto_AndItsSubPoint_AreTheLibrarysReads`; red on f70ee32). `sub-point` decides whether
  its object is a site once its kernels are loaded, so that a kernel naming a body counts. `CelestialItem.Create` and
  `new CelestialBody` of these identifiers still throw: they have no frame.
- **A spacecraft or a custom body had the solar system barycentre as centre of motion** ([#747](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/747)).
  The constructor of an item built from custom parameters (`Spacecraft`, both constructors, and the custom
  `CelestialBody`) never set `CenterOfMotionId` and `BarycenterOfMotionId`: both stayed 0 whatever the orbit (a
  spacecraft about the Earth, 0 and 0, measured on f70ee32), while the natural-body constructors give the Moon 399 and
  3. They now are the observer of the initial orbital parameters and that observer's barycentre (the observer itself
  when it is a barycentre, that of its body for a site, that of a spacecraft for a spacecraft about it), 0 and 0
  without an initial orbit, as before, and `Spacecraft.SetInitialOrbitalParameters` sets them again from the new orbit
  (`CustomItemCenterOfMotionTests`: a spacecraft and a custom body about the Earth, the Moon, the Sun, the Earth-Moon
  and the Mars barycentres and the solar system barycentre, the static Earth, a spacecraft about a spacecraft, LRO from
  its kernels about the Earth and the Moon, a spacecraft moved from the Earth to the Moon, Mars, the Earth-Moon
  barycentre and back, from the Moon to the Sun, and one built without an orbit and given one, the barycentre against
  the record of `SpiceAPI.GetCelestialBodyInfo`; red on f70ee32). No library code reads the two values of such an item.
- **No CDM the library wrote validated against the SANA schema** ([#615](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/615)). `CdmWriter` put the root,
  `cdm` or the `ndm` that wraps it, in the namespace `urn:ccsds:schema:ndmxml` with every other element, so the SANA
  NDM/XML 4.0.0 qualified master, which declares `ndm` and `cdm` in no namespace (no `targetNamespace`), rejected every
  CDM written by `CdmWriter`, `Cdm.WriteTo*` and `EncounterCase.ToCdm(...).WriteTo*`, wrapped or not, at the root ("No
  matching global declaration available for the validation root", lxml 6.1.3 and .NET's validator on the embedded
  master, measured on a85098d); the library's own check accepted it through a synthetic root in the namespace. The writer
  now writes the qualified form of CCSDS 508.0-B-1 Cor. 2, 4.3.3: the root in no namespace with
  `xmlns:ndm="urn:ccsds:schema:ndmxml"` and `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation` (SANA's qualified master, identical to the
  embedded one; optional in the issue, kept, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18) declared on it, every element below it, the `cdm` of an `ndm` included, in the namespace under the
  prefix `ndm` (`CdmTests.WriteTo_RootOutsideTheNamespace_ValidatesAgainstTheSanaQualifiedMaster`:
  the written text, through `WriteToString` wrapped and bare, `WriteToStream` and `WriteToFile`, validated against the
  embedded master compiled in the test with no synthetic root, 4 cases red on a85098d). `Cdm.ValidateSchema` checks it
  as a standard form; a root in the namespace, the form written before, is still read and checked as before
  (`ReadFromString_RootInTheNamespace_FormWrittenBefore615_IsStillReadAndValidated`).
- **The CDM writer read a date without a kind as local time** ([#617](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/617)). `CdmWriter` wrote every date
  through `ToUniversalTime()`, which takes a `DateTime` of kind `Unspecified`, that of `new DateTime(y, M, d, h, m, s)`,
  as local time: on a machine outside UTC a CDM built by hand was written with its eight dates (`CREATION_DATE`, `TCA`,
  the screen period, the screen entry and exit, `TIME_LASTOB_START`/`END`) shifted by the zone's offset, a TCA of
  2010-03-13T22:37:52.618 written `2010-03-13T21:37:52.6180000Z` under Europe/Paris and `2010-03-14T03:37:52.6180000Z`
  under America/New_York (measured on a85098d), while `EncounterCase.ToCdm` took such a date as UTC. The writer and the
  exporter now share one rule (internal `CcsdsDates.ToUtc`): `Utc` as given, `Unspecified` taken as UTC, `Local`
  converted. The OPM and OMM writers wrote a local time as its clock reading whatever `TIME_SYSTEM`; their dates in
  `TIME_SYSTEM` now convert it under UTC and refuse it under any other, `CREATION_DATE` converting it (Changed, below).
  `CcsdsLocalTimeTests` runs the three writers in child processes under `TZ=Europe/Paris` and `TZ=America/New_York`,
  the expected texts from the IANA rules of each zone (2 cases red on a85098d); `CdmTests`,
  `OpmWriterTests` and `OmmWriterTests` check each kind in the test process (8 refusals red on a85098d).
- **The CDM named its collision probability method `FOSTER-2D`, which no registry holds** ([#618](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/618), with
  [#342](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/342)). `EncounterCase.ToCdm` wrote
  `COLLISION_PROBABILITY_METHOD = FOSTER-2D`, or `FOSTER-2D-MAX-PC` for an encounter flagged
  `SingleCovarianceMaximumPcUsed` (reached only by a case built by hand with both covariances), neither in the SANA
  registry `cdm_cpm`, so a receiver that maps the method through the registry could not tell which Pc it was given. The
  method the analysis computes, Foster and Estes (1992), is `FOSTER-1992` there and in the examples of CCSDS 508.0-B-1
  Cor. 2 (annex E, 3.6.3, 4.4): it is now written (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17). The single-covariance maximum Pc
  has no registered value and a CDM carries both covariances: an encounter flagged so is refused, as one with a single
  covariance already was, and the dead branch is gone (`CdmTests.ToCdm_ManualEncounter_ExportsExpectedValues` and
  `ToCdm_SingleCovarianceMaximumPc_IsRefused`, red on a85098d). No number moves.
- **The OPM and OMM writers lost digits** ([#728](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/728)). Their `FormatDouble` kept `G17` only in scientific
  form and otherwise wrote `0.##############`: at most 14 decimals and, a .NET custom format, 15 significant digits.
  A written message no longer read back as the values written: an eccentricity of 0.00012345678901234567 was written
  0.00012345678901 (1.9e-11 relative), a mean motion of 10.270509831248424 rev/day 10.2705098312484, and over 1e5 values
  in [1e-4, 1e3) 81.6 % were lost, by up to 4.9e-11 relative (measured on a85098d), every value of the OPM (state
  vector, Keplerian elements, spacecraft parameters, covariance, maneuvers) and of the OMM (mean elements, spacecraft
  and TLE parameters, covariance). The OPM, OMM and CDM writers now share one form (internal `CcsdsValues.Format`), the
  shortest round-trip form `"R"`, which reads back bit for bit as `xsd:double` (`OpmWriterTests` and `OmmWriterTests`
  `WriteToString_EveryRealValue_ReadsBackBitForBit`: each written text read by `double.Parse` and by the reader, the
  value given bit for bit, 44 OPM and 35 or 36 OMM values, all but one lost before, red on a85098d).
- **The OPM writers wrote `REF_FRAME = J2000`, which is not a CCSDS frame name** ([#339](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/339); decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-18). `Opm.CreateFromStateVector` and `Spacecraft.ToOpm` wrote the SPICE name of the state's
  frame, `J2000` for `Frame.ICRF`, under `REF_FRAME`, and `ToOpm` under each `MAN_REF_FRAME` too: no CCSDS list of
  reference frames holds it, `OpmValidator` warned "Reference frame 'J2000' is not a standard CCSDS frame." on the
  library's own OPMs, and a receiver that maps the frame through the CCSDS names could not read them. Both now write
  the CCSDS name of the frame (internal `CCSDS/Common/CcsdsFrameNames`): `ICRF` for `Frame.ICRF`, the frame's own name
  otherwise, which is already the CCSDS one for `Frame.GCRF` (`GCRF`), `Frame.TEME`, `ECLIPJ2000`, `ITRF93`, `B1950`
  and `FK4`. `ICRF` and `GCRF` both read back as `Frame.ICRF` (they share its axes), the state bit for bit
  (`OpmTests.CreateFromStateVector_WritesTheCcsdsNameOfTheFrame`, `SpacecraftTests.ToOpm_CarriesTheExecutedImpulses`
  and `ToOpm_ExportsTheCovarianceOfTheInitialStateInKm2`, `SpacecraftToOpmTests.Propagated_WritesTheStateMassAndManeuversOfTheEpoch`:
  7 cases red on f70ee32, each `Expected: "ICRF"`, `Actual: "J2000"`). No number moves.
- **A TLE without an international designator could not be re-created or carried through an OMM** ([#604](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/604); decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-18). Columns 10-17 of line 1 may be blank, and `new TLE(...)` reads such a TLE, but `TLE.Create`
  threw `ArgumentException` (`cosparId`) for a null or blank designator and `TLE.ToOmm` "Object ID is required."
  (`objectId`), its blank columns giving an empty `OBJECT_ID` that `OmmMetadata` refuses: of the 15 919 TLEs of the
  study of lot 5 of #457, 11801 and 88888 of Vallado's `SGP4-VER.TLE`. `TLE.Create` now writes eight blanks for a null
  or blank `cosparId`, `TLE.ToOmm` writes `OBJECT_ID = UNKNOWN` (the element is mandatory in the ODM; CCSDS's value for an
  unknown designator, confirmed by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18), and `Omm.ToTle` reads `UNKNOWN`, trimmed and in any letter case,
  back as the blank columns (internal `OmmMetadata.UnknownObjectId`). Both TLEs go through `Create`, and through
  `ToOmm`, the XML written and read and `ToTle`, to their own text, each field at its columns, but for the ephemeris type
  of 11801, blank in the set and written 0 (SGP4's) by `Create` as for every TLE (`TleBlankDesignatorTests`, 15 cases
  red on f70ee32). The fit of `OrbitalParameters.ToTLE(Configuration)` goes through `TLE.Create` too: a null or blank
  `Configuration.CosparId` threw "TLE conversion using Equinoctial elements failed after 15 iterations"
  (`InvalidOperationException`; the `ArgumentException` of the designator was caught inside the fit) and now writes the
  blank columns, the lines otherwise those of the same fit with a designator, the checksum of line 1 recomputed
  (`TleBlankDesignatorTests.ToTLE_NullOrBlankCosparId_WritesBlankColumns`, 3 cases red on f70ee32). An empty `OBJECT_ID`
  is still refused by the reader and `OmmMetadata`, as #708 decided (S. Guillet, 2026-11-16); the decision of #604 also
  reads an empty value as the blank columns, which the internal conversion does, but no OMM reaches it with one: whether
  the reader should accept an empty `OBJECT_ID` is open, for S. Guillet to settle. No number moves.
- **The CCSDS readers loaded a date outside the standard's forms** ([#619](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/619), the date half).
  `CcsdsEpochParser`, which the CDM, OPM and OMM readers share since #490, passed a text outside the date branch of
  `epochType`, and a calendar text with a field out of range, to `DateTime.TryParse`: a `TCA` or an `EPOCH` of
  `22:37:52.618` was read on the day of the read (2026-11-17T22:37:52.618), `1.5` and `1,5` as 5 January of the current
  year, `2010-03-13` as its midnight, and `13 March 2010 22:37:52.618`, `03/13/2010 …`, RFC 1123, a space or a lowercase
  `t` for the `T`, a lowercase `z`, a decimal comma, a missing second, a `+0100` or `+01` offset and a blank around the
  date as the date they spell (measured on a85098d; the pattern's `$` also matched before a final line feed). CCSDS
  508.0-B-1 §6.3.2.6 and 502.0-B-3 allow two forms, `yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss[.d→d][Z]` and `yyyy-dddThh:mm:ss[.d→d][Z]`,
  "All fields require leading zeros", and lxml 6.1.3 with the repository's NDM/XML 4.0.0 schema rejects each of these
  texts as an `epochType` but `1.5`, the type's bare-number branch, which the standards do not allow in a date field.
  The parser now reads the two forms only (with the `±hh:mm` offset of `epochType`, the pattern anchored with `\z`), and
  the readers throw their parse exception naming the field and the text (`CcsdsEpochParserTests`
  `TextOutsideTheTwoForms_IsRejected` and `Readers_RejectTextOutsideTheTwoForms`, `CdmTests`
  `ReadFromString_DateOutsideTheTwoForms_ThrowsCdmParseException`: 32 rows red on a85098d). Dates in the two forms read
  bit for bit as before (the `CcsdsEpochParserTests` of #490 against CSPICE's `str2et`); none of the CDMs of the
  conformance suite moves. The same issue's `units="km"` on a `lengthTypeUO` length is refused (Changed below:
  `CdmTests.ReadFromString_OptionalUnitLengthNotInMeters_ThrowsCdmParseException`, 10 rows red on a85098d).

- **The OPM and OMM unit conversions overflowed to ±Infinity** ([#729](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/729)). `OpmStateVector.ToStateVector`
  multiplied km and km/s by 1000 and `CovarianceMatrix.ToMatrixWithUnitConversion` km², km²/s and km²/s² by 1e6 without
  a check: a finite value above about 1.8e305 km (1.8e302 km²) became ±Infinity in the `StateVector` of
  `Opm.ToStateVector` or in its covariance (measured on a85098d: `X` 1e306 gave +Infinity m, `CX_X` 1e303 +Infinity m²),
  where the CDM reader refuses such a value since #708. `OpmStateVector` and `CovarianceMatrix` now refuse a value whose
  product is not finite (Changed below), and the OPM and OMM readers report it as `OpmParseException` or
  `OmmParseException` naming the keyword and its text. `KeplerianElements.FromOMM` computed (n × 2π) / 86400, whose
  product overflowed above about 2.86e307 rev/day where the quotient is finite: it now takes the same two roundings on
  n × 2⁻¹⁰ and 86400 × 2⁻¹⁰ there, the value an unbounded exponent gives, and is bit for bit unchanged below.
  `Omm.ToTle`, its one caller in the library, converted that value back with `TLE.Create`, whose product overflowed over
  the same range: an OMM with `MEAN_MOTION` 3e307 gave, without an exception, a TLE whose mean motion field was the text
  `Infinity` (measured with the `FromOMM` change above). `ToTle` now refuses a `MEAN_MOTION` above the 99.99999999 rev/day of its
  11-character field (columns 53 to 63 of line 2), naming the keyword (Changed below;
  `OmmTests.ToTle_MeanMotionBeyondTheTleField_ThrowsNamingMeanMotion`, 5 rows red, two of them with no exception). References:
  the IEEE 754 bounds (the largest double whose product is finite, 1.7976931348623156e305 for 1000 and
  1.7976931348623154e302 for 1e6, stored and converted as given) and the two roundings in exact rational arithmetic
  (`OpmStateVectorTests`, `CovarianceMatrixTests`, `OpmReaderTests`, `OmmReaderTests` `*OverflowingInSiUnits*` and
  `TLETests.FromOMM_MeanMotionAboveTheOverflowOfTheProduct_IsTheExtendedExponentQuotient`: 100 rows red on a85098d).

- **`CdmCovarianceMatrix.StateCovarianceRtn` accepted a matrix that is not 6×6** ([#730](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/730)). Its init
  accessor checked the terms since #717, whatever the size: a 3×3 matrix or `default(Matrix)` built, and `CdmWriter`
  then threw `IndexOutOfRangeException` or `NullReferenceException` (`Cdm.Validate` reported the size when it ran). It
  now throws `ArgumentException` naming `StateCovarianceRtn` before the terms (Changed below; `CdmTests`
  `Init_CovarianceNotSixBySix_*` and `Init_DefaultCovarianceMatrix_*`, 8 rows red on a85098d). The reader always built a
  6×6 matrix, so reading is unchanged.

- **`TleParameters` named `revNumber` in its exception** ([#734](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/734)). A negative revolution number threw
  `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` with the `ParamName` `revNumber`, the private validator's parameter, which no public entry
  has; it names `revolutionNumberAtEpoch`, the parameter of the constructor and of the four `CreateWith*` factories
  (Changed below), and `OmmReader` maps `REV_AT_EPOCH` to it, so its `OmmParseException` still names the keyword
  (`TleParametersTests.Entry_NegativeRevolutionNumber_NamesRevolutionNumberAtEpoch` and
  `OmmReaderTests.ReadFromString_NegativeRevAtEpoch_NamesTheKeywordAndTheParameter`, 6 rows red on a85098d).

- **`Constants.Parsec2Meters` was truncated** ([#733](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/733)).
  It was 3.085677581e16 m, 1.592e-10 relative below the parsec, 648000/π au exactly (IAU 2015 Resolution B2) with the
  au of 149597870700 m (IAU 2012 Resolution B2), 30856775814913672.789 m. It is now 3.0856775814913673e16, the nearest
  double, 30856775814913672 m (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17): the quotient at 40 digits (mpmath) and in decimal (28
  digits), each read back by `double.Parse` (`StarTests.Parsec2Meters_Is648000OverPiAstronomicalUnits`, red on a85098d).
  It sets a star's distance from its parallax: every `Star.Distance`, and every position of a star from the solar system
  barycenter, grows by 1.592e-10 relative (a parallax of 0.3792″: 8.13733539293249e16 m before, 8.13733539422829e16 m
  now, within 3 roundings of the exact quotient, `StarTests.Create`, which held the old snapshot), its direction from
  the barycenter unchanged bit for bit; from an observer at r_obs the direction moves by at most |r_obs|/r · 1.6e-10
  (6e-16 rad for a star at 1.3 pc seen from 1 au). The tests of the straight line of #718 measure against the star's own
  `Distance` and do not move. The reference of `StarOccultationTests`
  (`tools/occultation_reference/star_occultation_reference.py`, spiceypy 8.4.0, CSPICE N0067) takes the new parsec: its
  parallaxes, declinations and directions move in their last digit, its edges not at all; the test's literals are
  regenerated, its worst edge 2.38 µs and direction 1.19e-16 rad on Linux x64, within the thresholds of 4.8e-6 s and
  4.4e-16 rad.

- **A `Star` accepted a parallax that gives no distance** ([#732](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/732)).
  The constructor stored any parallax and set `Distance` to 1/parallax parsecs, silently: 0 gave +∞ (−0 −∞) and
  positions of infinities, a negative parallax a negative distance that put the star in the opposite direction (cosine −1
  with its catalog direction for −0.5″; Gaia DR3 holds many negative parallaxes), NaN a NaN distance, ±∞ a distance of
  0, and a positive parallax below about 1.7e-292″ a distance that overflowed to +∞ (measured on a85098d). The
  constructor now throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` naming `parallax`, its value as `ActualValue`, for each of them,
  0 included (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17: refused, not a star at infinity, which every state, SPK and occultation
  path would have to handle) (`StarTests.Constructor_AParallaxThatGivesNoDistance_Throws`, 9 values, red on a85098d;
  `Constructor_APositiveParallax_GivesAFiniteDistance` for 1e-291″, 1e-6″ and 1e300″). Every star of the test suite
  keeps its parallax.

- **The state of a star carried a zero velocity while its position moved** ([#731](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/731)).
  Since #718 a star moves along a straight line, but `GetGeometricStateRelativeTo` gave a zero velocity from the
  barycenter and the opposite of the reference body's velocity from another, `GetEphemeris` the opposite of the
  observer's, and `Propagate`, `PropagateAsync`, `Scenario.SimulateAsync` and so the SPK of `WriteEphemeris` a zero
  velocity: Barnard's star seen from the Earth had a velocity 1.12 relative away from the reference (its 89 km/s
  missing), its range rate 53.4 m/s (its velocity along the line of sight, turned by its proper motion since 2016;
  measured on a85098d). The state now carries the star's space velocity, the derivative of its straight line,
  r0 (μα* e_α + μδ e_δ) per Julian year of TDB, constant (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17): against the derivative of
  the straight line in long double (`tools/sofa_reference/starpm_ref.c --velocity`), every star of the harness at 0 to
  1000 years, 1.98e-16 relative (`StarVelocityTests.GetGeometricStateRelativeTo_Velocity_IsTheDerivativeOfTheStraightLine`,
  1 before); against the derivative of `iauStarpm` (rv = 0, central differences over ±1 year) with its two terms the
  model does not take added in closed form (`iauStarpv`'s inertial radial velocity −c β²/(√(1 − β²) + 1) ≈ −v_t²/(2c)
  along the catalog direction, 1.5e-4 of Barnard's speed, and its light time from the catalog epoch, a rate scaled by
  1 − (ṙ(dt) − ṙ(0))/c), 3.62e-10 relative, the resolution of the central difference for Polaris
  (`IsTheDerivativeOfIauStarpm`); within 6.2e-16 of the position of the central difference of the library's own
  positions (`IsTheRateOfThePosition`); from the Earth, the space velocity minus the Earth's velocity from SPICE
  (`GetEphemeris_FromTheEarth_IsTheSpaceVelocityMinusTheEarths`); and read back by `spkezr` from the SPK of
  `WriteEphemeris`, 1.84e-16 relative (`WriteEphemeris_TheSpkHoldsTheSpaceVelocity`); all red on a85098d. Thresholds
  twice the worst over Linux x64, Windows x64 and macOS arm64 (the same figures on the three). The positions of the star's own
  states are unchanged, bit for bit; the rate of the stellar aberration of the `+S` corrections, which takes the
  relative velocity, follows. A star as observer takes its space velocity too, which moves positions on the paths that
  integrate it (the Changed entry below). The limit of the [Stars](../reference/stars.md#the-velocity) page is removed.

- **The state of Keplerian elements near e = 1** ([#472](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/472)). `ToStateVector()` took p = a(1 − e·e),
  r = p / (1 + e cos ν) and v ∝ e + cos ν: 1 − e·e kept the rounding of e·e divided by |1 − e²|, and near the apoapsis
  and the asymptote of a hyperbola the two other products kept the rounding of cos ν divided by 1 + e cos ν or 1 − e.
  Outside the parabolic band the state was off by up to 2.2e-11 relative away from the apsides and 8.1e-11 near them
  (e = 0.999 to 1.001, q = 7000 km: 155 m at the apoapsis of e = 0.999999), and `ToEquinoctial().P` of
  `KeplerianElements` by 2.2e-11. Now p = (a (1 − e))(1 + e) for 0.5 ≤ e ≤ 2, where 1 − e is exact (Sterbenz's lemma),
  and 1 + e cos ν = (1 − e) + 2e cos²(ν/2), e + cos ν = 2 cos²(ν/2) − (1 − e) for 0.5 ≤ e ≤ 1.2 (choices 1 and 2,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18). Against the conic state of the double elements at 60 digits
  (`tools/conic_state/conic_state_reference.py`, mpmath), 301 points of e = 0.1 to 3 with ν at the periapsis, the
  apoapsis (π ± 1e-1 to 1e-6, fl(π)) and up to 0.9999 of the asymptote: p within 1.7e-16, the state within 4.5e-16 in
  position and 3.1e-16 in velocity away from the apsides, 3.7e-15 near them for e = 0.999 to 1.001
  (`ConicStateTests`, red on f70ee32; the same on Linux x64, Windows x64 and macOS arm64, thresholds twice the worst,
  CI run 44395076184). Near the asymptote of a hyperbola
  beyond e = 1.01 the rounding of cos ν divided by 1 + e cos ν stays (2.8e-13 at e = 1.2, 0.9999 of ν∞), which neither
  form lowers. Below e = 0.5 and above e = 2 p and the state are unchanged, bit for bit. The state floors of
  `KeplerEquationTests`, set by this loss at its NaN regression (1.652 of the floor), tighten from 3.4 to 1.9 and 1.7.

- **Kepler's equation near the periapsis at e → 1** ([#484](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/484)). Near the periapsis x − e sin x and e sinh x − x
  differ by about (1 − e) x + x³/6, so the residual of the solver and the reverse direction kept the rounding of
  e sin x, about ε x, divided by 1 − e: E up to 9.3e5 ulp off at e = 0.999999 (1.4e5 at e = 1.00001, 902 at 0.999,
  9 to 10 iterations), M = E − e sin E (`StateVector.MeanAnomaly()`, `TrueAnomalyToMeanAnomaly`) up to 1.9e-10 of M,
  and the states from a mean anomaly within two periapsis radii up to 6.7e-11 of |r|. Both directions now evaluate
  (1 − e) x + e (x − sin x) and (e − 1) x + e (sinh x − x), x − sin x and sinh x − x by their series to x¹⁹/19! below 1,
  for 0.5 ≤ e ≤ 2 (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18; the same rewriting as R. H. Gooding and A. W. Odell's EMKEP,
  Celestial Mechanics 44, 1988, confirmed by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18): against the root and M* at 60 digits
  (`tools/kepler_equation/kepler_periapsis_reference.py`, mpmath), E within 1.9 ulp in 6 iterations at most, M within
  6.4e-16, the states within 9.7e-16 of |r| and the anomaly of the round trip state → elements within 2 ulp (6.2e5
  before) (`KeplerPeriapsisTests`, red on f70ee32; the worst over Linux x64, Windows x64 and macOS arm64, thresholds
  twice that, CI run 44395076184). The derivative, the
  start, the stop and the cap of the solver are unchanged. Below e = 0.5 and above e = 2, where the former forms lose at
  most a factor 2, every result is unchanged, bit for bit.

- **The periapsis of a parabola** ([#737](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/737)). `PerigeeVector()` was a(1 − e) P̂, ∞ × 0 = NaN at e = 1
  exactly, and so `PerigeeVelocity()`; within 1e-6 of e = 1 it is now q P̂, q the perigee radius of the band, from which
  its state comes (outside the band a(1 − e) P̂ as before, bit for bit): for the parabola of the issue (q = 7000 km), 7000 km
  and √(2μ/q) = 10 671.73 m/s, vis-viva (`ElementsValidationTests.Issue737_*`, red on f70ee32).
- **Keplerian elements of a semi-major axis of the wrong sign** ([#738](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/738)). The constructor accepted a < 0 for
  e < 1, a > 0 for e > 1 and a = 0 outside the parabolic band, which no conic has (p = a (1 − e²) > 0): `ToStateVector()`
  returned a NaN velocity without an exception, and `AtEpoch` threw naming the mean anomaly (the mean motion NaN). It
  throws now (Changed below; `ElementsValidationTests.Issue738_*`, red on f70ee32).

- **The two-body motion of the near-parabolic band** ([#753](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/753)). Within 1e-6 of e = 1 the motion advanced
  Barker's anomaly at Barker's rate √(μ/(2q³)) (#459), exact at e = 1 only: 0.088 m from the exact motion of the conic
  after 600 s at |e − 1| = 5e-7, 0.16 m at 9e-7, 0.54 m from the periapsis, 3.1 km after a day at 9.9e-7 (1.3e-5 of
  |r|), and `TimeToRadius` up to 1.5e-3 s off; Kepler's equation of the conic, the other model measured by #459, is
  kilometres off near e = 1. The motion of the band but at e = 1 exactly (`AtEpoch`, `ToStateVector(Time)`,
  `ToKeplerianElements(Time)`, `EpochAtMeanAnomaly`, `TimeToRadius`, the first state of a propagation from such elements)
  is now that of the conic of e and q in universal variables from the periapsis, √μ t = q χ + e χ³ S(z) with the
  Stumpff functions, solved by a safeguarded Newton's method from Barker's root (internal `UniversalKepler`, the form of
  CSPICE's `prop2b_c`; D. A. Vallado, *Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications*, algorithm 8, confirmed by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-18), the elements at the new epoch carrying its true anomaly and Barker's mean anomaly of it, the anomalies of
  the band (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18: in the band only, `IsParabolic()` keeping its meaning). Against the exact
  conic at 60 digits (`tools/near_parabolic`, sections 9 and 10), 108 motions of the band (|e − 1| from 1e-12 to 9.9e-7 on
  both sides, ν0 from −1.5 to 2 rad, 600 s, a day, −1 h): within 6.8e-15 of |r| and 3.6e-15 of |v| (1.2e-7 m after a
  day), the states of #459 600 s later within 3 nm, and the times to a radius to the tick
  (`NearParabolicBandTests.Issue753_*`, red on f70ee32; the worst over Linux x64, Windows x64 and macOS arm64,
  thresholds twice that, CI run 44395076184). At e = 1 exactly
  Barker's law and outside the band Kepler's equation are unchanged, bit for bit. Next to the band, at e = 1 − 1.1e-6
  before the periapsis, the ellipse is still 3.1 m off after 600 s (1.9e-7 of |r|): the constructor keeps its mean
  anomaly in [0, 2π), where it rounds (#471, not part of 11.0.0); on the hyperbola side 9.4e-10.

- **The CLI's coordinate search read neither the coordinate systems nor the coordinates its help listed**
  ([#652](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/652)). The help of
  `find-windows-from-coordinate-constraint` listed the coordinate systems `LATITUDINAL`, `SPHERICAL` and `CYLINDRICAL`
  and the coordinate `COLATITUDE`, which the library has not, and the command read both arguments by member name only
  (`Enum.Parse`), so that `RA/DEC` and `RIGHT ASCENSION`, the values the help showed, ended in "Requested value was not
  found" (measured on f70ee32). The help now lists exactly the members of `CoordinateSystem` (`RECTANGULAR`, `RA/DEC`,
  `GEODETIC`, `PLANETOGRAPHIC`) and `Coordinate` (`X`, `Y`, `Z`, `ALTITUDE`, `DECLINATION`, `LATITUDE`, `LONGITUDE`,
  `RADIUS`, `RANGE`, `RIGHT ASCENSION`); both arguments are read by description, as the relational operator, or by
  member name (`RaDec`, `RightAscension`), in any case, before the kernels are loaded; an unknown value throws
  `ArgumentException` naming its argument and listing the values the command reads; a coordinate the system has not is
  SPICE's error, as before (`GeometryFinderTests.CoordinateConstraint_HelpListsTheValuesOfTheEnumerations`,
  `_ReadsDescriptionsAndMemberNames` against the search of `SpiceAPI` with the members, `_UnknownValue_ThrowsListingTheValues`,
  `_EveryListedValueIsRead`, red on f70ee32; `_CoordinateOfAnotherSystem_ThrowsSpiceError`). The latitudinal, spherical
  and cylindrical systems and the colatitude are not added. The entry under Known limitations is removed.

- **`Time.ToLocal()` of an instant in the first repeated hour was an hour later** ([#751](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/751);
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18). `LocalTimeFrame` builds the local label with `DateTime.ToLocalTime()`, which marks
  an instant of the first of the two repeated hours of a fall transition as daylight time, but the `Time` constructor
  called `DateTime.SpecifyKind(…, Local)`, which drops that mark, so the label was read back with the standard offset:
  in America/New_York, 2025-11-02T05:30Z gave local 01:30, whose `ToUTC()` is 06:30Z, and `utc == utc.ToLocal()` was
  false, for every instant of 05:00Z to 06:00Z, 60 of the 481 minutes about the transition (measured on f70ee32). The
  constructor keeps a `DateTime` of kind `Local` in the repeated hour as it is, so a conversion changes the label, not the instant
  (#512): over both transitions of 2025, every minute from 4 h before to 4 h after each, `ToLocal()` is the calendar of
  the zone's rule, equals the instant and converts back to it to the tick
  (`ColdStartTests.ToLocal_KeepsTheInstant_AcrossTheTransitionsOfDaylightSavingTime`, a child in America/New_York,
  skipped on Windows, where `TZ` does not set the zone; red on f70ee32). A label built from the calendar of the repeated
  hour still reads with the standard offset (documented on [Time and Windows](../reference/time-and-windows.md)). The
  mark is kept only while the label is in the repeated hour, and dropped outside it (`TimeZoneInfo.Local.IsAmbiguousTime`):
  the arithmetic of a local time, that of its calendar, carries the mark (`DateTime.AddTicks` keeps it), and a mark kept
  everywhere made a label moved out of the hour and back read with the daylight offset where an equal label of the same
  calendar read with the standard one, 1 h after the local time of 05:30Z then 1 h before giving 05:30Z, and the same steps from the local time
  of 07:30Z, the same instant, calendar and frame, 06:30Z (630 of 2706 such pairs of labels about the transition
  differed after the same step of ±30, ±60 or ±90 min; the child's check, red before the mark was dropped). The limit
  stated there since #512 is removed.

- **A second `Propagate` on one `CentralBodyPropagator` under an adaptive RK7(8) was not a fresh run**
  ([#782](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/782), decisions 21, 22 and 25 of lot L4
  of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-22). `RK78Integrator` resets its step and the history of its PI controller only in `Initialize`, which the
  propagator called at construction and after each event, never at the start of a run: since #583 a second run re-armed
  the spacecraft, but its first segment started from the step the first run proposed last (188 to 340 s against the
  initial 60 s in LEO, the maximum step of a day in SSB mode) and from its last error. Measured at 1dc77ffc, run 2 against
  a fresh spacecraft and propagator, Linux x64 (`PropagatorReuseTests`): 119 of 121 outputs off, up to 1.7e-5 m, one step
  fewer, on a 2 h point-mass LEO at 1e-10; 180 of 181 outputs, up to 2.0e-5 m, with EGM2008 10×10, the Moon, the Sun,
  NRLMSISE-00, SRP, a prograde attitude and an apogee impulse over 3 h (83 + 48 steps against 83 + 52), the burn, ΔV, fuel
  and attitude record off; every element of Φ and P off with the covariance asked for, under Auto, and with process
  noise, consider parameters and the step control (136 steps against 135); 2 steps against 13 and 1.5e-4 m in SSB mode at
  1e-12 over 2 days; 3.5e-5 m after a run stopped inside its first segment (a stop past an impulse was fresh by chance,
  the event having re-initialized the integrator); 1.7e-5 m for a subclass of `PropagatorBase` and 38 m for a
  bare `IIntegrator` wrapping an RK7(8) (its outputs, a cubic Hermite of its steps, on another step grid), whose
  `Initialize` the library never called again. Every library path builds a new
  propagator per run (`Spacecraft.Propagate`, `Scenario.Simulate`, `BatchPropagator`, `MonteCarloPropagator`, the
  avoidance options and the non-linearity index), so only a propagator a caller ran twice was affected. `Propagate` now
  initializes the integrator with the initial state of the propagation at the start of every run, once the token is read
  (a token already cancelled still changes nothing, decision 6) and before the re-arm (an `Initialize` that throws
  changes nothing); runs 2 and 3 of an instance are bit for bit a fresh run in every case above, after a completed or a
  stopped run (positions, velocities, steps, stored states arc by arc, attitude record as rotation angles, executed
  maneuvers and their windows to the tick, fuel, Φ and P; `RepropagationTests` gains a `SameInstance` path). The solutions
  of the runs of one instance share one lock of their forces, held by each run (decision 25): before, each run took a
  new lock, so an evaluation of an earlier solution could run concurrently with a later run over the same force instances,
  whose partials are not reentrant (found by reading the code, not measured). The lock is held for the whole run, the
  caller's forces included (decision 28 of lot L4 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-22), so the runs of an
  instance, two concurrent `Propagate` calls on it and the evaluations of its earlier solutions serialize, with three
  consequences, stated in `docs/guides/thread-safety.md`, both CLAUDE.md files, the remarks of `Propagate` and the
  cancellation section of `docs/reference/propagators.md`: code a run calls (a `ForceBase`, a bare `IIntegrator`) must
  not evaluate the solution of another propagator that may be running, since two reused instances whose forces evaluate
  each other's earlier solutions deadlock (the library evaluates no solution under the SPICE lock or the lock of an
  attitude record, so it cannot deadlock by itself); an evaluation of an earlier solution on another thread waits for
  the end of the run of the instance in progress, and then gives the values it gave before
  (`PropagatorReuseTests.AnEvaluationOfRunOne_WaitsForTheEndOfRunTwo`, red at 1dc77ffc, where it returned while run 2
  was held inside a force); a `Propagate` waiting for the lock reads its token once it holds it. Velocity-Verlet and a fixed-step RK7(8) keep
  no step state and were already fresh; every first run is bit for bit unchanged (an extra `Initialize` with the initial
  state before a first run is a no-op, measured on 15 configurations), every golden unchanged, except a run whose caller
  re-initialized the integrator with another observer or frame (under **Changed**). A reused instance keeps the initial
  state, covariance and options of its construction, and since lot L5 throws once the spacecraft holds another initial
  orbit (#783, under **Changed**).
- **A first run after states and attitudes added by hand is a fresh run** ([#803](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/803) (b), lot L5a, R08 of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decision 38,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): the re-arm of a propagation (`Spacecraft.ResetPropagation`) dropped the stored
  states and the attitude record only when `IsPropagated` was true, so the first run of a spacecraft kept the attitudes
  added by `AddStateOrientationToICRF` (the stored states were replaced): measured in the gap analysis of L5, a record of
  4 entries against 2 for a fresh spacecraft, a quarter turn off it from mid-window to the end and outside the window,
  while a second run gave the fresh record. It now drops them whatever `IsPropagated` says, on every path
  (`Spacecraft.Propagate`, a `CentralBodyPropagator`, a batch, a scenario, both integrators, a TLE spacecraft sampled by
  `TLEPropagator` before; `RunIndependenceTests`). Runs on a spacecraft without such entries are unchanged, bit for bit.
- **The solutions of the runs of one `TLEPropagator` share no state** ([#785](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/785), decision 39 of #668): each run samples
  into arrays of its own, its first sample included; before, every solution of an instance held the propagator's one
  array, whose first state was built once at construction, so a later run rewrote the states of an earlier solution
  (`RunIndependenceTests.TheSolutionsOfTwoRunsOfOneTLEPropagator_ShareNoState`). The samples are those of before, bit
  for bit.

- **A re-armed `PlaneAlignmentManeuver` waited for the crossing of the last run's node** ([#784](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/784), lot L5a, decision 51 of
  #668): the re-arm cleared `IsAscendingNode` but left `EventCrossingDirection`, so a run that did not reach the
  maneuver ended with a node of none and the direction of the last run's node. `Reset` now clears both, the direction
  back to `Any`, as a fresh maneuver's (`ManeuverPreviewTests.PlaneAlignment_TheReArm_ClearsTheCrossingDirection`, red
  before the change, both integrators). No trajectory moves: the detector locks the node again at its first evaluation.
- **Calls that look like previews changed a maneuver or a spacecraft outside a run** ([#802](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/802), lot L5a, decisions 49 and
  50 of #668): the public `TryExecute` of a maneuver burnt the fuel, set the windows and moved the standby chain of a
  finished run (592.27 kg taken and the `DeltaV` of the run overwritten in the gap analysis of L5), `Engine.Ignite` burnt
  fuel (60.12 kg after a run) and threw `NullReferenceException` on a tank of no spacecraft, and the public
  `ComputeEventValue` locked the node of a `PlaneAlignmentManeuver` and wrote the intersection of an
  `ApsidalAlignmentManeuver`. The first two are internal, `ComputeEventValue` is pure on every library maneuver, and the
  previews are `ComputeDeltaV` and `ComputeStateOrientation` (under **Added**, **Changed**). So is `ManeuverEventDetector`
  (decision 88 of #668), whose public `HandleEvent` executed a maneuver outside a run: after an apogee raise propagated
  3 h, a call at a state of the solution took the fuel from 850.075099 to 744.573379 kg, the `DeltaV` from 229.243040 to
  172.742734 m/s and moved the thrust window by 2 h (the probe of the first review of L5a); the run's record was left.
  A custom `IIntegrator` still received the detectors within the run and could keep them: a detector kept past the run
  executed its maneuver outside it (472 kg of fuel burned and `DeltaV` rewritten in the probe of the second review of
  L5a). A detector now serves the run that built it only (decision 95 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-24): the
  run disarms it when it ends, completed, stopped or thrown, and its `Evaluate` and `HandleEvent` throw
  `InvalidOperationException` afterwards, changing nothing; a call already in progress when the run ends completes
  (decision 98 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-24: only an integrator that keeps a detector past its
  `IntegrateSegment` call meets it, 12 of 300 runs of a probe calling `HandleEvent` in a loop from a thread burning fuel
  after `Propagate` returned; no lock is added). Within the run, a custom `IIntegrator` that kept the
  detector of an impulse executed it a second time (6.74 kg burned, `DeltaV` rewritten, nothing in
  `ExecutedManeuvers`, in the probe of the third review of L5a): a detector now executes its impulse once at most for calls that do not overlap
  (decision 97 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-24), disarming itself as its `HandleEvent` starts to execute it,
  an execution that throws included (the fourth review of L5a: one that threw after the fuel burned left it armed, and
  each later call burned again), a detector that skipped an occurrence (`Continue`) staying armed.
- **A published propagation solution could be changed from outside the library** ([#796](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/796), lot L5a, decision 55 of
  #668): `PropagationSegment.AddStep`, `PropagationSolution.AddSegment` and `SetOutputStates` were public, and
  `Segments`, `StateVectors` and `Steps` returned the inner list or array, so a caller could add a step to a solution the
  spacecraft keeps for the conjunction analysis (`LastPropagation`), widening its window (a read at its end + 5000 s
  accepted where it threw), or replace an output state through a cast; `Integrator.UpdateStateVector` let a subclass
  rewrite any state in place. They are internal and the collections read-only views, allocated once (under
  **Changed**; `RunResultsSurfaceTests`).
- **A list of executed maneuvers or a scenario summary held by a caller changed with the next run** (lot L5a,
  decisions 58 and 59 of #668): `Spacecraft.ExecutedManeuvers` was a live set the next run emptied (measured 1 to 0 in
  the gap analysis of L5), and `SpacecraftSummary.Maneuvers` held the definitions, whose `DeltaV`, `FuelBurned` and
  windows the next run reset (258.818 m/s and 92.637 kg read 0 after a run that reached no burn). A run now swaps in
  new lists, and the summary holds the records of its run (under **Changed**; `RunResultsSurfaceTests`,
  `ExecutedManeuverRecordTests`).

  and as U+200E then "-1" under he-IL, while their angles and vectors were already invariant: the frame kernels failed

  `IO.Astrodynamics.Tests.Culture`, which runs outside invariant globalization, under sv-SE, fi-FI and he-IL; red

- **The kernel writers and the Cosmographia export upper-cased the names in the culture of the thread**
  ([#798](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/798), lot L5c, decisions 74 and
  101 of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,

  the instrument frame and instrument kernels, the site frame kernel and the catalog of an export named `İSS_İMAGER`
  the object every other culture names `ISS_IMAGER`, the frame of a site, named at construction, was `<NAME>_TOPO` in

  which Cosmographia does not know. Every name that reaches a kernel, a path or the catalog is upper-cased, and the

  `astro propagate`. The bytes are unchanged outside the Turkish and Azeri cultures, and always under invariant

  ASCII names compared byte for byte with 21d0e648); under tr or az a name with "i" now writes "I", and a name that
  holds "ı" (U+0131) keeps it. `Site.Frame.Name` changes under tr and az only. Migration: none, but a kernel or a
  catalog written before 11.0.0 under tr or az names its objects with "İ" (`KernelWriterCultureTests`, under tr-TR, red

- **`Spacecraft.WriteOrientation` said "it has not been propagated" of a spacecraft a `TLEPropagator` had run**
  ([#546](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/546), lot L5c, decision 81 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,

  which gives the spacecraft attitudes to write (after the run, whose re-arm drops those added before it). Migration:

- **`CosmographiaExporter.ExportAsync` deleted the previous export before it wrote the new one**
  ([#799](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/799)(b), lot L5c, decision 74 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-23): the export deleted `<Mission>_<Scenario>`, then wrote its kernels and its catalog, so a writer that threw

  all. The export checks its names, writes its kernels and its catalog into its scratch directory, and only then replaces

  21d0e648 on an export of a spacecraft, an instrument, a site and a star; the native SPKs of the site and the star hold

- **A scenario named `/..` made `CosmographiaExporter.ExportAsync` delete the whole output directory**

  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-25): `<Mission>_<Scenario>` resolved to the output directory itself, which the export deleted with everything
