  (`ExportCheckTests`, red before the change: the output directory and the file beside the export were deleted).
- **`SpiceAPI.TransformFrame` over a window dropped the end of the window even on the grid**
  ([#781](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/781), lot L6, decision 9 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-22): its loop stopped strictly before the end, while the other window reads read it, so one hour at 20 min
  gave 3 orientations for 4. Its epochs are the points of `Window.Sample(stepSize)`, the grid of every window read,
  the end read when it lies on the grid (Breaking, under **Changed**; `EphemerisWindowStepTests`, `SpiceApiTest`, red
  before the change).
- **`SpiceAPI.ReadEphemeris` and `ReadOrientation` over a UTC window across a leap second read one epoch past its end**
  ([#829](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/829), lot L6, decision 107 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-25): the number of epochs counted the leap second while the epochs followed the UTC calendar, so the two UTC
  minutes around the leap second of 2012-06-30 at 1 s gave 122 states for 121, the last at 2012-07-01T00:01:01Z, and a
  read whose data ended at the window end threw `SpiceException`. The epochs are the points of `Window.Sample(stepSize)`
  (Breaking, under **Changed**; `SpiceApiWindowReadTests`, red before the change).
**Changed**

- **Breaking: the scale of a `Time` is a required argument** (lot L2, R24 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), D3, decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-13 and amended 2026-11-19: no forwarder). `ITimeFrame`, `TimeFrame`, `TimeSystem.Frames` (`TDBTimeFrame`,
  `TDTTimeFrame`, `TAITimeFrame`, `UTCTimeFrame`, `GPSTimeFrame`, `LocalTimeFrame`) and `TimeFrame.LeapSecondsFrom` are
  replaced by `TimeScale` (under **Removed**); `Time.Frame` becomes `Time.Scale`, and every `ITimeFrame` parameter a
  `TimeScale` (`Time(DateTime, TimeScale scale)`, `Create`, `CreateFromJD`, `ConvertTo`); `ToTDT()` becomes `ToTT()`.
  The calendar constructor `Time(year, month, day, hour = 0, …, ITimeFrame frame = null)`, which read a calendar without
  a frame as TDB, 69.18 s from UTC in 2024, is replaced by four constructors whose scale is the last argument. The
  conversions are those of the frame classes tick for tick (`TdbSeriesTests`, `ConvertToOwnFrameTests`), so no result
  moves. Migration: `TimeFrame.TDBFrame` → `TimeScale.TDB`, `UTCFrame` → `UTC`, `TAIFrame` → `TAI`, `TDTFrame` → `TT`,
  `GPSFrame` → `GPS`; `t.Frame` → `t.Scale`, `t.Frame is UTCTimeFrame` → `t.Scale == TimeScale.UTC`; `t.ToTDT()` →
  `t.ToTT()`; `new Time(2024, 1, 1)` → `new Time(2024, 1, 1, TimeScale.TDB)` (the old default; most callers meant
  `TimeScale.UTC`), `new Time(2024, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0, frame: TimeFrame.UTCFrame)` → `new Time(2024, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0,
  TimeScale.UTC)`, a call that gave an hour without minutes and seconds writes them as 0; a named `frame:` argument
  becomes `scale:`.
- **Breaking: `new Time(DateTime, TimeScale)` refuses a `DateTime` of kind `Local`, and one of kind `Utc` in another
  scale than UTC** (D3.2 of #668), `ArgumentException` (`dateTime`); before, the frame replaced the kind silently, so a
  `DateTime.UtcNow` given with `TDBFrame` was read as a TDB calendar, and a local `DateTime.Now` as a calendar of the
  frame. A UTC time's `DateTime` is of kind `Utc`, so relabelling it in another scale throws too. The CCSDS readers give
  their epochs, read in `TIME_SYSTEM`, as clock readings, bit for bit (internal `CcsdsTimeSystemMapping.ToTime`).
  Migration: `new Time(DateTime.Now, …)` → `Time.UtcNow` (or `new Time(dt.ToUniversalTime(), TimeScale.UTC)`); a UTC
  calendar meant in another scale: `DateTime.SpecifyKind(dt, DateTimeKind.Unspecified)`; an instant: `ConvertTo`.
- **Breaking: `Time(string)` is replaced by `Time.Parse`** (D3.4 of #668), on one grammar: `new Time("2024-06-21T12:00:00
  UTC")` → `Time.Parse("2024-06-21T12:00:00 UTC")`, an untagged string (TDB before) → `Time.Parse(s, TimeScale.TDB)`.
  `Parse` throws `FormatException` only (`ArgumentException` for a second 60, an unknown tag or a tag after `Z` before);
  `Parse(s, scale)` gives `scale` to an untagged string and refuses a tag of another scale.
  Its changes of meaning: an offset (`+02:00`) is the UTC instant, where it gave a local time of the machine; a day of
  year (`2024-173T12:00:00 UTC`) and a Julian date (`JD 2460483.0 UTC`) are read; the forms `DateTime.TryParse` read
  beyond ISO 8601 are refused (`06/21/2024 12:00`, RFC 1123, a `GMT` suffix). Migration: `Time.Parse`, or
  `Time.TryParse` for a string that may be refused.
- **Breaking: `Time.ToString` writes TT as `TT`** (D3.5 of #668; `TDT` before), and `Parse` still reads `TDT`.
  Migration: a consumer that matched ` TDT` matches ` TT`.
- **Breaking: `default(Time)` is 0001-01-01T00:00:00 TDB** (D3.1 of #668, `TimeScale.TDB` is 0): a time with no frame
  before, which came before every time with a frame and was equal to none; it is now that TDB calendar, equal to
  `new Time(DateTime.MinValue, TimeScale.TDB)` and before every later instant. Migration: none for a sort or a
  comparison with a later time.
- **Breaking: `Time.Create(year, doy, sec)` becomes `Time.FromDayOfYear(year, dayOfYear, seconds, scale)`** (D3.2 of
  #668), the scale explicit (the old factory was UTC), its checks those of #680, its parameters named `dayOfYear` and
  `seconds` in the exceptions (`doy` and `sec` before). Migration: `Time.Create(2024, 173, 43200.0)` →
  `Time.FromDayOfYear(2024, 173, 43200.0, TimeScale.UTC)`.
- **Breaking: `Constants._2PI` and `Constants.PI2` become `Constants.TwoPi` and `Constants.HalfPi`** (R24 of #668, D2's
  N3, section A), the same doubles (`TwoPi` is `Math.Tau`, `HalfPi` π/2: `PI2` was π/2 under a name that read 2π).
  Migration: rename.
- **Breaking: `Matrix` is immutable** (lot L2, R26 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), section A as amended, decided
  by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19: no error-level trap, the public `Set` removed outright, under **Removed**). No member
  changes a matrix once built, so a matrix given to a `StateVector`, an encounter, a CDM record or a Monte Carlo result,
  or read from one, keeps its terms whatever the caller does afterwards (#722 and #745 had closed the aliasing through
  copies; `Set` still wrote the matrix a caller held). With it: an index outside the matrix throws
  `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` naming `row` or `column` from `Get` and the indexer (`IndexOutOfRangeException`
  before); a negative dimension throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` from the constructors (`OverflowException` before);
  `default(Matrix)` is the 0 × 0 matrix for every member (`Get`, `ToArray`, `Inverse` and `Decompose` threw
  `NullReferenceException` on it); `ToString()` prints the rows, `[[1, 0], [0, 1]]`, each term in invariant culture
  and round trip, `[]` without rows (the record's `Matrix { Rows = 2, Columns = 2 }` before; nothing of the library
  read it). Results do not move. Migration: build the terms, then the matrix: `var m = new Matrix(6, 6); m.Set(0, 0,
  25.0); …` → `Matrix.Diagonal(25.0, …)`, `new Matrix(terms)` from a `double[,]` filled first, or
  `Matrix.Create(6, 6, (i, j) => …)`; a change of one term of an existing matrix → `m = m.With(i, j, value)`;
  `catch (IndexOutOfRangeException)` around `Get` → `catch (ArgumentOutOfRangeException)`.
- **Breaking: `double[] * Matrix` is the row product vᵀ M** ([#774](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/774), lot L2 of the ergonomics review, decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-21). The operator returned `rhs.Multiply(lhs)`, the column product M v, which equals vᵀ M only for
  a symmetric matrix: for a rotation it applied the rotation where vᵀ M applies its inverse. It now returns vᵀ M,
  `Columns` components, each the sum, from 0 and in row order, of v[i] · m[i, j] (the components of Mᵀ v), and throws
  `ArgumentException` (`lhs`) for a vector of another length than `Rows` (before, for a length other than `Columns`,
  with no parameter name and the message "Matrixes with incompatible size"). The
  library's one use, the perifocal-to-inertial rotation of `OrbitalParameters.ToStateVector`, meant M v and is written
  `r * pos`, the same arithmetic: its states do not move, bit for bit. Migration: code that meant M v writes `M * v`;
  code that meant vᵀ M has its product now, where it had M v before.
- **Breaking: one meaning per `KeplerianElements` constructor** (lot L2, R23 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-19, no forwarder). The public constructor is `KeplerianElements(semiMajorAxis, eccentricity, inclination,
  ascendingNode, argumentOfPeriapsis, meanAnomaly, observer, epoch, frame, elementsType = Osculating)`: its optional
  `trueAnomaly`, `period` and `perigeeRadius` are removed, which it stored unchecked beside the elements (a true anomaly
  that put the state 6177.2 km from the mean anomaly's, a perigee radius of 1 m on an ellipse returned by
  `PerigeeRadius()`, a period of 1 h on any orbit), and `rigthAscendingNode` is renamed `ascendingNode`. Within 1e-6 of
  e = 1 the constructor throws `ArgumentException` naming `eccentricity`, pointing to `Parabolic` (before: naming
  `perigeeRadius`). The library's own elements (conversions, the two-body motion, SPICE's elements, the TLE's mean set)
  keep their computed values through an internal constructor: no state or element moves, bit for bit. Migration:
  `new KeplerianElements(a, e, i, o, w, m, centre, epoch, frame, trueAnomaly: nu)` →
  `KeplerianElements.FromTrueAnomaly(a, e, i, o, w, nu, centre, epoch, frame)` (its M is M(ν), not the m given beside
  it); `new KeplerianElements(double.PositiveInfinity, 1.0, i, o, w, m, centre, epoch, frame, perigeeRadius: q)` →
  `KeplerianElements.Parabolic(q, i, o, w, m, centre, epoch, frame)`, an e of the band as the last argument and its a
  computed; `period:` → nothing (`Period()` computes it); a `perigeeRadius:` beside an ellipse or a hyperbola → nothing
  (`PerigeeRadius()` computes a (1 − e)); `rigthAscendingNode:` → `ascendingNode:`.
- **Breaking: the data provider seam speaks domain types** (lot L3, R04 with R20 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19, so that a
  custom provider changes once). `IDataProvider.GetEphemeris` returns a `StateVector` (`OrbitalParameters` before,
  always built as a `StateVector`); `IDataProvider.GetCelestialBodyInfo`, `SpiceAPI.GetCelestialBodyInfo` and
  `MemoryDataProvider.GetCelestialBodyInfo` return a `CelestialBodyInfo`, and `MemoryDataProvider.AddCelestialBodyInfo`
  takes `params CelestialBodyInfo[]` (the interop struct `IO.Astrodynamics.DTO.CelestialBody` before, now internal,
  whose name clashed with `IO.Astrodynamics.Body.CelestialBody`), throwing `ArgumentNullException`
  (`celestialBodyInfos`) for a null array or record and storing nothing (`NullReferenceException` part way before). The
  values are the same, bit for bit. The interface documents its exception contract (an unknown name or identifier
  `ArgumentException`, a known item without data `InvalidOperationException`), unchanged since #680. Migration: a custom
  provider returns `StateVector` from `GetEphemeris` and `CelestialBodyInfo` from `GetCelestialBodyInfo`; a caller that
  wrote `.ToStateVector()` after a provider read may drop it; `info.Id` → `info.NaifId`; `new DTO.CelestialBody(id,
  centerOfMotionId, barycenterOfMotionId, name, new Vector3D(x, y, z), gm, frameName, frameId, j2, j3, j4)` → `new
  CelestialBodyInfo(id, name, centerOfMotionId, barycenterOfMotionId, new Vector3(x, y, z), gm, frameName, frameId, j2,
  j3, j4)` (the name second), or named arguments; `using BodyInfo = IO.Astrodynamics.DTO.CelestialBody` → `using
  IO.Astrodynamics.DataProvider`.
- **Breaking: `CelestialItem.ExtendedInformation` is private protected** (R04 of #668, section A): a field of the
  interop struct, protected, so that a subclass outside the library read the body information through it. Migration:
  read the members of the body (`Name`, `GM`, `Radii`, `Frame`, `J2`, `CenterOfMotionId`, ...), or
  `Configuration.Instance.DataProvider.GetCelestialBodyInfo(naifId)`.
- **Breaking: every public struct is read only** (R04 of #668: `IntegrationResult`, `EventInfo` and `EventResult`, the
  positional record structs of the integrators and the event detectors, had public setters, and `Plane` was not read
  only), so that a copy taken from a property or a collection cannot be changed in the belief that the original is
  (`PublicSurfaceScopeTests`). Migration: `result = result with { Action = EventAction.Continue }` in place of
  `result.Action = EventAction.Continue`.
- **Breaking: the ephemeris reads are typed as the `StateVector` they build** (lot L3, R20 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), choice 1, decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-19). `ILocalizable.GetEphemeris` returns a `StateVector` at an epoch and an `IEnumerable<StateVector>` over a
  window, and so do the implementations of `CelestialItem` (its virtual and the overrides of `Spacecraft` and `Star`),
  `Site`, and `SpiceAPI.ReadEphemeris` (both): `OrbitalParameters` before, every implementation building a
  `StateVector`. The states are the same objects, bit for bit. Migration: an `ILocalizable` implementation or a
  `GetEphemeris` override changes its return types; `List<OrbitalParameters> l = x.GetEphemeris(window, ...).ToList()`
  → `List<StateVector>`, or `IEnumerable<OrbitalParameters> l = x.GetEphemeris(...)` where a sequence of the base type
  is meant; a `.ToStateVector()` after a read may be dropped.
- **Breaking: `ToFrame` and `RelativeTo` are virtual, typed as a `StateVector` on a `StateVector`** (R20 of #668): the
  covariant overrides `StateVector.ToFrame(Frame)` and `StateVector.RelativeTo(ILocalizable, Aberration)`, so that
  `sv.ToFrame(Frame.ECLIPTIC_J2000).Position` reads without `.ToStateVector()`. The conversions are those of
  `OrbitalParameters`, bit for bit; on any other orbital parameters they keep their type, the parameters themselves in
  their own frame or about their own observer (a `TLE` in TEME stays the TLE). Migration: none for a caller; a `var`
  that held `OrbitalParameters` holds a `StateVector`, and a subclass of `OrbitalParameters` that declared a member
  `ToFrame` or `RelativeTo` of these signatures overrides it.
- **Breaking: a geodetic coordinate search from an observer that is not a body throws `InvalidOperationException`**
  (R20 of #668): the managed coordinate searches of `CelestialItem` and `Site` in `CoordinateSystem.Geodetic` read
  `ToPlanetodetic()`, whose observer must be a `CelestialBody`; before, the cast threw `InvalidCastException`. The
  windows of every other search are unchanged, bit for bit (the same two calls). Migration: a
  `catch (InvalidCastException)` catches `InvalidOperationException`.
- **Breaking: the coordinate records take camelCase constructor parameters** (lot L3, R20 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), PR R20-b of the first annex,
  D2 N1): `Planetodetic(longitude, latitude, altitude)`, `Planetocentric(longitude, latitude, radius)` and
  `Horizontal(azimuth, elevation, range, epoch)`, each with its `Deconstruct` of the same names; before, positional
  records whose parameters were named as their properties, so the design's `new Planetodetic(longitude: lon, latitude:
  lat, altitude: 1e3)` did not compile. The properties keep their names and their `init` accessors (`with`), equality,
  `ToString` and the order of the components are unchanged (`CoordinateConstructorTests`). Migration: a named argument
  takes the lower-case name, `new Planetodetic(Longitude: lon, Latitude: lat, Altitude: h)` →
  `new Planetodetic(longitude: lon, latitude: lat, altitude: h)`; positional calls, `with` and deconstruction are
  unchanged.
- **Breaking: `GeopotentialModelParameters` is a value** (lot L4, R06 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668)): a sealed record (`with` for
  `CentralTerm`), equal to another of the same source (the full path of a model file, EGM2008 embedded, or streams of the
  same bytes), degree, constants and central term (by reference before); `GeopotentialDegree` and the degree of the
  constructors are an `int` (a `ushort` before; a negative degree throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`), and the
  constructor of a path checks the file (`FileNotFoundException`, as the `FileStream` it opened before) and reads it at
  the first body or propagation; a stream is read to its end by the constructor and left open (it was closed by the first
  body). The fields and the results are the same, bit for bit. Migration: none for a call with a `ushort` or literal
  degree; `(ushort)n` casts may go; the `StreamReader` of `GeopotentialModelPath` is gone (under **Removed**).
- **One geopotential field per propagation** (R06 of #668, section A of the re-baseline, decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-19): every propagation that builds its forces evaluates the central gravity with its own field, built from the
  body's model over the coefficients the model reads once, where it evaluated the body's field; the results are the same,
  bit for bit (`GeopotentialOptionsTests`), and a `CelestialBody` with a geopotential may now be shared by concurrent
  propagations, a batch, a scenario and a Monte Carlo campaign, and by the RK7(8) evaluations of their solutions
  ([Thread Safety](../guides/thread-safety.md)). The body's own `EvaluateGravitationalAcceleration` still evaluates its
  field, one thread at a time. Not breaking.
- **Breaking: a null `ConjunctionAnalysisOptions.CovariancePropagation` throws** (R06 of #668, structuring choice 3,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19: throw, rather than flip silently to Auto): `ArgumentNullException` in `init`, naming
  `CovariancePropagation` and pointing to `CovariancePropagationOptions.None`; before, null held the covariance of the
  initial state in RTN, while in `PropagationOptions` a null value is Auto. Migration: `CovariancePropagation = null` →
  `CovariancePropagation = CovariancePropagationOptions.None`, the same results, bit for bit (the 25 call sites of the
  repository, the covariance tutorial among them).
- **Breaking: `PropagationTask` is no longer a positional record** (R06 and R07 of #668): `new PropagationTask(spacecraft,
  window, options = null)` is its one constructor, with `Spacecraft`, `Window` and `Options`; `Deconstruct` is gone, and
  the constructor of the flags and the integrator factory of 10.x with its properties is removed (under **Removed**).
  Migration: deconstruct by the properties.
- **Breaking: the outputs of a propagation end at its window end whatever its step** (R11 of #668, structuring choice
  6, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19): when round(L/ΔT) rounds the window of length L up, the outputs are start + i·ΔT
  inside the window, then the window end, which replaces the last grid point (at least ΔT/2 past the end) and is merged
  with a point within ΔT/10 of it, on every path: `Spacecraft.Propagate`, `CentralBodyPropagator` (both forms),
  `Scenario.Simulate`, `BatchPropagator`, `MonteCarloPropagator` and `TLEPropagator`, whose rule of #598 this is. Before,
  the grid ran to round(L/ΔT)·ΔT, up to ΔT/2 past the window, and the propagation with it (#626): 3 590 s at 60 s
  outputs ended at 3 600 s. What moves (decision 8 of lot L4, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-22): in RK7(8) only the last
  output, now the state at the window end, every other output bit for bit; in Velocity-Verlet, or an integrator without
  dynamics, the last output and, when the integration step does not divide ΔT, the outputs inside the last integration
  step, which ends at the window end where it ended at round(L/ΔT)·ΔT (67.48 m at the output of 3 540 s for Velocity-Verlet
  at 100 s about the Earth, 60 s outputs, Linux; `OutputGridTests.WhatMoves_AgainstTheFormerGrid`). Every output of a
  window the step divides or rounds down (#741) is that of before, bit for bit, and the accepted steps are those of the
  propagation of the window with one output step (`OutputGridTests`: RK7(8) and Velocity-Verlet, the Earth in TT seconds
  and the Moon in TDB seconds, every path). The force caches cover the window (#626), and a propagation no
  longer reads data past it. Migration: none for a step that divides the window; a caller that read the state at
  round(L/ΔT)·ΔT reads it from a window that long.
- **Breaking: the window searches return `IReadOnlyList<Window>`** (lot L6, R16 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), choice 2, decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-19): the 21 public searches (`FindWindowsOnDistanceConstraint`,
  `FindWindowsOnOccultationConstraint`, `FindWindowsOnCoordinateConstraint` of `CelestialItem`, `ILocalizable` and
  `Site`, `Site.FindWindowsOnIlluminationConstraint` and `FindDayWindows`, `Instrument.FindWindowsInFieldOfViewConstraint`,
  `GeometryFinder.FindWindowsWithCondition` and the six searches of `SpiceAPI`) returned the arrays and lists they build
  as an `IEnumerable<Window>`; they return them as an `IReadOnlyList<Window>`, the same windows bit for bit, with `Count`
  and the indexer. A dependent compiled against 10.x must be rebuilt, an implementer of `ILocalizable` changes the return
  type of its three searches, and a `var` result later assigned a LINQ query no longer compiles (CS0266). Migration:
  rebuild; in an `ILocalizable` implementation, return `IReadOnlyList<Window>` (an array or a list); declare as
  `IEnumerable<Window>` a variable that a query is later assigned to, or end the query with `.ToArray()`. The searches of
  `CelestialItem`, `ILocalizable`, `Site` (but `FindDayWindows`), `Instrument` and `GeometryFinder` are removed since,
  in lot L6 (see **Removed**), and the searches on the observer that replace them return an `IReadOnlyList<Window>` too.
- **Breaking: a reversed window throws** (R11 of #668, section A of the re-baseline, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19): `new Window(start, end)` throws `ArgumentException`
  (`endDate`) for an end before its start, and `new Window(start, length)` `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (`length`) for a
  negative length, where they built a window of negative length; a window of zero length is accepted, and each end keeps
  its scale (`WindowTests`). Migration: order the ends.
- **Breaking: a negative maneuver hold throws** (R11 of #668): every maneuver constructor, impulses and attitudes, throws
  `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (`maneuverHoldDuration`) for a hold below zero, which it accepted, the window it gave an
  attitude or an impulse mid-propagation ending before it started; zero is accepted; `ManeuverHoldDuration` is set through
  the same check by a setter no type outside the library reaches (decision 11 of lot L4, decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-22; its `private protected` access, where it was `protected`, validated by decision 16 the same day:
  `PhasingManeuver` computes its hold at execution and sets it through the check)
  (`ManeuverHoldTests`). Migration: a hold of zero or more; a subclass outside the library gives its hold to the
  constructor.
- **Breaking: a propagation over a window of zero length throws `ArgumentException`** (`window`; decision 7 of lot L4,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-22) at the start of the call, before anything changes: `Spacecraft.Propagate`, both
  `CentralBodyPropagator` constructors and `Scenario.Simulate` (before its stars, whatever the scenario holds: a scenario
  of stars alone throws too, its stars not propagated and `IsSimulated` unchanged, decision 18 of lot L4, decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-22, where it propagated its stars and reported itself simulated; `Star.Propagate` itself since
  lot L6, the entry below); a batch task reports it as its error. Before, the propagation re-armed the spacecraft and threw `InvalidOperationException` "Solution
  contains no segments". The `TLEPropagator` constructor throws it too, for a window in TDB or in UTC, one rule on every
  propagation path (decision 15 of lot L4, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-22), where it returned one sample at the start,
  and so does `MonteCarloPropagator.Propagate` for a `MonteCarloConfiguration.Window` of zero length, before anything is
  sampled, where each run failed inside the batch and the campaign returned no statistics and no reason
  (`ZeroLengthWindowTests`). Migration: a window with a length; for the SGP4 state at one epoch,
  `tle.ToStateVector(epoch)`.
- **Breaking: the methods that run take a `CancellationToken`, last** (lot L4, R28 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decisions 4 to 6, C1 and C2 of
  lot L4, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-22): `Spacecraft.Propagate(window, options, cancellationToken)`,
  `Scenario.Simulate(options, cancellationToken)`, `IPropagator.Propagate(cancellationToken)` (`PropagatorBase`,
  `CentralBodyPropagator`, `TLEPropagator`), `BatchPropagator.Propagate(tasks, options, cancellationToken)` with
  `Propagate(tasks, progress, options, cancellationToken)`, and `MonteCarloPropagator.Propagate(config,
  cancellationToken)` with `Propagate(config, progress, cancellationToken)`, each token optional; no constructor, record
  or property takes one. A token already cancelled throws before anything changes (before the re-arm of the
  spacecraft); `VVIntegrator` and `RK78Integrator` read it at each accepted step (an internal hook: the interface
  `IIntegrator` does not change), never between the rejections of a step, and the propagator before each segment, so an
  integrator implemented outside the library stops between its segments; it is not read after the last segment, so the
  outputs, the attitude record and the stored states are written as one block. Every path throws
  `OperationCanceledException` carrying the caller's token, a batch and a Monte Carlo campaign one, never an
  `AggregateException`. A stopped run leaves the spacecraft re-armed and partial: no stored state and no attitude record
  (those added by hand to a spacecraft never propagated, `AddPropagatedStates` and `AddStateOrientationToICRF`, included),
  not `IsPropagated`, nothing kept for the conjunction analysis (a TLE spacecraft reads SGP4 again, any other its initial
  orbit), its fuel, `ExecutedManeuvers` and standby chain advanced up to the stop; in `Scenario.Simulate` and a batch the
  earlier spacecraft are complete, `IsSimulated` stays false and no summary or result is returned. One exception: a
  stopped `TLEPropagator` run changes nothing and leaves the spacecraft as it was (decision 19 of lot L4, decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-22; since lot L5 the rule of its runs, which re-arm and store their samples in one block, under
  **Changed**). A
  run with a live token is the run without one, bit for bit, every golden unchanged (`CancellationTests`: both integrators, an outer
  integrator, the covariance, an impulse, the SSB mode, a TLE spacecraft, a batch, a Monte Carlo campaign, a scenario, a
  task; a stop inside a step makes only the force evaluations left in it, 2 to 4 for RK7(8) about the Earth, 8 in SSB
  mode, none for Velocity-Verlet, the same on Linux x64, Windows x64 and macOS arm64 in the CI of #789, run
  45145382114). Binary break; source break for an implementation of `IPropagator`, which takes
  the parameter. Migration: rebuild; pass a token where a run must stop. See
  [Propagators](../reference/propagators.md#cancellation).
- **Breaking: a batch stops its running tasks** (R28 of #668, decision 4 of lot L4): the token of
  `BatchPropagator.Propagate` reaches the propagation of each running task, which stops at its next accepted step;
  before, the token of `BatchOptions` was read before each task only, and a running task ran to its end. A stopped task
  is not reported to the progress. `BatchOptions` holds `MaxDegreeOfParallelism` alone, with the `Default` of every
  options record (D1), `CancellationToken` and `Progress` being removed (under **Removed**). `Propagate(tasks, null)` is
  ambiguous between the two overloads (CS0121, accepted by decision 5 of lot L4). Migration: `new BatchOptions {
  CancellationToken = t, Progress = p }` → `BatchPropagator.Propagate(tasks, p, options, t)`; a configuration's
  `BatchOptions` of a Monte Carlo campaign likewise → `MonteCarloPropagator.Propagate(config, p, t)`;
  `Propagate(tasks, null)` → `Propagate(tasks, options: null)`.
- **Breaking: the propagators are not `IDisposable`** (R28 of #668, choice 3 of the first annex): `IPropagator`,
  `PropagatorBase` and `TLEPropagator` no longer implement it; their `Dispose` was empty or cleared two fields, and held
  no resource. A `using` of a propagator does not compile (CS1674; the 53 of the repository removed, 4 in the library
  and 49 in the tests). Binary break. Migration: `using var propagator = new CentralBodyPropagator(…)` →
  `var propagator = …`; `using (var p = …) { … }` → the block with `var p = …`.
- **Breaking: an `Initialize` by the caller between construction and `Propagate` has no effect on the run**
  ([#782](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/782), decision 23 of lot L4 of #668,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-22): the propagator initializes its integrator with the initial state of the propagation
  at construction, at the start of every run and after each event. Before, a later `Initialize` by the caller replaced
  the propagator's for the first segment, the whole run without an event: with another observer or frame it changed the
  run, under both integrators (measured at 1dc77ffc, Linux x64, `IntegratorInitializationTests`: 2.941e4 m over 2 h for a
  state in ECLIPJ2000 on an ICRF propagation about an EGM2008 10×10 Earth, 1.265e6 m over 2 days for the state about the
  solar system barycentre of a spacecraft in SSB mode, RK7(8) and Velocity-Verlet alike); with the observer and the frame
  of the propagation it changed nothing. An `IIntegrator` implemented outside the library receives `Initialize` at the
  start of every run and must reset there every state a run depends on (a recording one counts the construction plus one
  per run, plus one per event); a subclass of `PropagatorBase` sets `InitialState` in its constructor, the base
  initializing the integrator with it at every run. First runs are unchanged unless the caller re-initialized with
  another observer or frame, which now changes the run under both integrators. Migration: drop the `Initialize`; to
  integrate from another state, give it as the spacecraft's initial orbit and build a new propagator.
- **Breaking: an integrator belongs to one propagator** ([#782](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/782),
  decision 24 of lot L4 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-22): every constructor that receives an integrator
  (`CentralBodyPropagator(window, spacecraft, integrator, deltaT)`, its overload with `covariancePropagation`, the
  protected constructor of `PropagatorBase`) claims it atomically and throws `ArgumentException` (`integrator`) for one
  already given to another propagator, before it changes it: the integrator and the first propagator are untouched.
  The claim is made once the checks of the window, the spacecraft and its maneuvers pass, and is never released, as that
  of an options propagation: a constructor rejected by a later check (a central body of GM 0, covariance options the
  integrator or the initial covariance cannot take) leaves the integrator claimed, and a second propagator given it
  throws (decision 27 of lot L4 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-22). The message names both cases, an
  integrator already given to another propagator or to a propagator constructor that threw after claiming it, and says
  the claim is never released, so a new integrator is built (decision 29 of lot L4 of #668, decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-22).
  Before, a second propagator re-initialized the integrator with its own state and set its time argument and variational
  equations for both: an Earth propagator run after a Moon propagator was built on its integrator was 5.16e7 m off, and
  two covariance propagators sharing one threw from the variational equations of the other (gap analysis of #782). Runs
  with one integrator per propagator, every golden, are unchanged (`PropagatorReuseTests`). Migration: build a new
  integrator, with its forces, for each propagator, and a new one after a constructor that threw.
- **Breaking: the step of `GetEphemeris` over a window is above zero** (R11 of #668): `CelestialItem.GetEphemeris(window,
  observer, …, stepSize)` (spacecraft, bodies, stars, barycentres) and `Site.GetEphemeris(window, observer, …, stepSize)`
  throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (`stepSize`) for a step of zero or less, where a zero step looped without end on a
  site and asked a list of `int.MaxValue` states on a body, and a negative one threw the list's `capacity` exception or
  returned the start alone, and so does `SpiceAPI.TransformFrame(window, fromFrame, toFrame, stepSize)` at the call, not
  at the enumeration, where a zero step enumerated without end (decision 10 of lot L4, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-22;
  its end, dropped even on the grid, is read since lot L6, #781, the entry below) (`EphemerisWindowStepTests`).
  Migration: a positive step.
- **Breaking: `SpiceAPI.TransformFrame(window, fromFrame, toFrame, stepSize)` reads the end of the window when it lies on
  the grid** ([#781](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/781), lot L6, decision 9
  of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-22): its epochs are the points of `Window.Sample(stepSize)`, start + i·step up
  to the end, as the other window reads. Before, the loop stopped strictly before the end, so a step that divides the
  window dropped its last orientation: one hour at 20 min gave 3 orientations for 4, one day at 1 day 1 for 2. Every
  other orientation is unchanged, bit for bit, and so is a grid whose end lies off it (`EphemerisWindowStepTests`,
  `SpiceApiTest`). The grids of `GetEphemeris` over a window (`CelestialItem`, `Site`), `Star.Propagate` and the command
  `orientation` take `Window.Sample` too, bit for bit. Migration: none for the end; to keep the former orientations,
  drop the last one when the end lies on the grid.
- **Breaking: `Star.Propagate(window, stepSize)` over a window of zero length throws `ArgumentException` (`window`)**
  (lot L6, decisions 7, 15 and 18 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-22), checked before the step, the states the
  star held kept: the rule of every propagation path. Before, it stored the one state of the start in place of the
  star's states, which `WriteEphemeris` then refused (fewer than three). The parameter `timeWindow` is renamed `window`,
  the name of every propagation's window (`StarTests`). Migration: a window with a length; a named argument
  `timeWindow:` becomes `window:`.
- **Breaking: `SpiceAPI.ReadEphemeris(window, …, stepSize)` and `ReadOrientation(window, …, stepSize)` stop at the end of
  a UTC window that spans a leap second** ([#829](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/829),
  lot L6, decision 107 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-25): their epochs are the points of
  `Window.Sample(stepSize)`, start + i·step in the UTC calendar up to the end, as their documentation said ("while within
  the window"). Before, the number of epochs came from the window's length, which counts the leap second, while the
  epochs followed the calendar, so the read went one step past the end: the two UTC minutes around the leap second of
  2012-06-30 at 1 s gave 122 states (and 122 CK records) for 121, the last at 2012-07-01T00:01:01Z, and a read whose data
  end at the window end threw `SpiceException` there. Every other window is read as before, bit for bit
  (`SpiceApiWindowReadTests`). Migration: none; a caller that counted on the extra state reads it by its epoch.
- **Breaking: an angular threshold outside the range of its angle throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`** (lot L6, R11 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), section A of the re-baseline,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19: range guards on the comparison operators only): the threshold (`value`) of
  `FindWindowsOnCoordinateConstraint` (`CelestialItem`, `Site`, `SpiceAPI`) for a right ascension or a planetographic
  longitude outside [0, 2π], a geodetic longitude outside [−π, π], a declination or a latitude outside [−π/2, π/2], and
  of `Site.FindWindowsOnIlluminationConstraint` and `SpiceAPI.FindWindowsOnIlluminationConstraint` outside [0, π], or
  NaN, with `Greater`, `Lower`, `Equal`, `NotEqual`, `GreaterOrEqual` or `LowerOrEqual`, before any search, on the managed
  and the CSPICE paths; the twilight (`twilight`) of `Site.FindDayWindows` and of the `Launch` constructor outside
  [−π/2, π/2]. Each range is closed; the four extremes and the lengths are not checked. The message says the angles are
  in radians; the command line maps it to an error of `--value`, exit code 2. Before, the search ran on the value given:
  a threshold in degrees gave no window or the whole search window, without an error (`WindowSearchAngleGuardTests`).
  Every threshold in its range searches as before, bit for bit. The searches of `CelestialItem` and `Site` are removed
  since, in lot L6 (see **Removed**): the guard is that of `FindCoordinateWindows`, `Site.FindHorizontalWindows` (an
  elevation in [−π/2, π/2], an azimuth in [0, 2π]) and `Site.FindIlluminationWindows` that replace them. Migration: give
  the angle in radians (`Constants.Deg2Rad`).
- **Breaking: the field-of-view search throws `InvalidOperationException` for a search window that leaves the stored
  states** (lot L6, decisions 81 and 86 of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668),
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): the managed `Instrument.FindWindowsInFieldOfViewConstraint` refuses a search window

  catch `InvalidOperationException` there.
- **Breaking: `Site.FindDayWindows` labels its windows in the scale of the search window's start** (lot L6, R15 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), IC-12, decided by S. Guillet,

- **Breaking: `OccultationSearchOptions.ConvergenceTolerance` is a `TimeSpan?`, null for 1 µs** (lot L6, R15 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), D1 rule 2 and choice 6,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19): the three window search records repeat it with one type and default; a tolerance
  that is not positive throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` naming `ConvergenceTolerance` (it named `value`), and the

  bit. Migration: `options.ConvergenceTolerance ?? TimeSpan.FromTicks(10)` where a `TimeSpan` is read; `TimeSpan.FromTicks(10)`
  for `DefaultConvergenceTolerance`.
- **Breaking: the occultation search of a site observer is the library's** (lot L6, R15 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), choice 4 and IC-10, decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-19): `site.FindOccultationWindows(window, target, front, options)` runs the managed occultation
  search whatever the site, as the search of the target from the site did (`target.FindWindowsOnOccultationConstraint(window,
  site, …)`), equal to it bit for bit (`ObserverWindowSearchTests`). The removed `Site.FindWindowsOnOccultationConstraint`
  ran CSPICE's `gfoclt_c` for a site, a spacecraft target and a front body all from the kernels: there the windows move,
  the same windows with each edge within 5.0e-7 s geometric, 3.7e-4 s with LT, 1.2e-4 s with CN and 6.2e-4 s with XLT
  (LRO behind the Moon from DSS-13, 7 windows over 12 h at a 60 s step, `Occultation_SiteObserver_MovesFromGfocltWithinItsMeasure`;
  which of the two light-time models is right is [#828](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/828)),
  and the windows are labelled in the scale of the search window's start. A site built from coordinates, the case of the
  conformance runner, searched with the library before as now. Migration: none; for `gfoclt_c`'s windows from a site of the
  kernels, call `SpiceAPI.FindWindowsOnOccultationConstraint` with the site's NAIF id as observer.
- **Breaking: the searches on the observer label their windows in the scale of the search window's start** (lot L6, R15
  of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), IC-7 and IC-8, decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-19), where the removed searches on the target labelled TDB on the paths of CSPICE and of the
  occultation and field-of-view searches: the same instants, an end at a bound of the search window that bound, an end
  inside a UTC leap second kept in TDB. On a UTC or TT search window, `Window.Length` and `EndDate − StartDate` of a result
  count TT seconds, not TDB seconds (#508): up to 3.3e-10 of the length plus 100 ns for each converted end (3.2e-10 on the
  passes of LRO, 3.8e-10 on a window of 261 s, `ObserverWindowLabelTests`). The conformance runner gives its occultation
  searches the search window in TDB, its report unchanged, bit for bit. Migration: compare the windows as instants
  (`Window` equality); for TDB labels and lengths, search over `new Window(start.ToTDB(), end.ToTDB())`.
- **Breaking: `EquinoctialElements` takes a perigee radius with a non-finite P only** (R23 of #668, choice 3 of the
  first annex): a finite P fixes q = P / (1 + e), so a perigee radius beside it throws `ArgumentException`
  (`perigeeRadius`); before, it was stored, and `PerigeeRadius()` returned 1 m for P = 7000 km given 1 m. The library's
  `ToEquinoctial()` keeps the perigee radius of its parabolas (internal constructor), bit for bit. Migration: drop the
  argument when P is finite.
- **Breaking: the CLI's epochs** (D3 of #668, choice 4 of R24): seconds from J2000 take any scale tag (`757339200 TT`
  threw before; untagged stays TDB), and every other epoch is read by `Time.TryParse(s, TimeScale.TDB)`, so a day of
  year is read, an offset is the UTC instant, a Julian date is its digits to the nearest tick (through a double before,
  at most one tick away), `NaN JD` throws `FormatException` (`ArgumentOutOfRangeException` before), and a string holding
  a `z` or the letters `utc` anywhere is no longer UTC for that reason. A tagged epoch is read by `Time.TryParse(s)`
  first, so its tag gives its scale (`Parse(s, scale)` refuses a tag of another scale). `time-converter` without a
  target or a format writes TDB in ISO (it threw before; under **Added**). Migration: none for the documented forms.
- **Breaking: `time-converter` refuses an argument after the epoch** (D3.7 of #668), `ArgumentException` naming the
  quoted epoch: before, `time-converter 2020-01-01T12:00:00 TAI -u` dropped `TAI` and read the epoch untagged, as TDB,
  so it printed 2020-01-01T11:58:50.8160783Z, 69.18 s from the instant meant. Migration: quote an epoch that holds a
  space, `time-converter "2020-01-01T12:00:00 TAI" -u`.
- **Breaking: `time-converter --format jd` and `--format seconds` (`-j`, `-e`) write the tag of their scale** (D3.4 of
  #668: no implicit scale), `2433282.5 JD UTC` and `631152069.1839217 TDB` where they wrote `2433282.5 JD` and
  `631152069.1839217`, the numbers in invariant culture (the machine's culture before, `2433282,5` in French): an
  untagged output of UTC, TAI or GPS read back as an epoch was taken as TDB, 69.18 s early for UTC in 2024. Migration: a
  script that read the number takes the first token of the line.
- **Breaking: an error SPICE signals throws `SpiceException`** (lot L1, R03 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), structuring choice 10, decided
  by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19), an `InvalidOperationException` with SPICE's `ShortMessage` and `LongMessage` (under
  **Added**), on every path that threw SPICE's message in an `InvalidOperationException`: the kernel loads, unloads and
  reloads, the ephemeris and orientation reads, `TransformFrame`, the CSPICE window searches, the SPK and CK writers,
  the TLE reads, the element conversions and `Propagate2Bodies`, and the paths built on them (`GetEphemeris`, `ToFrame`,
  the searches of `CelestialItem`, `Site` and `Instrument`), the inner exception of R25's `ArgumentException` included.
  A centre without GM of a conversion or of an SPK ("CelestialItem id507 can't be read: The variable BODY507_GM could not
  be found in the kernel pool.") is SPICE's `SPICE(KERNELVARNOTFOUND)`; a failure of the native layer that is not SPICE's
  (a C++ exception with no SPICE error pending) stays an `InvalidOperationException`, and so does every check of the
  library. The messages and the results do not move. Migration: none for a
  `catch (InvalidOperationException)`, which still catches it; a check of the exact type
  (`e.GetType() == typeof(InvalidOperationException)`, xUnit's `Assert.Throws<InvalidOperationException>`) reads
  `SpiceException`, and a caller that parsed SPICE's code out of the message reads `ShortMessage`.
- **Breaking: the library's own exceptions derive from the standard types** (R03 of #668, section A, decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-19). `InsufficientFuelException` derives from `InvalidOperationException` (`ExceptionBase`, an
  `Exception`, before; under **Removed**), so a `catch (InvalidOperationException)` around a propagation now catches a
  burn the fuel does not allow; it gives the masses (under **Added**). `NewtonRaphson.Solve`, `SolveVector` and
  `BoundedNewtonRaphson` throw `InvalidOperationException` for a derivative too small, an estimate that is not finite or
  no convergence, with the same messages (`System.Exception` before), and so does the initial orbit determination that
  calls `Solve`. `OmmParseException`, `OmmValidationException`, `OpmParseException`, `OpmValidationException` and
  `CdmParseException` derive from `CcsdsFormatException`, a `FormatException` (`Exception` before), their names, members
  and messages unchanged, so a `catch (FormatException)` around a CCSDS read now catches them. Migration: none for a
  `catch (Exception)` or a catch of the type itself; a `catch (InvalidOperationException)` or `catch (FormatException)`
  that must not take them catches them first, and `Assert.Throws<Exception>` of the solver reads
  `InvalidOperationException`.
- **Breaking: a propagation about a central body without GM throws `ArgumentException`** (R03 of #668, structuring
  choice 10, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19), `spacecraft`, before anything runs or is claimed: the message names the
  body, its `BODYnnn_GM` and NAIF's `gm_de440.tpc`. A body read from the kernels has a GM of 0 when the kernel pool holds
  no `BODYnnn_GM` (ELARA, 507, with `gm_de440.tpc`; any body when no GM kernel is loaded), which `new CelestialBody(id)`
  still accepts; before, a propagation about it ran without central gravity, silently, on a straight line. Every path
  checks it (the propagator constructors, the builder, `Spacecraft.Propagate` and `PropagateAsync`, `Scenario.SimulateAsync`
  and the batch, both integrators; `ForceModelDefectTests`), and the Sun of the SSB mode the same way. Migration: load a GM
  kernel before building the body, or give a custom body its GM.
- **Breaking: a frame name the loaded kernels do not define throws `ArgumentException`** (R25 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), section A, decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-19), as `MemoryDataProvider` does: on every path that hands the name to SPICE,
  `SpiceAPI.TransformFrame` (`ParamName` `fromFrame` or `toFrame`, also when the other end is TEME, CIRS, TIRS or a site
  frame only the library holds), `ToFrame` of a frame or a state either way (`targetFrame` or `frame` for the target, no
  `ParamName` for the frame of the instance or the state, which is no argument of the call, nor for
  `GetStateOrientationToICRF` and `ToEquatorial`; `source` for `SpiceDataProvider.FrameTransformationToICRF`), the
  ephemeris reads (`GetEphemeris`, `SpiceAPI.ReadEphemeris` at an epoch or over a window, `frame`),
  `SpiceAPI.ReadOrientation` (`referenceFrame`) and the window searches of CSPICE: `FindWindowsOnCoordinateConstraint`
  (`frame`), `FindWindowsOnIlluminationConstraint` (`fixedFrame`), `FindWindowsOnOccultationConstraint` (`frontFrame`,
  `targetFrame`) and `FindWindowsInFieldOfViewConstraint` (`targetFrame`), the last two for an ellipsoid (a point target
  reads no frame), each a `SpiceException` before. The library asks SPICE (`namfrm_c`, through `GetFrameInfoProxy`) after
  the failed call, so a frame kernel loaded after `new Frame(name)` counts; the message names the frame, and the
  error thrown before, with SPICE's message, is the inner exception, now a `SpiceException` (R03, above). The names `ICRF` and
  `EME2000`, which are no SPICE names, stay other names, and their message points to `Frame.ICRF` (on both providers). A
  known frame that SPICE cannot orient at the epoch (outside the Earth's binary PCK) keeps its
  `InvalidOperationException`, a `SpiceException` since R03, which the orientation cache of a propagation still reads as unavailable. Results do not
  move where SPICE gives a transform: the same `sxform_c` and `spkezr_c` calls. The frame of a managed spacecraft without
  an attitude record and of a kernel-backed spacecraft that no frame kernel defines, read by name, throw it too.
  Migration: a `catch (InvalidOperationException)` meant for a mistyped or unloaded frame catches `ArgumentException`.
- **Breaking: the static SPICE frames of `Frame` read the data provider of the process at each transform**
  (structuring choice 1 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19). `Frame.ICRF`, `ECLIPTIC_J2000`, `ECLIPTIC_B1950`,
  `GALACTIC_SYSTEM2`, `B1950`, `FK4` and `ITRF93` read `Configuration.Instance.DataProvider` when they transform, their
  last orientation kept for one provider and one generation of the kernel pool; a frame built by name keeps the provider
  set at its construction, as every object the caller builds. Before, the static frames read the provider set when the
  type `Frame` was first used, for the life of the process, so that after `SetDataProvider` they read the former
  provider (a child process with two memory providers measures both rules, `MemoryDataProviderBodyTests`). Nothing moves
  for a process that keeps one provider. Migration: none for one provider; a program that swaps providers and meant the
  static frames to stay on the former one builds its frames by name before the swap.
- **Breaking: `NaifObject` is an `INaifObject` of an identifier and a name, without `Frame`** (R02 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), section A, decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-19). The record struct is `NaifObject(int NaifId, string Name) : INaifObject`; its `Frame`,
  which the library read nowhere, is removed: it was wrong for the Moon (`IAU_MOON` against `MOON_ME` with the usual
  frame kernels) and for NEW NORCIA (`NEW NORCIA_TOPO`), empty for the comets and asteroids and null for the Lagrange
  points. A catalogue entry is now accepted where an `INaifObject` is asked. Results do not move: the bodies built
  from an entry read their frame from the kernels, as before. Migration: `new NaifObject(id, name, frame)` becomes
  `new NaifObject(id, name)`; `PlanetsAndMoons.EARTH.Frame` becomes the frame of the body, `new CelestialBody(PlanetsAndMoons.EARTH).Frame`
  (`ITRF93` with `earth_assoc_itrf93.tf`, `IAU_EARTH` without), or the literal name (`new Frame("ITRF93")`).
- **Breaking: a repeated `LoadKernels` hands SPICE only the files it does not hold** (lot L1, R01 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), structuring choice 9, decided
  by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19). A path already loaded, a path inside a loaded directory, or a directory that holds loaded
  entries, furnishes only the kernel files that no load of `SpiceAPI` handed SPICE (those written since), and the
  others keep their precedence; a directory that holds loaded entries replaces them by its own entry, listed last.
  Before, such a load unloaded the entry and loaded it again, on top of every kernel loaded after it, at 4 to 7 times
  the cost (211 to 250 ms a repeat on `Data/SolarSystem`, against 34 to 49 ms for the first load; first annex of #671):
  loading `f`, `z` and `f` again, two kernels that assign one variable, gave `f`'s value, and gives `z`'s now
  (`KernelLoadingTests`, TK frames of closed-form rotation, and KEEPER's list on Linux). The generation of the kernel
  pool, after which the predefined bodies read their data again, is raised only by a load that hands SPICE a file, a
  failed one included; a repeated load and a path that does not exist leave it (before, every call raised it). When
  SPICE fails to load a file of a directory, the files loaded before it stay loaded and are listed under the path, so
  that its unload removes them (before, they were loaded and not listed, and a later load handed them to SPICE a second
  time). Migration: a caller that loaded a path again to read a kernel rewritten on disk, or to give it precedence
  again, calls `ReloadKernels` (under **Added**).
- **Breaking: the files of a directory load in ordinal order, component by component** (R01 of #668, structuring choice
  9, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19). `LoadKernels` of a directory sorts the entries of each level by name,
  `StringComparer.Ordinal` (capitals before lower case), a subdirectory walked at its place, so the order is the one of
  the paths relative to the directory compared component by component, the same on every platform (`x/y.tf` before
  `x0.tf`, which a sort of the whole paths swaps between `/` and `\`); where two files assign the same variable or
  cover the same object, the later one wins. Before, the order of the directory listing, which depends on the file
  system (the hash of the names on ext4, the reverse creation order on tmpfs): twenty kernels `k00` to `k19` of one
  variable gave `k19`'s value only by chance. No file of `Data/SolarSystem` overlaps another (its SPKs cover distinct
  objects, and the one variable defined twice, `TKFRAME_EARTH_FIXED_*`, has the same value in `earth_fixed.tf` and
  `earth_topo_201023.tf`; first annex of #671), so no result of the suite or of the conformance runner moves.
  Migration: rename the files of a folder of conflicting kernels so that the one to win sorts last, or load them one
  by one in the order wanted.
- **Breaking: `UnloadKernels(null)` throws `ArgumentNullException`** (`path`), as `LoadKernels(null)` does (R01 of
  #668); it returned before. With the string overloads, `LoadKernels(null)` and `UnloadKernels(null)` no longer compile
  (CS0121, an ambiguous call; accepted by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19). Migration: drop the call, or cast the null (`(FileSystemInfo)null`) where a null path is
  meant to throw.
- **Breaking: the thrust window of an impulse is the burn whose acceleration has its centroid at the impulse**
  ([#335](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/335), derived from
  S. Guillet's remark of 2026-11-18 that the acceleration grows during the burn, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18). The
  equivalent constant-thrust burn of duration dt is placed on [t − f dt, t + (1 − f) dt], t the impulse epoch,
  f = 1/x + 1/ln(1 − x) for the mass fraction burned x = Δm/m0 (Tsiolkovsky, the engine's Isp and fuel flow, the mass
  before the burn): the centroid of the acceleration F/(m0 − q τ), which grows as the mass drops, where an impulse
  gives the burn's velocity change and, in a field-free space, its displacement after it. f → 1/2 for a small burn,
  0.509 at x = 0.1, 0.557 at 0.5, 2/3 only at x ≈ 0.89. Before 11.0.0 the window opened a fixed 0.666 dt before t, a
  split of no recorded derivation: 1.6 s earlier for a burn of 10 s at x = 0.1, 5.4 s for one of 50 s at x = 0.5, to the
  tick against the centroid by quadrature now (`ImpulseThrustWindowTests`). The same split in
  `ImpulseManeuver.TryExecute` and in the TT windows of a propagation about the Earth (#547). It moves, by
  (0.666 − f) dt later: `ThrustWindow`, `ManeuverWindow` (its length unchanged), `MAN_EPOCH_IGNITION` of
  `ToOpmManeuverParameters` and `Spacecraft.ToOpm` (`MAN_DURATION` unchanged), the opening of the impulse's attitude in
  the attitude record and the CK, the instant from which `ToOpm` counts an impulse as ignited, and the gate of the next
  maneuver of the chain, so an attitude chained after an impulse activates later and an impulse gated by it fires later
  where the gate binds (a crossing between the old and the new gate now waits for the next one). The propagated state
  of an impulse is unchanged (the whole ΔV at t). Migration: none for the state; a caller that reads the windows, the
  ignition epoch or the epochs of a chain whose gates bind sees the new ones, and one that relied on 2/3 computes
  t − 0.666 dt from the event and the burn duration itself.
- **Breaking: when an event fires** ([#580](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/580), [#578](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/578), [#581](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/581); decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17).
  - **A g-value exactly zero at a step end** after a non-zero one is a crossing there, its direction read from the sign
    before it (Hipparchus's rule); RK7(8) takes the step end as the root without bisecting. A zero at the base of a
    segment followed by a non-zero value is not a crossing of a detector without a gate (Hipparchus's convention), so a
    caller that restarts from an event with the same detector does not find it again.
  - **A gated detector exactly zero at the base** (an impulse whose g-function is 0.0 at the start, its minimum epoch at
    or before the start) fires at the base when the first step end has the target sign (GMAT's convention, #577's
    choice 6; the split of the two conventions at the base, which only direct callers of `IntegrateSegment` meet, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18): a minimum epoch before the start now gives the burn a minimum epoch at the start gives (RK7(8) at the
    start, Velocity-Verlet at its first step end), not one orbit later.
  - **Several detectors:** `IIntegrator.IntegrateSegment` reports one event per call, the earliest crossing of the step,
    ties in list order: `RK78Integrator` locates each root and keeps the earliest, `VVIntegrator` estimates each on the
    cubic Hermite of the step and reports the earliest at the step end. With Velocity-Verlet another crossing of the same
    step falls before that step end: a caller that restarts from the event starts that detector from its g-value before
    the step, or loses it. The protected `Integrator.CheckEventDetectors` evaluates every active detector and applies the
    rule of a zero at a step end; it still returns the first crossing in list order, which a subclass with several
    detectors orders by time itself. `Propagate`, `Scenario.SimulateAsync` and the batch pass one detector.
  - **At the base of a segment** a gated detector whose gate is open there is evaluated from the start of its search
    (`ComputeEventValueAtSearchStart`), the detector of the event just handled from its g-value past that root, now in
    Velocity-Verlet too: a `PlaneAlignmentManeuver` whose propagation starts within 1e-6 |r| past a node takes the node
    ahead.
  - **Moves:** a burn whose g-function is exactly zero at a step end or at the base (time-like user impulses, apsides
    given by Keplerian elements) and plane alignments started just past a node; every other event bit for bit in RK7(8),
    and in Velocity-Verlet but for the label of the event (below).
  - **Migration:** a caller of `IntegrateSegment` with several detectors takes the reported event as the earliest; a
    custom `IEventDetector` whose g-function is exactly zero at step ends now fires there.
- **Breaking: a Velocity-Verlet event is carried onto the tick of its label** ([#572](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/572)). The step that holds the event
  is integrated again, from its start, to the time of the label of its end (`PropagationTimeArgument.OnEpochGrid`, up to
  half a tick of 100 ns from it, one more force evaluation), so the state the next segment starts from, the event time
  and the base of the next segment are the same instant, as in RK7(8); a step end on the tick grid keeps its step. Every
  Velocity-Verlet trajectory after an event about the Earth moves by up to v · 5e-8 s per event, the burn epochs by up
  to half a tick: a chain of 7 events without ΔV in 12 h now ends within 1.2e-6 m (10 s steps) to 1.1e-4 m (0.7 s) of
  the propagation without events, Velocity-Verlet's own sensitivity to the phase of its grid, where it ended 1.3e-3 to
  2.0e-3 m away; about the Moon at whole-second steps (ticks) nothing moves. A step end whose label rounds to the tick
  before it reports its event up to 5e-8 s before a root in that last half tick, the continued root still skipped
  (accepted, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18). After an event that continues the
  propagation, Velocity-Verlet starts the detector from its g-value past the root, as RK7(8).
- **Breaking: an impulse at the end of the propagation leaves the solution with the state after it** ([#575](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/575);
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17). An impulse executed with no time left after it opens a last segment of zero length
  from the state after it, one step of zero length, as RK7(8) ends after a root before the end: the last output at the
  end, `InterpolateAt` and `GetEphemeris` there give the state after it, the same doubles as the state before plus the ΔV,
  and `Segments` holds one more segment. The stored states end with a last arc of one state, the state after the
  impulse (the last output); the SPK, whose segments need two epochs, ends with the arc before it, so SPICE reads the
  state before the impulse at that last epoch. A segment shorter than the landing tolerance of RK7(8) is one step of zero
  length too (it was a segment with no step). The propagator asks the integrator for that segment with
  `IntegrateSegment(..., duration: 0.0)`, a call the loop never made before: `IIntegrator.IntegrateSegment` now gives,
  for a duration of zero, a segment of one step of zero length that holds the start state; for an integrator implemented
  outside the library that returns no step there (a `while (t < duration)` loop), the propagator adds that step itself,
  so the solution ends with the state after the burn on that path too. **Migration:** code that reads the last segment of
  a solution finds the segment of zero length after a burn at the end; extend the window past the last maneuver to
  propagate after it. A custom `IIntegrator` should return, for a duration of zero, one `AcceptedStep` of zero length
  from the start state with its acceleration (the propagator otherwise gives that step the acceleration of its forces for
  an `Integrator` subclass, and the end acceleration of the previous segment for a bare `IIntegrator`).
- **Breaking: Velocity-Verlet is of second order with drag** ([#439](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/439)). The acceleration at the end of a step is
  evaluated with the predicted end velocity v + h a instead of the half-step velocity, which kept the drag at t + h wrong
  by O(h): on the dense pass of #439 the error against RK7(8) at 1e-13 is now 6.09 m, 6.09e-2 m and 6.11e-4 m at 1, 0.1
  and 0.01 s (272.6 m, 27.8 m and 2.78 m before), and on a 300 × 400 km LEO with 0.01 m² 0.947 m at 1 s, unchanged (its
  drag error was below the truncation). Every Velocity-Verlet result with drag moves, the default integrator's included;
  without a force that depends on the velocity, bit for bit. No golden of the propagator tests moved.
- **A propagation whose output step does not divide its window moves** ([#626](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/626), Fixed above).
  Its caches cover the span it integrates, up to half an output step past the window: with a geopotential, drag or
  third bodies, its states past window end + 120 s change (7.0 mm after 3 900 s at 600 s outputs, 4.76 m after 88 200 s
  at 3 600 s outputs, 2.4 km after 129 600 s at 86 400 s outputs in #626's measurement), and so the stored states read
  near the end of the window. `PropagationFrameOrientationCache.GetOrientation` and `PropagationEphemerisCache.GetPosition`
  and `GetState`, public, read the frame or the body at their epoch outside their grid, where they held its first or last
  point or extrapolated. A propagation whose step divides its window, as with the common 60 s, does not move. No code
  change is needed.
- **Breaking: a propagation with a geopotential or drag about its central body moves by the orientation it reads** ([#561](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/561), Fixed above).
  With the exact SLERP the orientation of the central body read by the geopotential and by drag moves by up to 3.4e-10
  rad (2.3 mm at a LEO radius): the bit-for-bit goldens of `PropagationGoldenTests` are recaptured, the GEO case moved by
  2.1e-6 m, the maneuver case by 1.1e-6 m (its maneuver epoch unchanged), the SRP case by 1.66 mm with 100 steps instead
  of 103 (the integration error at 1e-11 of other steps). A point-mass propagation, which reads no orientation, does not
  move. The references of the Validation records by central differences of whole propagations take other steps, another
  draw of their noise: the penumbra record of R4 (`StmValidationTests`) is set again at 9.6e-8 (its Φ 4.8e-8 there, 3.6e-9
  before, Φ under test moved by 1.3e-9) and the arc record of Ψ_Cr of the eclipsing case (`ManeuverStmValidationTests`)
  at 3.9e-5 (1.94e-5, 6.2e-6 before, Ψ_Cr under test moved by 4.3e-11), twice the Linux worst, the Validation category
  running on Linux x64 alone (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18). Eleven draws of each reference, its
  start moved by −5 to +5 ulps with the quantity under test unchanged, show the noise of the references: R4 in the
  penumbra 2.3e-9 to 6.7e-8 (2.3e-9 to 1.1e-8 on a85098d), Ψ_Cr over the arc 4.1e-6 to 4.6e-5 (6.2e-6 to 5.6e-5 on
  a85098d, 9 of 11 above the former record). Two records of the test suite that compare propagations at two tolerances
  were drawn again on every platform and set again at twice the worst over Linux x64, Windows x64 and macOS arm64 (CI
  runs 44225490669 and 44237671637), their distributions unchanged over draws one ulp apart: `AvoidanceFallbackTests` in
  RK7(8), the option at 1e-13 against its reference at 1e-14, state 9.40e-5 m, miss 7.73e-5 m and Pc 7.90e-7 on Windows x64
  (on main a85098d at worst 6.36e-5 m, 5.21e-5 m and 4.98e-7, macOS arm64), thresholds 1.9e-4 m, 1.6e-4 m and
  1.6e-6 (8.3e-5 m, 6.8e-5 m and 6.4e-7 before; over 81 draws on Linux x64, 4.9e-7 to 1.02e-4 m after and 7.3e-7 to
  9.62e-5 m before); `MinimumStepNoiseTests`, Φ at 1e-13 against Φ at 1e-14 on the steps of the state, 1.34e-10 on
  Windows x64 (4.95e-11 on main a85098d at worst), threshold 2.7e-10 (9.1e-11 before; over 40 draws on Linux x64,
  2.9e-12 to 2.30e-10 after and 4.9e-12 to 6.35e-10 before), and against central differences 1.14e-7, threshold 2.3e-7
  (2.6e-7 before). Migration: none in code; a golden of a propagation with a geopotential or drag is to be captured
  again.
- **Breaking: a propagation near a third body, SSB mode about the Earth included, moves** ([#576](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/576), [#544](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/544), Fixed above).
  `ThirdBodyPerturbation.Apply` takes the direct difference where the spacecraft is closer to the perturbing body than
  half its distance to the central body (|r − d| < |d|/2): SSB mode near any planet, and a spacecraft near the Moon
  propagated about the Earth (within about 190 000 km of it). Those propagations take other steps and end elsewhere, within
  their integration error (an hour of LEO in SSB mode at 1e-10: 49 steps instead of 21 363); every other propagation is bit
  for bit unchanged. Migration: none in code; a result in SSB mode or near the Moon about the Earth is to be measured
  again, and an RK7(8) tolerance loosened for SSB mode (1e-9) can be tightened.
- **Breaking: the density of Mars air below 54.887 km rises by 2.1e-4 to 3.6e-4** ([#438](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/438), Fixed above).
  Below the isothermal layer (49.887 km) and through its transition (to 54.887 km), `MarsStandardAtmosphere` takes the
  curve fit's own 273.1 instead of 273.15 (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17: 273.1 in the curve fit only, the 139 K
  layer unchanged). The layer is unchanged bit for bit (its base, where the fit's temperature reaches −134.15 °C, kept
  there, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18, where 49 864.86 m would move every layer density by about 0.1 %, and its pressures do not depend on the offset); through the transition the absolute temperature goes from the fit's
  T + 273.1 (138.95 K at the base) to 139 K and the temperature in °C from the fit's to −134.15 °C by the existing
  smootherstep, so the density and its first two derivatives stay continuous. `GetTemperature` and `GetPressure` are
  unchanged. Every density, drag and propagation through Mars air below 54.887 km moves: the RK7(8) run of
  `MarsDragTests` across the base takes 36, 49 and 94 steps at 1e-11, 1e-12 and 1e-13 (35, 47 and 79 before); the
  ratios to Seiff (1982) move by at most 3.6e-4. Migration: none in code; a result that needs the former density
  multiplies it by (T + 273.1) / (T + 273.15) below the base.
- **Breaking: a light-time corrected state in a non-inertial frame is rotated at the epoch of the frame's centre**
  ([#593](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/593), Fixed above). On the reference-body path, a state read with a correction other than `None` in a
  non-inertial frame not centred on the observer moves: by 620 m for the Moon from DSS-13 in
  ITRF93 with `LT`, 1.48 km in MOON_ME, 38 km for a site given by its coordinates in its own frame from the Moon; the
  coordinate searches in such frames move with it. Migration: for the former value, read the state in ICRF and rotate
  it with `ToFrame(frame)`, which rotates at the state's epoch. The native library exports `GetFrameInfoProxy`, which
  the .NET layer of the same release calls: a native library of an earlier release throws `EntryPointNotFoundException`
  there.
- **A light-time corrected read of two objects of the kernels in a frame only the library holds moves** ([#739](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/739), Fixed above).
  With a correction other than `None`, a state read by CSPICE in TEME, CIRS, TIRS, the frame of a site given by its
  coordinates or the frame of a managed spacecraft with an attitude record, not centred on the observer, takes the frame
  at the epoch of its centre: the Earth from the Moon in TIRS with `LT` by 3.9e4 m, the Moon from the Earth in the frame
  of a site by 620 m, TEME and CIRS by millimetres; the coordinate searches that read such states move with them.
  `None`, inertial frames and frames centred on the observer are unchanged, bit for bit. Migration: for the former value,
  read the state in ICRF and rotate it with `ToFrame(frame)`, which rotates at the state's epoch.
- **Breaking: `InstrumentPointingToAttitude` applies its light time, and takes an `Aberration`** ([#549](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/549), Fixed
  above; decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17). The constructor takes an optional `aberration`, `Aberration.LT` by default,
  what the law requested, exposed as `Aberration`; an undefined value throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`. Every
  pointing at a celestial target moves to its light-time direction (the Moon by 4.4e-5 to 9.2e-5 rad from a LEO), and
  so do the attitude records and the CKs written from them; a site target takes the light time from the spacecraft; a
  `Star` target takes no light time, so only its `+S` corrections move it, by its stellar aberration.
  Migration: pass `Aberration.None` for the former geometric direction of a celestial target; recompile, the
  constructor's signature changed.
- **A spacecraft or a custom body is about the observer of its initial orbit** ([#747](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/747), Fixed above).
  `CenterOfMotionId` and `BarycenterOfMotionId` of a `Spacecraft` or a `CelestialBody` built from custom parameters are
  the observer of its initial orbital parameters and that observer's barycentre (399 and 3 about the Earth), where they
  were 0 and 0 whatever the orbit; without an initial orbit they stay 0, and `Spacecraft.SetInitialOrbitalParameters`
  sets them from the new orbit. Migration: none; a caller that read them for such an item gets the centre of its orbit.
- **NOTO and NEW NORCIA are read by their identifier** ([#750](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/750), Fixed above). `SpiceAPI.ReadEphemeris`
  by identifiers from 398989 or 398990, a frame centred on them on the reference-body path, and the CLI's `ephemeris` and
  `sub-point` of them read them from SPICE (`InvalidOperationException` without their SPK) where they threw
  `ArgumentException` for the body 398; the observer of the state is an object of the kernels named NOTO or NEW NORCIA.
  Migration: none; a caller that caught `ArgumentException` for them catches SPICE's `InvalidOperationException`.
- **`CelestialAttitudeTarget` corrects from the spacecraft** ([#740](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/740), Fixed above). An attitude built
  on a `CelestialAttitudeTarget` with a correction other than `None` (`TriadAttitude` and its records and CKs) moves:
  from a LEO by 1.0e-6 rad for the Moon with `LT`, about 2.5e-5 rad with a `+S` correction, 1.0e-4 rad for the central
  body with `LT`. `None`, the default, is unchanged, bit for bit. No signature changes.
- **Breaking: `InitialOrbitDetermination.CreateFromObservation_Gauss` reads the observer at its geometric position**
  ([#489](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/489), Fixed above). The observer's
  position relative to the centre of motion at each observation epoch is read without light time (`Aberration.None`),
  where it took the observer at t − lt: every determination moves, by the Earth's motion over the light time from the
  Sun about the Sun (Mars from DSS-13 at 10 days: 5.65e-2 to 6.94e-2 % of the position against the state from the Sun
  with `LT`, the error of the method at that spacing), and about the Earth by the site's rotation over its light time
  from the Earth's centre for a site read by CSPICE (a kernel site), a site given by its coordinates already read
  geometric before this release. Migration: none in code; observations are the target's directions from the observer
  at each epoch, corrected for the target's light time as before.
- **Breaking: two times are equal when they are the same instant** ([#512](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/512), Fixed above; decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-17). `Time.Equals`, `==`, `!=` and `GetHashCode` follow `CompareTo`, the one order of times by their ticks
  converted to TAI, within a frame and across frames: `utc == utc.ToTDB()` is true and both hash alike, so a hash
  collection keyed by times finds the same instant in another frame. Within UTC, TAI, TT and GPS the order is that of
  the calendars, as before; within TDB too, but for two consecutive TDB ticks that convert to one TAI tick (TDB − TT,
  rounded to the tick, gains one there, about every 300 s near its steepest), which are now equal and compare to 0,
  where they compared by their calendars, so that equality stays transitive. `Window` equality is that of its two ends
  as instants, `Length` excluded (a UTC window built from a length across a leap second equals the window of its ends),
  and so the equality of every record that holds a time (`StateOrientation`, `Equatorial`, a tuple) compares it as an
  instant. A local time (`TimeFrame.LocalFrame`) is the instant `DateTime.ToUniversalTime` gives its calendar in the
  zone of the machine, local times compared with each other included, where they compared by their calendars: in a zone
  with daylight saving time, two labels of the skipped hour and the hour after it are one instant (in America/New_York,
  local 2025-03-09T02:30 and 03:30 are both 07:30 UTC, and 02:30 comes after 03:00), and a label of the repeated hour
  built from its calendar is read with the standard offset (the `ToLocal()` of an instant keeps the instant, #751, Fixed
  above) (`ColdStartTests.LocalTimes_AreTheInstantsOfTheirZone`, skipped on Windows, where `TZ`
  does not set the zone; red with a85098d's comparison of local calendars restored). The default time (no frame) comes
  before every time with a frame and equals only itself, so comparing it no longer throws `NullReferenceException` (`<`,
  `SortedSet`, `Window` of it). The library's comparisons follow: `AddPropagatedStates` replaces a stored state at the
  same instant in another frame, and `StateVector.ToStateVector(epoch)` still relabels a state read at its instant in
  another frame (a label comparison, internal `Time.HasSameLabel`); the library's caches whose values carry their key as
  a label (the orientations of a `Frame` and of `TLEPropagator`, the range rates read once by the conjunction search)
  stay keyed by label (internal `Time.LabelComparer`), so an orientation carries the epoch asked and the bisection of a
  TCA in ticks (#624) reads both of two consecutive TDB ticks, bit for bit as before; the other comparisons of the
  library (the ends of the dense search, the `Distinct()` of the knots, the epoch checks of the propagators) are on
  instants (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18). Results move only for two TDB
  ticks of one TAI tick, by a tick at most. Within TDB, `-` still counts the ticks of the calendars: two equal
  consecutive TDB ticks differ by one tick.
  Migration: code that told two labels of one instant apart by `==`, `Equals` or `Assert.Equal` compares `DateTime` and
  `Frame` (the tests of the library's labels do so through `LabelAssert`: 380 assertions that `Assert.Equal` or `==`
