  with a NaN velocity from `ToStateVector()`, a negative semi-major axis from `ToKeplerianElements()` and NaN states from
  `AtEpoch` and `ToStateVector(Time)` (so from the start of a propagation and the CLI's `--from-equinoctial`), a P of
  ±Infinity on an ellipse a non-finite state, and a parabola of perigee radius ≤ 0 or NaN the same kind of result
  (measured on a85098d, as in the issue). It now throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (`p`) for a P that is not finite
  and above 0 (p = h²/μ > 0 for every conic; −0.0 included), a non-finite P being accepted only in the parabolic band
  |e − 1| < 1e-6, where #452 documents it with a perigee radius as the way to give a parabola, and
  (`perigeeRadius`) for a perigee radius given and not finite and above 0, as SPICE CONICS rejects rp ≤ 0
  (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17, the recommendation of the issue: the check in the constructor, no bound beyond
  P > 0). The elements the library builds pass (`ToEquinoctial()`, whose P is finite since #462, and the TLE fit, which
  raises P to keep its perigee). The ellipse row of `WithoutAFinitePOrAPerigeeRadius_TheStateIsUndefined` (P = NaN) now
  throws from the constructor, and the P < 0 row of `ConvertEquinoctialElementsToStateVector_OutsideTheDomainOfEqncpv`
  too (a semi-major axis ≤ 0 with P > 0 needs e > 1, outside EQNCPV's e ≤ 0.9). Tests: `ElementsValidationTests.Issue481_*`
  (red on a85098d), `OrbitalParametersTests.EquinoctialWithANegativeSemiLatusRectum_IsRefused` (CLI). Migration: give P
  finite and above 0, or a parabola's non-finite P with its perigee radius.
- **Breaking: within 1e-6 of e = 1 the semi-major axis, the mean motion and the state are the conic's** ([#459](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/459)).
  `IsParabolic()` holds for |e − 1| < 1e-6, and the whole band was taken as a parabola whatever its energy:
  `StateVector.SemiMajorAxis()` and `EquinoctialElements.SemiMajorAxis()` returned +Infinity where the conic has
  −μ/(2ξ) (about 1.4e10 km at |e − 1| = 5e-7), `MeanMotion()` Barker's √(μ/(2q³)), 2e9 times the conic's √(μ/|a|³)
  at ±5e-7, the state of elements in the band took p = 2q where the conic has q (1 + e), so that
  `sv.ToKeplerianElements().ToStateVector()` and the equinoctial round trips moved a state by |r| |e − 1| / (1 + e)
  (1.9 m at ±5e-7, 3.4 m at ±9e-7, 4.2e7 m near the apoapsis of an ellipse given at e = 0.999999, which comes back in
  the band from its state about one time in four), and `KeplerianElements` refused a finite semi-major axis in the band
  (measured on a85098d). Option 1 of the issue (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17): `SemiMajorAxis()` is the conic's for
  every e ≠ 1, +Infinity for e = 1 exactly (`StateVector`: −μ/(2ξ), +Infinity for ξ = 0 too, which rounding gives the state of
  an exact parabola whose e is one ulp off 1; `EquinoctialElements`: P / (1 − F² − G²), +Infinity where it overflows, or
  q / (1 − e) for a non-finite P given its perigee radius); `MeanMotion()` is √(μ/|a|³), Barker's only for an infinite semi-major
  axis; the state of elements in the band takes the conic's p = q (1 + e), 2q at e = 1 bit for bit; and
  `KeplerianElements` accepts in the band, with the perigee radius q it requires (not derived from a finite a, whose
  q = a (1 − e) would carry a relative rounding of 1e-16/|1 − e|, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18), the semi-major axis of the same conic,
  a (1 − e) = q to rounding: |q/a − (1 − e)| ≤ 6 ε (1 + e), twice the 3.0 ε (1 + e) measured on Linux x64, Windows x64
  and macOS arm64 over 6400 states of the band (|e − 1| from 0 to 9.99e-7, q from 6600 km to 1 AU) through every path
  that builds elements there (the state, equinoctial elements, `AtEpoch`, SPICE's `oscltx`);
  +Infinity at e = 1 exactly, and within a few ulps of it only (the state of an exact parabola, whose e rounds off 1
  where ξ rounds to 0). The a of another conic throws `ArgumentException` (`semiMajorAxis`), as it did on a85098d: the
  review of #459 measured `new KeplerianElements(7e6, 1 − 5e-7, ..., perigeeRadius: 7e6)` built with the semi-major axis,
  mean motion, period and apoapsis of a 7000 km circle and the state of the near-parabola, and a = −7e6 or +Infinity at
  e ≠ 1 built too (+Infinity giving the pre-#459 values). A missing perigee radius throws `ArgumentException`
  (`perigeeRadius`). `SpiceAPI.ConvertStateVectorToConicOrbitalElement` forced a = +Infinity in the band, so Barker's
  mean motion, 2e9 times the conic's at ±5e-7 (measured by the review): it keeps `oscltx`'s −μ/(2ξ), +Infinity where
  `oscltx` gives 0 (e = 1 or a zero energy) (`NearParabolicBandTests.Issue459_InTheBand_*`,
  `Issue459_SpiceConversionInTheBand_*`, red on the branch before the review; the measurement of the tolerance is
  `Issue459_InTheBand_TheElementsOfASweepOfStatesAreOneConic`). The
  motion of the band keeps Barker's anomaly, well conditioned there: `AtEpoch`, `ToKeplerianElements(Time)` and
  `EpochAtMeanAnomaly` (so `ToStateVector(Time)`, `TimeToRadius`, the start of a propagation) advance it at Barker's
  rate through a private method, the public `MeanMotion()` being the conic's. Outside the band every result is
  unchanged, bit for bit; at e = 1 exactly too. Against 60-digit references (`tools/near_parabolic/near_parabolic_reference.py`): a and n
  within 6.2e-16 and 9.3e-16 relative times |e − 1| (the cancellation of ξ, ε v²/(2|ξ|): 6e-10 at ±5e-7, 6e-4 at
  ±1e-12), the round trips within 6.0e-16 of |r|, the state 600 s later within 6.1e-16 of the band model and 0.16 m of
  the exact conic (1.8e-7 m at |e − 1| = 1e-12; 0.54 m from the periapsis at 5e-7), and the double edges of the band as
  Keplerian elements (0.9999990000000001 and the double nearest 1.000001, both inside it, with their finite a, red on
  a85098d) within 2.9e-16 (`NearParabolicBandTests.Issue459_*`, red on a85098d; thresholds twice the worst over Linux
  x64, Windows x64 and macOS arm64). The comment of the issue asked for the solvers of #467 to be measured inside the band before Barker's law is
  kept for all of it: Kepler's equation for the conic, solved by `KeplerEquation` in doubles from the state's a, e and
  ν, is 2.3 to 5.8 mm from the exact motion at |e − 1| = 5e-7 to 9e-7, better than Barker's law there (0.09 to 0.16 m),
  and 2.8 to 5.0 km off at |e − 1| = 1e-12, where Barker's law is within 1.8e-7 m
  (`NearParabolicBandTests.Issue459_KeplersEquationForTheConic_AgainstBarkersLaw`, on the 60-digit references of
  `tools/near_parabolic`): neither holds over the whole band, so Barker's law is kept as decided. A motion that holds
  over it (universal variables, or a band narrowed to where Barker's law is the better one) would change what
  `IsParabolic()` means across the library: it is not part of 11.0.0 and needs its own issue, #753. The tests of #477 that measured the 2q of the band now measure
  rounding (3.6e-16 where 2.0e-7), and `TestHelpers.KeplerComparer` and `EquinoctialComparer` compare two orbits of the
  band by their perigee radii, their semi-major axes being ill-conditioned there (`StateVectorTests.ToParabolicKeplerian`,
  `KeplerianElementsTests.ParabolicToState`, `EquinoctialElementsTests.ParabolicToStateVector`: the state of an exact
  parabola has a semi-major axis of about ±1e20 m, or +Infinity at a zero energy). Migration: code that read +Infinity from `SemiMajorAxis()` to recognize the band
  calls `IsParabolic()`; code that took `MeanMotion()` as the rate of the mean anomaly in the band uses `AtEpoch` or
  `EpochAtMeanAnomaly`; elements within 1e-6 of e = 1 given +Infinity at e ≠ 1 (the only form 10.x accepted) give
  instead the conic's a, q / (1 − e), with the perigee radius.
- **Breaking: `Period()` of an open orbit throws `InvalidOperationException`** ([#663](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/663), item 3 of [#455](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/455)).
  `Period()` passed 2π √(a³/μ) to `TimeSpan.FromSeconds` without a check: a hyperbola (a < 0) threw TimeSpan's
  `ArgumentException` "TimeSpan does not accept floating point Not-a-Number values", a parabola (a = +Infinity) its
  `OverflowException`, with no message saying that an open orbit has no period (measured on a85098d, as in the
  issue). It now throws `InvalidOperationException` naming e and a when the semi-major axis is not finite and above 0
  (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17, the fix of the issue: the test is on a, not on e, so the conic's finite a of the
  near-parabolic band keeps its period, #459), before the cached period, so that a period given to `KeplerianElements`
  for an open orbit, or the 0 of SPICE's `oscltx` for one (`SpiceAPI.ConvertStateVectorToConicOrbitalElement`), is not
  returned either (the review of #663 measured 01:00:00 and 00:00:00; `Issue663_AnOpenOrbitGivenAPeriod_HasNoPeriod`).
  `ConvertStateVectorToConicOrbitalElement` passes SPICE's period only when it is above 0 and fits a `TimeSpan`: an
  ellipse at e = 1 − 2e-6, whose period is 2.1e12 s, threw `OverflowException` from the conversion and is now built
  (`Issue663_SpicesElementsOfAnEllipseWithoutATimeSpanPeriod_AreBuilt`). An ellipse whose period exceeds
  `TimeSpan.MaxValue` (29 227 years: within 1e-6 of e = 1, for instance) still throws `TimeSpan`'s `OverflowException`
  from `Period()`, now documented. The callers
  (`PhasingManeuver`, `CosmographiaExporter`) let it through, as before. Tests: `ElementsValidationTests.Issue663_*` on
  a `StateVector` at escape speed and above, Keplerian and equinoctial hyperbolas and parabolas (red on a85098d), and an
  ellipse unchanged. Migration: catch `InvalidOperationException` instead of `ArgumentException` or `OverflowException`,
  or test `IsElliptical()` first.
- **Breaking: mean elements stay mean through `AtEpoch` and `ToKeplerianElements(Time)`, and a propagation refuses a mean initial orbit** ([#463](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/463)).
  `AtEpoch(t)` and `ToKeplerianElements(t)` built their `KeplerianElements` without `elementsType`, so mean elements came
  back labelled `Osculating`, even at their own epoch, and the guard of `ToStateVector()` let them through: a spacecraft
  whose initial orbit was a mean set in an inertial frame (`KeplerianElements.FromOMM(..., Frame.ICRF)`, the public
  constructors with `Mean`) was propagated from the two-body state of the mean numbers, with no error, by every path
  (11.75 km and 7.7 m/s from SGP4 at the epoch for the ISS, 468 km after a day; measured on a85098d, as in the issue);
  only a mean TEME set was refused, by the inertial-frame check. The recommendations of the issue (decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-17): both methods keep `ElementsType`; `ToKeplerianElements(Time)` is virtual and a `TLE`
  overrides it as `ToKeplerianElements().ToKeplerianElements(epoch)`, its osculating SGP4 set moved in time, which stays
  `Osculating` (as before); and every `CentralBodyPropagator` constructor (so `Spacecraft.Propagate` and
  `PropagateAsync`, `CentralBodyPropagatorBuilder`, `Scenario.SimulateAsync`) throws `ArgumentException` (`spacecraft`)
  naming the spacecraft and pointing to `TLEPropagator` and `TLE.ToOsculating()` for a mean initial orbit other than a
  TLE, checked with the inertial-frame check before the initial state is computed (a mean TEME set still meets the frame
  check first, `TlePropagationTests.MeanTemeSet_StaysRejected`). `AtEpoch` of mean elements advances the mean anomaly at
  the two-body mean motion only, without the secular rates of the theory, as before, now documented; a mean set moved to
  its own epoch writes the same TLE through `TLE.Create`, which refused it before. Osculating elements and states are
  unchanged, bit for bit (only labels change), so no golden moves. Tests: `MeanElementsTypeTests` (mean Keplerian and
  equinoctial sets from `FromOMM`, `TLE.ToMeanKeplerianElements()`, `ToEquinoctial()` and the constructors, in ICRF and
  `ECLIPTIC_J2000`, at their epoch and an hour later; the seven propagation paths, Velocity-Verlet and RK7(8), windows at
  and after the epoch; the TLE's osculating set within 8.9e-16 of CSPICE `prop2b` over the TT seconds of the hour on
  Linux x64 and macOS arm64, 3.8e-15 on Windows x64, whose native library MSVC builds, threshold twice the worst), red
  on a85098d. Migration: propagate a TLE with `TLEPropagator` or
  start from `TLE.ToOsculating()` (or the TLE itself, whose SGP4 state starts the propagation); build osculating
  elements for a numerical propagation.
- **Breaking: `Spacecraft.SetStandbyManeuver` sets the head of the maneuver chain**
  ([#584](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/584), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-17). `InitialManeuver` and `StandbyManeuver` both become the given maneuver, whatever was set before or left by
  a propagation, null clears the chain, and nothing is added to `ExecutedManeuvers`, which lists the maneuvers of the
  last propagation. The advance of the chain inside a propagation keeps its bookkeeping in the internal
  `ChainStandbyManeuver`. Migration: a caller that called `SetStandbyManeuver` several times to build a chain links it
  with `SetNextManeuver` and sets its head once; one that read `ExecutedManeuvers` between the call and the propagation
  no longer finds the previous head there.
- **Breaking: every numerical propagation re-arms the spacecraft and makes it `IsPropagated`**
  ([#583](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/583), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-17). `PropagatorBase.Propagate` resets the spacecraft once its checks pass (the tanks refuelled,
  `ExecutedManeuvers`, the stored states, the attitude record and the gates cleared, the chain put back in standby from
  `InitialManeuver`), and `IsPropagated` is true after a run through `CentralBodyPropagatorBuilder` or a
  `CentralBodyPropagator` built directly, as after `Spacecraft.Propagate` (false before). A propagator built and not run
  changes nothing. Migration: a caller that propagated one spacecraft several times through the builder to continue a
  chain (the second run started from the fuel and the standby maneuver the first left) propagates once over the whole
  window, or sets the next head with `SetStandbyManeuver` and the state with `SetInitialOrbitalParameters`.
- **Breaking: a propagated spacecraft is read within its propagated states**
  ([#527](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/527), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-17). `Spacecraft.GetGeometricStateRelativeTo`, `GetEphemeris` and every read through them (the managed
  geometry and field-of-view searches, `IsInFOV`, the attitude targets) throw `InvalidOperationException`, as a
  read past the coverage of SPICE, at an epoch before the first stored state or after the last, the epoch a light-time
  correction reads allowed up to its light time outside them. The window checks of the conjunction overloads and of the
  field-of-view search (`ArgumentException`, #622) are unchanged. Migration: read a propagated spacecraft within its
  propagation window, or propagate it over the epochs read. The stored states run from the first output to the last,
  round(L/ΔT)·ΔT after the start for a window of length L at outputs ΔT, up to ΔT/2 after the end of the window when ΔT
  rounds it up, and to the window end when ΔT rounds it down (#741, under Fixed: they stopped up to ΔT/2 before it, a
  3 610 s window at 60 s outputs storing its states to 3 600 s), so every epoch of the window can be read.
- **Breaking: `Spacecraft.ToOpm` writes the propagated state, mass and maneuvers of its epoch**
  ([#658](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/658), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-17). A spacecraft that holds propagated states writes `GetEphemeris(epoch, observer, frame, Aberration.None)`
  with the observer and the frame of its initial orbital parameters, with the mass and the impulses ignited by then
  (its mass after the propagation plus the fuel of the impulses ignited after the epoch, and only the impulses ignited
  by the epoch), an impulse counting from the start of its thrust window, the `MAN_EPOCH_IGNITION` written (between the
  ignition and the event, about half of the burn since #335, the state written is still the state before the impulse); an epoch outside the propagated states, the default one included when the propagation
  started later, throws `InvalidOperationException` (#527). A spacecraft without propagated states writes the motion of
  its initial orbit as before. Migration: pass the epoch of the instant to export, the end of the propagation for the
  state after every maneuver (the default epoch, the initial one, kept, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18, now carries no maneuver of a propagation that starts
  there); a caller that wanted the initial orbit writes `Opm.CreateFromStateVector` from `InitialOrbitalParameters`.

- **Breaking: `EvaluateAvoidance` refuses a step of zero or less** ([#640](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/640), Fixed above).
  `AvoidanceSearchOptions.AnalysisSampleStep` and `MaximumEventSearchStep`, when given, must be positive, the rule of
  `ConjunctionAnalysisOptions`: `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (its `ParamName` the option), where a negative step was
  accepted or the call ran out of memory. Migration: give a positive step, or null for the encounter's.

- **Breaking: a window without a close approach gives its closest end, flagged, and `AnalyzeAll` nothing** ([#621](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/621), Fixed above).
  `Analyze`, `Screen` and the re-analysis of each avoidance option return the closest window end where the sampled path
  returned the midpoint (and where the search on two propagations returned the end the distance grows into, the same end
  but for a minimum its seeds miss), with `EncounterQualityFlags.TcaAtWindowEnd` (new, `1 << 8`) raised; the
  `ILocalizable` `AnalyzeAll` returns an empty list where it returned one midpoint encounter. Every encounter of a
  window without a close approach carries the flag, the CDM export's comment of the flags included; a close approach the
  sampled search finds on a window end (its range-rate zero in the half-tick next to the end, the tick nearer it #624
  returns) does not, and `AnalyzeAll` lists it
  (`ConjunctionKernelAndWindowTests.CloseApproachInTheLastHalfTick_IsListedAtTheEnd_NotFlagged`, red on 415442e, where
  the flag was raised for any TCA on a window end). Migration: test
  `QualityFlags.HasFlag(EncounterQualityFlags.TcaAtWindowEnd)` for an encounter whose closest approach lies outside the
  window, and widen the window to find it; expect an empty list from `AnalyzeAll` where one midpoint encounter came.

- **Breaking: the remediation of an initial covariance is bounded** ([#443](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/443), decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17; the two frames and the bound of 1e-3, a producer of 3 significant digits needing 1e-2, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18).
  `StateVector.WithRemediatedCovariance()` and the conjunction analysis remediated any indefinite covariance by eigenvalue
  clipping, however deep its defect: a T–Ṙ correlation of −10 by a change of 5.5 times the values, flagged
  `CovarianceRemediated` only. Both now refuse a defect deeper than the rounding of the elements to 4 significant digits
  (the form of the CDM's covariances, CCSDS 508.0-B-1, confirmed by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18) explains: the smallest eigenvalue
  of the correlation matrix below −1e-3 of its trace (`CovarianceChecks.RemediationDepthBound`) in the frame of the state
  and in its RTN frame (the frame a CDM rounds in; a rotation deepens a rounding defect, up to −0.11 of the trace measured
  for covariances rounded in RTN). The bound is above the rigorous worst of that rounding, 8.34e-4 of the trace by Weyl's
  inequality (measured: 1.5e-4 over 6000 LEO and GEO covariances of ranks 1 to 6, 2.1e-4 by an adversarial search). A
  correlation of −1.01 in RTN (1.67e-3 of the trace) is refused; −1.0059 (9.8e-4) is remediated. The clipping is made in
  the frame of the state when the depth passes there, bit for bit as before; otherwise in the RTN frame of the state,
  rotated back: clipped in the frame of the state, a covariance rounded in RTN whose depth there reached −0.75 of the
  trace changed by up to 2.9 √(M_ii M_jj) (adversarial review of #443); clipped in RTN, by the size of its rounding
  (4.4e-4 at worst over 83 such covariances, `WithRemediatedCovariance_DeepOnlyInTheFrameOfTheState_IsClippedInRtn`, red
  on b8e2e42).
  `WithRemediatedCovariance` throws `InvalidOperationException` with the depth in both frames in its message; the
  analysis holds such a covariance in RTN, as its other refusals, without `CovarianceRemediated`
  (`CovarianceRemediationBoundTests`, `ConjunctionCovarianceEdgeTests.Analyze_InitialCovarianceBeyondTheDepthBound_IsHeldInRtn`,
  red on a85098d for every case beyond the bound). Results change only for such a covariance. Migration: a covariance
  refused by the bound is not one that rounding explains: correct its source, or give it at its full precision (one
  rounded to 3 digits or fewer may be refused).

- **Breaking: a CSPICE window search returns every window, up to 10000** ([#653](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/653), Fixed above).
  `SpiceAPI.FindWindowsOnDistanceConstraint`, `FindWindowsOnCoordinateConstraint`, `FindWindowsOnIlluminationConstraint`,
  `FindWindowsOnOccultationConstraint` and `FindWindowsInFieldOfViewConstraint`, and the CSPICE paths of the searches of
  `CelestialItem`, `Site` and `Instrument`, return every window CSPICE finds where they returned the first 1000, and an
  illumination search of 1001 to 10000 windows returns them where it threw; beyond 10000 each throws
  `InvalidOperationException` with the long message of CSPICE's `SPICE(WINDOWEXCESS)` ("Window has size, 20000,
  cardinality 20000. Cannot insert an additional interval into the window."; the short code is not in the message).
  Migration: a caller that split its search window to stay under 1000 windows (the workaround of
  the known limitation of the earlier previews) can search the whole window; one that needs more than 10000 windows
  splits it under 10000. The native proxies take two more arguments, the capacity of the buffer and the count written:
  the native library and the .NET library of 11.0.0 go together.

- **Breaking: the window reads of `SpiceAPI` are on the grid start + i·step** ([#563](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/563), Fixed above).
  `SpiceAPI.ReadEphemeris(Window, ...)` and `ReadOrientation` read at start + i·step in the time frame of the window
  start (UTC steps for a UTC window, which the native layer stepped in TDB), i from 0 while within the window, the end
  included when it falls on the grid: one more state or record where the drift of the former stepping dropped the last
  epoch (6001 for 6000 over 600 s at 0.1 s), and the epochs and labels of `ReadEphemeris` exactly on the grid where they
  drifted (by up to 4.29e-4 s after 9000 steps), labelled in the frame of the window start as before. `ReadOrientation` reads any number of epochs, where
  more than 10000 threw `InvalidOperationException`, and a step of zero or less throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`
  (`stepSize`) in both, where `ReadEphemeris` ran out of memory for 0 and read 10000 epochs backwards for a negative step.
  Migration: a caller that dropped or matched the drifting epochs reads the grid itself; one that relied on the last
  epoch being absent drops it. The native read proxies take the epochs: the native library and the .NET library of
  11.0.0 go together.
- **Breaking: a `MemoryDataProvider` no longer reads orientations stored under the name CIRS or TIRS** ([#656](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/656), Fixed above).
  `FrameTransformationToICRF` of a frame named CIRS or TIRS, in any case, returns the managed `Frame.CIRS` or
  `Frame.TIRS` (an instance of `CirsFrame` or `TirsFrame` its own), as it did for TEME, where it read the orientations
  `AddStateOrientationToICRF` stored under that name. Migration: none to read the IAU frames; a caller who stored another
  frame under one of those names gives it another name.

- **Breaking: `MemoryDataProvider.GetEphemeris` throws `NotSupportedException` for an aberration other than `None`, and `ArgumentException` for a frame it neither stores nor knows** ([#559](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/559), Fixed above).
  The provider holds geometric states only, and returned them for a read with light time or stellar aberration. It now
  refuses them (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17: an in-memory test provider; refusing is honest, and smaller than a
  light-time iteration on the stored states; `NotSupportedException`, not the `ArgumentException` of a bad argument,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18), so a library path that reads with an aberration (an occultation or
  illumination search with `LT`, `CelestialBody.TrueSolarDay`, a `CelestialAttitudeTarget` with `LT`) throws on it.
  Its reads in a frame other than ICRF's axes are rotated (Fixed above), so the orbit of a body built on it, in
  ECLIPJ2000 by default, changes numbers. A read in a frame without stored orientations other than ICRF, GCRF,
  ECLIPJ2000, TEME, CIRS and TIRS (any body-fixed frame, such as `IAU_EARTH` or the Earth's `ITRF93`) throws
  `ArgumentException` ("Frame not found"), where it returned the ICRF difference labelled with that frame. Migration:
  read with `Aberration.None`, or with a `SpiceDataProvider`; for another frame, store its orientations with
  `AddStateOrientationToICRF(frame, date, orientation)` over the epochs read (from SPICE, for example
  `SpiceAPI.Instance.TransformFrame(date, frame, Frame.ICRF)`), or read in ICRF, the numbers returned before.

- **Breaking: `Frame` keeps no orientations; the attitude record API is `SpacecraftFrame`'s** ([#541](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/541), Fixed above).
  The protected `_stateOrientationsToICRF` and `StateOrientationsToICRF` of `Frame` are removed, and
  `AddStateOrientationToICRF`, `GetStateOrientationsToICRF`, `GetLatestStateOrientationToICRF` and
  `ClearStateOrientations`, virtual on `Frame`, are members of `SpacecraftFrame`, the only frame that implemented them
  as an attitude record (decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17); `Spacecraft.Frame` is a `SpacecraftFrame`, so its callers
  compile unchanged. On another frame they stored the orientations given in the frame's own dictionary, the one its
  reads filled, so an orientation added at an epoch that instance had not read yet replaced the data provider's at that
  exact epoch, for that instance only and outside a propagation's orientation cache (measured on a85098d: a 0.3 rad
  rotation about z added to `new Frame("ITRF93")` at an epoch was read back there, not SPICE's; `CirsFrame` alike); that
  override is removed, and the frame reads its provider. A frame
  keeps the orientation of its last epoch only: an orientation added to a `MemoryDataProvider` at the epoch the frame
  read last is read once the frame has read another epoch (kept, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18). Migration: a subclass of `Frame` that used the dictionary keeps its
  own store; code that added orientations to another frame to override its provider gives them to a `MemoryDataProvider`
  (`AddStateOrientationToICRF(frame, date, orientation)`), set as the data provider, whose frames read them (the managed
  TEME, CIRS and TIRS excepted, #656).

- **Breaking: the command line prints `Frame : J2000` for ICRF on every path** ([#657](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/657), Fixed above).
  `astro ephemeris` from a body or a kernel-backed spacecraft, and `astro orientation` of a kernel-backed spacecraft, in
  the default frame ICRF or a frame named `icrf` or `j2000`, printed `Frame : j2000`; they print `Frame : J2000`, as a
  site observer did. Numbers unchanged. Migration: a script that parses the label reads `J2000`, or compares it ignoring
  case.
- **Breaking: the two-body calls of `SpiceAPI` return the caller's observer and frame** ([#725](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/725)).
  The results of `Propagate2Bodies`, `ConvertStateVectorToConicOrbitalElement`, `ConvertConicElementsToStateVector` and
  `ConvertEquinoctialElementsToStateVector` (every overload) carried a new `CelestialBody` built from the identifier of
  the centre (`ProfilesConfiguration.Convert` of the native result) and a frame rebuilt from its name: the caller's
  geopotential and atmospheric model were lost, so a propagation started from the result ran about a point-mass Earth
  without the caller's atmosphere (#674 takes the models of the observer), a barycentre threw "Celestial celestialItem
  frame can't be defined" (measured on a85098d), and a body built from custom parameters of an identifier SPICE does not
  name threw `ArgumentException` from the overloads with an explicit GM. Each result now carries the observer and the
  frame instances of its input (`SpiceApiElementConversionTests.TwoBodyCalls_ReturnTheObserverAndTheFrameOfTheirInput`:
  the Earth with EGM2008 10×10 and the 1976 atmosphere, the Earth-Moon barycentre and a custom body, in
  ECLIPJ2000, red on a85098d for all three). The positions, velocities, elements and epochs are unchanged, bit for bit.
  Migration: none for a caller that read the observer's identifier or name; a caller that relied on a body read from the
  kernels gets its own instance back (build the observer from the kernels to have one).
- **Breaking: `SpiceAPI.ConvertEquinoctialElementsToStateVector` returns the state of its elements** ([#450](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/450), Fixed above).
  Its state was that of the elements with L0 read as a mean longitude; it is now the state at the true longitude L0, as
  `EquinoctialElements.ToStateVector()` gives it (within 1.0e-15 relative of the 60-digit closed form). Circular orbits,
  whose two longitudes coincide, give the same state. Migration: a caller that passed the mean longitude as L0 to work
  around the defect passes the true longitude.
- **Breaking: a site identifier is about its body, not an asteroid** ([#651](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/651), Fixed above).
  `SpiceAPI.GetCelestialBodyInfo` (so `SpiceDataProvider.GetCelestialBodyInfo` and the command `celestial-body-info`) of a
  site identifier, 100001 to 999999 with a planet or a moon SPICE names as body (399013 for DSS-13), gives its body as
  `CenterOfMotionId` and its body's barycentre as `BarycenterOfMotionId` (399 and 3), where it gave 10 and 0;
  `CelestialItem.IsAsteroid` is false for it, and a `CelestialBody` of that identifier is about its body, its
  `ToString` naming no type. Every other identifier is classed as before. Migration: a caller that read the Sun as the
  centre of a station reads its body.
- **Breaking: the CDM writer puts the root outside the NDM/XML namespace** ([#615](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/615), Fixed above). The text of
  every written CDM changes: `<ndm xmlns:xsi="..." xmlns:ndm="urn:ccsds:schema:ndmxml" xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="..."><ndm:cdm ...><ndm:header>...`, or
  `<cdm xmlns:xsi="..." xmlns:ndm="urn:ccsds:schema:ndmxml" xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="..." id="CCSDS_CDM_VERS" version="1.0"><ndm:header>...` with
  `wrapInNdmContainer: false`, where it was `<ndm xmlns="urn:ccsds:schema:ndmxml"><cdm ...>` and
  `<cdm ... xmlns="urn:ccsds:schema:ndmxml">`. The values are unchanged and the library reads both forms. Migration: a
  namespace-aware consumer that looked for the root `{urn:ccsds:schema:ndmxml}ndm` or `{urn:ccsds:schema:ndmxml}cdm`
  looks for `ndm` or `cdm` in no namespace (the elements below it keep the namespace); one that removed the namespace of
  the root to validate against the SANA schema no longer needs to.
- **Breaking: the CCSDS writers follow the kind of each date** ([#617](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/617), Fixed above; decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-17). `CdmWriter` (`Cdm.WriteTo*`) writes a date of kind `Unspecified` as the UTC clock reading given, where it
  shifted it by the offset of the machine's zone; a CDM written in UTC, read by `Cdm.ReadFrom*` (kind `Utc`) or exported
  by `ToCdm` is unchanged. `OpmWriter` and `OmmWriter` (`Opm.SaveTo*`, `ToXmlString`, `Omm.SaveTo*`, `ToXml`) write a date
  of kind `Local` as its UTC under `TIME_SYSTEM = UTC` and throw `ArgumentException` (`opm`, `omm`) naming the keyword
  for an `EPOCH`, `REF_FRAME_EPOCH` or `MAN_EPOCH_IGNITION` of kind `Local` under any other time system, where they wrote
  its clock reading; a local `CREATION_DATE` is converted to UTC. Dates of kind `Utc` and `Unspecified` are written as
  before. Migration: give a CDM's dates in UTC, with any kind but `Local` for a UTC clock reading; give an OPM or OMM
  epoch outside `TIME_SYSTEM = UTC` as its clock reading in that time system, of kind `Utc` or `Unspecified`.
- **Breaking: the exported CDM names its method `FOSTER-1992`** ([#618](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/618), Fixed above). `EncounterCase.ToCdm` writes
  `COLLISION_PROBABILITY_METHOD = FOSTER-1992` where it wrote `FOSTER-2D`, and throws `InvalidOperationException` for an
  encounter flagged `SingleCovarianceMaximumPcUsed`, where a case built by hand with both covariances was written
  `FOSTER-2D-MAX-PC`, or with the method `CdmExportOptions.CollisionProbabilityMethod` named. Migration: a consumer that
  matched `FOSTER-2D` matches `FOSTER-1992`; a caller that sets `CdmExportOptions.CollisionProbabilityMethod` keeps its
  method, except for an encounter flagged `SingleCovarianceMaximumPcUsed`, which is refused whatever the option says
  (that maximum is not the Pc of two covariances; decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18): such an encounter is no longer exported.
- **The OPM, OMM and CDM writers write the shortest round-trip form of each value** ([#728](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/728), Fixed above). The text
  of the written messages changes: the OPM and OMM write the digits they dropped (0.00012345678901234567 where
  0.00012345678901 was written), the CDM drops the digits `G17` added beyond the shortest exact form
  (0.1 where 0.10000000000000001 was written). A value read from an OPM or OMM the library writes is the value given,
  bit for bit; one read from a CDM is unchanged.
- **Breaking: the CCSDS readers refuse a date outside the two forms of the standard** ([#619](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/619), Fixed above;
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-17). `Cdm`, `Opm` and `Omm` `Load*`/`ReadFrom*` and their readers throw `CdmParseException`,
  `OpmParseException` or `OmmParseException` for a date field (`TCA`, `CREATION_DATE`, `EPOCH`, `MAN_EPOCH_IGNITION`, the
  screening and observation dates) that is not `yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss[.d…][Z|±hh:mm]` or `yyyy-dddThh:mm:ss[.d…][Z|±hh:mm]`
  with every leading zero, where `DateTime.TryParse` read it. Migration: correct the producer; a date written to the
  standard reads bit for bit as before.
- **Breaking: the CDM reader refuses a `lengthTypeUO` length in units other than m** ([#619](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/619); decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-17). `MISS_DISTANCE`, `RELATIVE_POSITION_R/T/N` and `SCREEN_VOLUME_X/Y/Z` with `units="km"` (or any
  value but `m`, which `lengthUnits` enumerates alone) throw `CdmParseException` naming the keyword and the units, where
  `km` was converted. Migration: write the length in m, as the schema and CCSDS 508.0-B-1 table 3-2 require; a length
  without `units` is still read in m (#613).
- **Breaking: `OpmStateVector` and `CovarianceMatrix` refuse a value that overflows in SI units** ([#729](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/729), Fixed
  above). `new OpmStateVector(...)` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` naming `x` ... `zDot` for a component whose
  product by 1000 is not finite (above about 1.8e305 km or km/s), and `new CovarianceMatrix(...)`, `FromFullMatrix` and
  `FromMatrix` naming `cxX` ... `czDotZDot` for a term whose product by 1e6 is not (above about 1.8e302), where they built
  it and the conversions gave ±Infinity; the OPM and OMM readers throw their parse exception naming the keyword. Values of
  a `StateVector` (`FromStateVector`, `FromMatrixWithUnitConversion`) always convert back. Migration: none for a physical
  state; such a value carries no orbit.
- **Breaking: `Omm.ToTle` refuses a `MEAN_MOTION` its TLE field cannot hold** ([#729](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/729), Fixed above). A mean
  motion above the 99.99999999 rev/day of the 11-character field throws `InvalidOperationException` naming `MEAN_MOTION`
  and its value, as a `NORAD_CAT_ID` or a `REV_AT_EPOCH` the TLE cannot represent, where `TLE`'s constructor threw its
  line-length `ArgumentException` and, above about 2.86e307 rev/day, a TLE was returned with the text `Infinity`.
  Migration: catch `InvalidOperationException` instead of `ArgumentException`; such an object has no TLE form.
- **Breaking: `CdmCovarianceMatrix.StateCovarianceRtn` refuses a matrix that is not 6×6** ([#730](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/730), Fixed above).
  An object initializer or a `with` expression with another size or `default(Matrix)` throws `ArgumentException` naming
  `StateCovarianceRtn`, where it built and the writer failed. `Cdm.Validate` no longer checks the size, which no record
  can hold. Migration: give the 6×6 RTN covariance (`FromRtnCovariance` already required it).
- **Breaking: a negative revolution number names `revolutionNumberAtEpoch`** ([#734](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/734), Fixed above). The
  `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` of `new TleParameters(...)` and the four `CreateWith*` factories has the `ParamName`
  `revolutionNumberAtEpoch`, where it was `revNumber`. Migration: a caller that tests `ParamName` compares with
  `revolutionNumberAtEpoch` (`nameof` of the parameter).
- **Breaking: `Omm.ToTle` reads `OBJECT_ID = UNKNOWN` as no designator** ([#604](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/604), Fixed above; decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-18). An OMM whose `OBJECT_ID` is `UNKNOWN` (trimmed, in any letter case) gives a TLE with blank
  columns 10-17, where `UNKNOWN ` (or `unknown `, as given) was written there (measured on f70ee32); `TLE.ToOmm` writes
  `UNKNOWN` for a TLE without a designator, where it threw, and `TLE.Create` writes blank columns for a null or blank
  `cosparId`, where it threw `ArgumentException`, and `OrbitalParameters.ToTLE` for a null or blank
  `Configuration.CosparId`, where it threw `InvalidOperationException` ("TLE conversion using Equinoctial elements
  failed"). Migration: a consumer that read `UNKNOWN` in the designator columns reads blanks; a caller that passed a
  placeholder designator to `TLE.Create` or `Configuration` (`00000A`) can pass null.
- **Breaking: the OPM writers write the CCSDS name of `Frame.ICRF`** ([#339](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/339), Fixed above; decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-18). `Opm.CreateFromStateVector` and `Spacecraft.ToOpm` write `REF_FRAME = ICRF` for a state in `Frame.ICRF`,
  and `ToOpm` `MAN_REF_FRAME = ICRF` for its impulses, where they wrote `J2000`; every other frame keeps its name, and
  `ImpulseManeuver.ToOpmManeuverParameters` still writes the name it is given. `Opm.ToStateVector` reads the OPM back in
  `Frame.ICRF` as before. Migration: a consumer that matched `J2000` in an OPM the library writes matches `ICRF`; a test
  that compared `opm.Metadata.ReferenceFrame` with `Frame.ICRF.Name` compares it with `"ICRF"`.

- **Breaking: the states of Keplerian elements with 0.5 ≤ e ≤ 2 move by rounding** ([#472](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/472), Fixed above).
  p = (a (1 − e))(1 + e) and, for 0.5 ≤ e ≤ 1.2, the half-angle forms of 1 + e cos ν and e + cos ν move
  `ToStateVector()`, `ToEquinoctial().P`, and every path through them (`ToStateVector(Time)`, `AtEpoch`, the first state
  of a propagation from elements, `ToTLE`'s fit, the conversions of a `StateVector` with e in the band, whose a comes
  from its energy) by a few 1e-16 relative in 40 to 100 % of the cases, by up to 8.1e-11 near e = 1; below e = 0.5 and
  above e = 2 every result is unchanged, bit for bit. The equatorial hyperbola of
  `EquinoctialElementsSingularityTests.AtAnotherEpoch_MatchesTheTwoBodyReference` (e = 1.5) moves from 9.4e-17 to
  3.6e-16 in velocity on the three platforms, another draw of one rounding of p (its bound 7.2e-16), and that of
  `AtATrueAnomaly_MatchesTheReference` from 1.2e-16 and 1.7e-16 to 3.2e-16 and 1.2e-16 on macOS arm64 (1.8e-16 and
  3.9e-17 on Linux x64 and Windows x64; its bounds 6.4e-16 and 2.4e-16, CI run 44395076184). The initial state of the
  Molniya case R5 (e = 0.74) moves by one ulp per position component, so `Data/GmatReference/cases.json` is recaptured
  (G4 starts from it; its GMAT outputs pass unchanged, regenerated by `gmat-reference.yml`), and the universal Kepler
  solver of the reference `KeplerianStm` stops at its rounding floor, where a perturbed R5 state oscillated above its
  1e-15 stop. No migration: a caller that compared such states bit for bit with an earlier version compares them within
  a few ulps.

- **Breaking: the anomalies with 0.5 ≤ e ≤ 2 move by rounding** ([#484](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/484), Fixed above). E and ν from M
  (`EccentricAnomaly()`, `TrueAnomaly()`, `AtEpoch`, `ToStateVector(Time)`, the start of a propagation from elements,
  `Spacecraft.GetGeometricStateRelativeTo` before a propagation), and M from E (`StateVector.MeanAnomaly()`, so
  `ToKeplerianElements()` of a state, `MeanAnomaly(ν)`, `ToStateVector(ν)`, `EquinoctialElements.MeanAnomaly()`,
  `TimeToRadius`, `EpochAtMeanAnomaly`) move by an ulp or so for these eccentricities, by up to 9.3e5 ulp near the
  periapsis at e → 1. Below e = 0.5 and above e = 2 nothing moves. No migration.

- **Breaking: an open orbit has no apoapsis** ([#737](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/737), Fixed above). `ApogeeVector()` and `ApogeeVelocity()`
  of a parabola or a hyperbola (a semi-major axis not finite and above 0, the test of `Period()`, #663) throw
  `InvalidOperationException` naming e and a, where they returned a point of the other branch of a hyperbola (and its
  speed), or ±Infinity and 0 for a parabola; the `ApogeeHeightManeuver` built from such a target orbit throws
  `ArgumentException` (`targetOrbit`). An ellipse of the band, of a finite a above 0, keeps its apoapsis. The impulses
  that read the apoapsis of the current state (`PerigeeHeightManeuver`, `CombinedManeuver`) fire at an apoapsis, which an
  open orbit never reaches. Migration: test `IsElliptical()` (or a finite `SemiMajorAxis()` above 0) before reading the
  apoapsis; give an ellipse as the target orbit of an apogee maneuver.
- **Breaking: `KeplerianElements` refuses a semi-major axis of the wrong sign** ([#738](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/738), Fixed above). Outside
  the band |e − 1| < 1e-6 the constructor throws `ArgumentException` (`semiMajorAxis`, its message naming a and e) when
  a (1 − e) ≤ 0, a = 0 included, where it built elements whose state had a NaN velocity. The elements the library builds
  (from states, equinoctial elements, SPICE's `oscltx`, the maneuvers, the TLE fit) have the sign of their conic.
  Migration: give a hyperbola its negative semi-major axis, a = −μ/(2ξ) (`KeplerianElementsTests.IsHyperbolic` gave
  a = 20 000 m with e = 1.1). Such elements used to reach the `CONICS` check of the three
  `SpiceAPI.ConvertConicElementsToStateVector` overloads (#711, `ArgumentException` naming `keplerianElements`); they now
  throw at their construction (`semiMajorAxis`), and that check is left with the elements it still sees, mean elements of
  e ≥ 1 from `FromOMM` and an a (1 − e) that overflows (`SpiceApiTest.ConvertConicElementsToStateVector_OfAPeriapsisNotFiniteAndAboveZero_ThrowsArgumentException`).

- **Breaking: the motion of the near-parabolic band is the conic's** ([#753](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/753), Fixed above). Within 1e-6 of
  e = 1 but at e = 1 exactly, `AtEpoch`, `ToStateVector(Time)`, `ToKeplerianElements(Time)`, `EpochAtMeanAnomaly`,
  `TimeToRadius`, `TimeToSphereOfInfluence` and the start of a propagation from such elements move by up to the former
  model error (0.16 m after 600 s at the band's edges, 3.1 km after a day); the elements at the new epoch carry the true
  anomaly of the motion (`TrueAnomaly()` returns it). `IsParabolic()`, the anomalies of the band (Barker's), its
  geometry and `MeanMotion()` are unchanged; the motion is no longer a constant rate of the mean anomaly there. No
  migration.

- **Breaking: `MemoryDataProvider.AddStateOrientationToICRF` refuses the frames the provider defines** ([#744](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/744);
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18). An orientation added under ICRF (J2000) or GCRF, the identity of the provider (its
  states are ICRF, #559; GCRF shares its axes, #543), or under TEME, CIRS or TIRS, the managed frames (#656), by name in
  any case, throws `ArgumentException` naming `frame` and stores nothing. Before, an orientation stored under ICRF or GCRF
  was returned by `FrameTransformationToICRF` while `GetEphemeris` took the identity: 90° about z stored under ICRF read
  back 1.5708 rad from the identity, and the stored state (1e11, 0, 0) m came back unrotated (measured on f70ee32);
  one stored under TEME, CIRS or TIRS was never read
  (`MemoryDataProviderFrameTests.AddStateOrientation_UnderAFrameTheProviderDefines_Throws`, 10 names,
  `_UnderTheLibrarysDefinedFrames_Throws`, red on f70ee32; the three `ConfigurationTest` tests of stored orientations
  now store under a frame of their own). ECLIPJ2000 and any other frame still take stored orientations, which come
  first. Migration: none for a read, which already took the definition of these frames in `GetEphemeris`; drop the
  call, or store the orientation under a frame of its own name.
- **Breaking: `new Matrix(double[,])` copies its array** ([#745](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/745);
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18). The constructor kept the caller's array as its own, so a write to the array
  afterwards changed the matrix and its hash code: `a[0, 0] = 5` after `new Matrix(a)` gave `Get(0, 0)` 5 (measured on
  f70ee32), and a matrix used as a key was lost. It now copies the array, as `Matrix(rows, columns, double[])` and
  `ToArray()` did, so the terms of a matrix change only through its own `Set` (#722 kept `Matrix` mutable by `Set`); a
  null array throws `ArgumentNullException`, where it threw `NullReferenceException`. The library's own results built in a
  fresh array (the inverse, the Jacobian, `CovarianceMatrix.ToMatrix`, `ToMatrixWithUnitConversion`, a site frame) wrap
  it without the copy, through the internal `Matrix.Wrap`, so their cost is unchanged; results are unchanged, bit for bit
  (`MatirxTests.Constructor_FromArray_CopiesTheArray`, red on f70ee32; `Results_ShareNoArrayWithTheirInputs` guards the
  product, the inverse, the copy, both Jacobian overloads and both covariance matrices: a write to a result reaches
  neither its source nor the next result).
  Migration: a caller that wrote the array to change the matrix calls `Set`, or builds the matrix again.
- **Breaking: a propagator refuses a spacecraft whose initial orbit changed** ([#783](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/783), lot L5a, R08 of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668),
  decision 37, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): `PropagatorBase.Propagate` (`CentralBodyPropagator`, both
  constructors, and a subclass) and `TLEPropagator.Propagate` throw `InvalidOperationException`, with the other checks of
  the run and before the token, so before anything changes, once the spacecraft holds other `InitialOrbitalParameters`
  than those the propagator was built from, compared by reference: an orbit replaced by an equal but distinct object
  throws too, the same object set again does not. Before, a reused `CentralBodyPropagator` ran from the orbit of its
  construction while the spacecraft reported another (6 930 000 m against a semi-major axis of 7 500 000 m in the
  probes of R08), and a `TLEPropagator` took its first sample from the TLE of its construction and the others from the
  spacecraft's orbit (a 668 860 m jump between samples 0 and 1). The guard covers the orbit only: the maneuver chain,
  the tanks and the coefficients are read at each run. `Spacecraft.Propagate`, `Scenario.Simulate`, `BatchPropagator`
  and `MonteCarloPropagator` build a propagator per call and are not concerned (`RunIndependenceTests`: both integrators,
  both constructors, ICRF, ECLIPJ2000, SSB mode, a TLE). Migration: build a new propagator after
  `SetInitialOrbitalParameters`.
- **Breaking: a `TLEPropagator` run re-arms the spacecraft and replaces its stored states** ([#803](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/803) (a), lot L5a,
  R08 of #668, decision 38, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): a run computes every sample and acceleration, then, in one block,
  re-arms the spacecraft as a numerical propagation does (stored states, attitude record and last solution dropped,
  `ExecutedManeuvers` cleared, tanks refuelled) and stores its samples alone, in one arc; a stop or an SGP4 failure
  changes nothing, so decision 19 of lot L4 is the rule. Before, a run added its samples to the stored states (two runs
  of one hour at 60 s gave one arc of 122 states, read across the gap between them) and kept the attitude record, the
  solution and the executed maneuvers of an earlier numerical run beside SGP4 states. After a run the spacecraft is not
  `IsPropagated` and reads SGP4 outside the samples, as a spacecraft only sampled did before. The unused orientations
  the propagator kept (an internal dictionary keyed by label) are gone. Migration: none for a single run; to keep the
  states of several windows, sample one window that holds them.
- **Breaking: `TLEPropagator` refuses a spacecraft with a maneuver plan** (lot L5a, R08 of #668, decision 40, decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): its constructor throws `ArgumentException` (`spacecraft`), and `Propagate`
  `InvalidOperationException` for a plan set after construction, before anything changes; before, the plan was ignored
  silently (measured in the gap analysis: an apogee raise over 3 h executed nothing, the fuel unchanged), and a plan on
  another spacecraft's tank was accepted. Migration: clear the plan (`SetManeuvers()`) or propagate the
  spacecraft numerically.
- **Breaking: `MonteCarloPropagator` refuses a template with a maneuver plan** (lot L5a, R08 of #668, decision 41,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): both `Propagate` overloads throw `ArgumentException` (`config`) before anything is
  sampled. Its runs propagate spacecraft built from the template's orbit, dry mass, area and coefficients, so a plan
  was dropped silently (1.0786e7 m from the template's own run after 3 h in the gap analysis), while the docs listed the
  campaign among the paths that run the chain (corrected). The fuel, payloads, axes, hard-body radius and COSPAR id the
  runs also drop are an issue of their own, fixed after lot L5. Migration: clear the plan of the template (`SetManeuvers()`).
- **Breaking: `Spacecraft.AddPropagatedStates` takes one window per call, and a read in the gap between two windows throws**
  ([#792](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/792), lot L5a, R08 of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668),
  decisions 42 and 83 to 87, and 89 to 91, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): a call whose states span a hull, closed, that meets no
  stored arc (touching counts as meeting) opens a new arc, inserted in time order; otherwise its states join the arcs
  the hull meets, merged where a gap separates them (a call over the gap between two windows joins them; arcs that touch
  at an impulse stay apart), each state the arc of its epoch among them, as before. A gap inside the states of one call
  is not detected. `GetGeometricStateRelativeTo`, the short-circuit of `GetEphemeris` and every read through them throw
  `InvalidOperationException` in a gap between two windows, as outside the stored states (#527), the light time of a
  corrected read allowed outside each arc (an epoch inside an arc is read by that arc, as before, bit for bit; a
  corrected epoch in a gap within the light time of two arcs is read by the nearer, the later one on a tie, decision
  91), and the window arguments of the field-of-view search and of the `ILocalizable` overloads of the
  conjunction analysis throw `ArgumentException` when they meet a gap, as when they leave the states; an arc of one
  state (a call of one state apart from every arc) is read at its exact epoch only, and `WriteEphemeris` keeps refusing
  it with `ArgumentException`. So is a spacecraft that stores one state only (decision 89): its read goes through the
  arcs, at its exact epoch only, any other read throwing as in a gap (`ToOpm` at another epoch included), its window
  of zero length refusing any wider window argument, where the two-body orbit of its initial orbital parameters
  answered before at every epoch, its own one included (1.408e7 m off the stored state in the probe of the review); a
  spacecraft that stores none keeps the two-body orbit. Before, every state joined the arc of its epoch, so the windows of several calls made one
  arc, read across the gaps without an error: 9.28e9 m off the two-body orbit 1 h 56 min into a gap of 4 h between two
  windows of one hour at 60 s (`AddedStatesGapTests`, with the reads of each window, to the bit those of a spacecraft
  holding it alone, and within 3.412e-4 m of the two-body orbit on Linux x64, Windows and macOS arm64 alike, the CI of
  #808), and a TLE spacecraft sampled by
  `TLEPropagator` and given later states interpolated across the gap where it now reads SGP4. A call within or touching
  the stored states, a propagation and a `TLEPropagator` run are unchanged, bit for bit, as is every read inside the
  stored states, and a corrected read past the end of a propagation that ends with an impulse, within the light time
  after the end, still reads the last arc of one state that impulse opens (#575), touching the arc before it at the
  impulse: the state after the impulse, as before (decision 90; decisions 85 and 87 apply to arcs separated by a
  gap), and `WriteEphemeris` leaves that arc out, a window added after it following a gap or not, its SPK ending that
  run of arcs with the arc before the impulse (8436db52 wrote the file, the added window joined to that arc across the
  gap; before the second review of lot L5a an added window made it throw "Arc 1 holds fewer than two states").
  Migration: add each window in its own call, and the states between two windows
  in one call that spans them to join them; one state per call opens an arc per state, read at its epoch only; a
  spacecraft given one state to stand for an orbit is given no state, its initial orbital parameters then read in
  two-body motion, or a window of states.

- **Breaking: the maneuver plan is set by `Spacecraft.SetManeuvers`, which claims its maneuvers** (lot L5a, R08 of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668),
  decisions 45 to 47, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): `Maneuver.NextManeuver` keeps its public getter and its setter
  is internal (protected before, so a subclass could relink a chain), `Spacecraft.StandbyManeuver`, the run's own state,
  is internal, and a maneuver is in one plan at a time. The checks that ran when the propagator was built now run at
  `SetManeuvers` too, where the call receives the maneuver, as `ArgumentException` (`maneuvers`): an engine that is not
  one of the spacecraft's `Engines`, added with `AddEngine` and compared by reference (decision 92: an engine built on
  the spacecraft's tank and never added ran before, the tank alone checked; a twin of an added engine, equal by value,
  is another engine), an engine whose tank is not the spacecraft's (`InvalidOperationException` when the propagator
  was built and at the run before, as still after the plan) and a target orbit in another frame than the one the
  spacecraft is propagated in (a TEME target on a TLE spacecraft, which the constructor of the maneuver accepts,
  included). The frame check of the propagator constructor stays as it was: a propagator built after the initial orbit's
  frame changed, so that a target set by `SetManeuvers` no longer shares it, throws `ArgumentException` naming
  `spacecraft`, the call receiving the faulty object; only `Propagate` re-checks the frames, with
  `InvalidOperationException` (decision 94 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23). The cycle check stays as a guard
  of the walks of the chain. No result moves. Migration:
  `spacecraft.SetManeuvers(m1, m2, m3)` for `spacecraft.SetStandbyManeuver(m1); m1.SetNextManeuver(m2).SetNextManeuver(m3)`,
  `SetManeuvers()` for `SetStandbyManeuver(null)`, `spacecraft.Maneuvers[0]` for `InitialManeuver`; for
  `StandbyManeuver` read after a run, the first maneuver of the plan the run did not execute, `spacecraft.Maneuvers[n]` with
  n = `spacecraft.ExecutedManeuvers.Count` when n is below `spacecraft.Maneuvers.Count`, none otherwise (a run executes
  the plan in its order); add the tanks and the engines (`AddEngine`, the engine instance the maneuver is built on) and
  set the initial orbit before the plan; a maneuver for two spacecraft is two maneuvers.
- **Breaking: the `Maneuver` hierarchy is closed** (lot L5a, R08 of #668, decisions 48 and 49, decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-23): `Maneuver`'s constructor is `private protected`, so a user maneuver derives from `ImpulseManeuver` or
  `Attitude`, the two kinds the propagation knows (a direct subclass of `Maneuver` compiled before, and could not be
  run); `TryExecute` is internal, and the protected `Execute(StateVector)` is on `ImpulseManeuver`, documented pure, its
  result the preview of `ComputeDeltaV` (it was on `Maneuver`, and `Attitude` returned a zero delta-V); `Engine.Ignite`
  is internal; the concrete maneuvers stay unsealed. Decision 48 is split (decision 93 of #668, decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-23): `Engine` moves to `ImpulseManeuver` and a protected `GetBodyAxis(BodyAxis)` replaces `GetBodyFront` in
  lot L5b, with R13 and `BodyAxis` (decision 69), both below.
  Migration: a preview of
  an impulse is `ComputeDeltaV(state)`, of an attitude `ComputeStateOrientation(state)`, the fuel of a delta-V
  `Tsiolkovski.DeltaM(isp, mass, deltaV)`; a user maneuver keeps its `Execute` override on an `ImpulseManeuver`.
- **Breaking: `ImpulseManeuver.ComputeEventValue` is pure** (lot L5a, decision 50 of #668, [#802](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/802)): it locks no node and
  writes no intersection; the node of a `PlaneAlignmentManeuver` is locked by the detector of a run, at its first
  evaluation, by the rule of before (the detector internal since decision 88). A run is bit for bit that of
  before. Migration: a caller that read `IsAscendingNode` or `EventCrossingDirection` after a call of
  `ComputeEventValue` reads them after the run that executed the maneuver, which writes the last run's values
  (decision 52).
- **Breaking: `ManeuverEventDetector` is internal** (lot L5a, R08 of #668, decision 88, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23,
  [#802](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/802)): the propagation builds its detectors from the maneuver plan and takes no user detector, and its
  public `HandleEvent` executed a maneuver outside a run (fuel burned, `DeltaV` and the windows rewritten, the probe of
  the first review of L5a: 105.5 kg of fuel taken after a run). `IEventDetector`, `EventResult`, `EventAction` and
  `CrossingDirection` stay public, as they are. A custom `IIntegrator` given to the propagator still receives the
  detectors as `IEventDetector` within the run, which decision 88 alone left open (the second review of L5a: a detector
  kept past the run burned 472 kg of fuel and rewrote `DeltaV`), so a detector serves the run that built it only
  (decision 95 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-24): the run disarms every detector it built when it ends,
  completed, stopped by its token or thrown, a run nested in a run of the same propagator on its thread included (the
  third review of L5a: the detectors the outer run built after the nested run stayed armed past it), and its `Evaluate` and `HandleEvent` then throw
  `InvalidOperationException` naming the maneuver, changing nothing (no fuel, `DeltaV`, window or node of a
  `PlaneAlignmentManeuver`; `IntegratorEventTests.ADetectorKeptPast*`, `ADetectorKeptFromAnEarlierRun_*`,
  `ADetectorBuiltAfterANestedRun_*`, a bare `IIntegrator` and an `Integrator`
  subclass over both integrators). This holds for the calls that start after the end: a call already in progress when
  the run ends completes (decision 98 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-24), which only an integrator that keeps
  a detector past its `IntegrateSegment` call, against the documented contract, meets; no lock is added. A detector also executes its impulse once at most for calls that do not overlap (decision 97 of #668, decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-24; the third review of L5a: a custom `IIntegrator` that kept the detector of an impulse executed
  it a second time during the run, 6.74 kg burned, `DeltaV` rewritten, nothing in `ExecutedManeuvers`): when its
  `HandleEvent` has executed the impulse it disarms itself, and a later `HandleEvent` or `Evaluate` within the run
  throws `InvalidOperationException` saying that it has already executed its impulse (once the run has ended, the
  message of a finished run is given first), changing nothing, while one that skipped the occurrence (`Continue`, the
  preconditions not met) stays armed; it disarms itself as the execution starts, so a `HandleEvent` whose execution
  throws disarms it too (the fourth review of L5a: an execution that threw after the fuel burned, a burn past the range
  of a `TimeSpan`, left it armed, and each later call burned again, three burns in one run); the propagation never
  calls a detector after its execution, so a run whose integrator calls `HandleEvent` on the event it returns throws
  from the propagation's own call rather than burning twice, and one whose integrator executes an event and returns
  none breaks the contract and returns incomplete, stopped at that event
  (`IntegratorEventTests.ADetectorCalledAfterItsImpulse_*`, `AnIntegratorThatHandlesItsEvent_*`,
  `ADetectorThatSkipped*`, `ADetectorWhoseExecutionThrows*`). No result moves. Migration: the propagation executes the plan
  (`Spacecraft.SetManeuvers`, then a propagation); the previews of a maneuver are `ImpulseManeuver.ComputeDeltaV` and
  `ComputeEventValue`, pure; a custom `IIntegrator` uses the detectors it receives within its call of
  `IntegrateSegment` only.
- **Breaking: `PhasingManeuver` takes no hold** (lot L5a, decision 51 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23,
  [#784](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/784)): its constructors are `PhasingManeuver(minimumEpoch, targetOrbit, revolutionNumber, engine)` and
  `PhasingManeuver(maneuverCenter, minimumEpoch, trueLongitude, revolutionNumber, engine)`; the hold, 0.9 N T₂, is set
  by the run that executes the burn and cleared to 0 by the re-arm of the next run (before, the hold given was replaced
  at the burn, so it was dead input, and the computed hold was left for good). No result moves. Migration: drop the
  hold argument.
- **Breaking: `PlaneAlignmentManeuver.RelativeInclination`, `ApsidalAlignmentManeuver.IntersectsP` and `IntersectsQ`
  are internal** (lot L5a, decision 51 of #668): side results of the execution that nothing read, which the re-arm
  left. Migration: none in the library, as they were run state; the relative inclination is the angle between the two
  orbits' normals (`SpecificAngularMomentum()` of the state and of the target orbit), and the intersection an apsidal
  alignment burnt at (P or Q) is the position of its burn, the solution's state at the epoch of its record
  (`PropagationSolution.GetStateVector(record.Epoch).Position`, `record` in `PropagationSolution.Maneuvers`), the
  intersection of the two orbits nearest the spacecraft in true anomaly where its g-function crosses.
- **The values a run writes on a maneuver are the last run's** (lot L5a, decision 52 of #668, decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-23): `DeltaV`, `FuelBurned`, `ThrustWindow`, `ManeuverWindow`, `MinimumEpoch`, the node of a
  `PlaneAlignmentManeuver` and the hold of a `PhasingManeuver` hold the values of the last run that executed the
  maneuver, cleared by the re-arm of the next run, documented in [Impulse Maneuvers](../reference/impulse-maneuvers.md#maneuver-plan).
- **Breaking: `PropagationSolution.InterpolateAt` is internal** (lot L5a, R09 of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decision 54, decided by S.
  Guillet, 2026-11-23; choice 8 of the re-baseline): the one public reader of a solution is `GetStateVector`, which
  returns a `StateVector` about `Observer` in `Frame` and throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` outside `Window`, where
  `InterpolateAt` returned an unnamed tuple and clamped to the first or last state. Inside the window the state is that
  of `InterpolateAt`, bit for bit; in covariance mode `GetStateVector` also computes the covariance, about 4 times the
  cost of the state alone. The library's readers that rely on the clamp (the outputs, the attitude samples, the
  conjunction analysis) keep the internal method; the conformance runner reads `GetStateVector`, its report bit for
  bit that of before (201 of 201 cases, every delta equal). Migration:
  `var s = solution.GetStateVector(epoch); var (position, velocity) = (s.Position, s.Velocity);` for
  `var (position, velocity) = solution.InterpolateAt(epoch);`, with an epoch inside `solution.Window`.
- **Breaking: a `PropagationSegment` cannot be changed from outside the library** (lot L5a, decision 55 of #668, option
  D, [#796](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/796)): its constructors are `PropagationSegment(Time baseEpoch)` and `PropagationSegment(Time baseEpoch,
  IEnumerable<AcceptedStep> steps)`, which copies the steps; `AddStep`, the constructor with a step count,
  `InterpolateAt(double)` and `HermiteInterpolate` are internal, and `Steps` is a read-only view (a cast to
  `List<AcceptedStep>` fails, and its `IList` indexer and `Add` throw `NotSupportedException`). `IIntegrator` stays an
  extension point. Migration: an integrator implemented outside the library collects its `AcceptedStep` values and
  returns `new PropagationSegment(baseEpoch, steps)` in its `IntegrationResult`; the state of a solution between steps
  is `GetStateVector`.
- **Breaking: the constructor and mutators of `PropagationSolution` are internal** (lot L5a, R09 of #668, decision 55
  and section A of the re-baseline, choice 5): `new PropagationSolution()`, `AddSegment` and `SetOutputStates`;
  `Segments` and `StateVectors` are read-only views (`StateVectors` was the array itself), and so is the new
  `Maneuvers`. `IPropagator` stays public, documented as implemented by the library and by `PropagatorBase` subclasses,
  which build their own solution. Migration: an `IPropagator` implemented outside the library subclasses
  `PropagatorBase`, or returns the solution of a library propagator it delegates to; a solution built by hand (a straight
  line for the conjunction analysis) has no public equivalent in 11.0.0.
- **Breaking: `Integrator.UpdateStateVector` is internal** (lot L5a, decision 55 of #668, [#796](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/796)): it was
  `protected internal static` on a class a caller can derive from, the one way outside the library to rewrite a
  `StateVector` in place, a published solution's or the stored states included. Migration: none in the library's
  integrators; a subclass builds new states.
- **Breaking: `PropagationSolution.CovariancePropagation` is `CovariancePropagationOptions.None` when the propagation
  propagated neither Φ nor the covariance** (lot L5a, R09 of #668, decision 56, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23), on
  every path, a `TLEPropagator` solution included; it was null, while `Options.CovariancePropagation` was `None`. A
  caller's `solution.CovariancePropagation == null` still compiles but is now always false, which the compiler does not
  catch. Migration: test `solution.CovariancePropagation.Mode == CovariancePropagationMode.None`.
- **Breaking: `Spacecraft.ExecutedManeuvers` is an `IReadOnlyList<Maneuver>`, a new list at each run** (lot L5a, R09 of
  #668, decision 58, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): an `IReadOnlyCollection` before, a live set that the next run
  emptied. The re-arm of a run swaps in an empty list, and each maneuver the run executes swaps in a new list that adds
  it, in execution order, so a list once read never changes (a read-only view; a cast cannot write it): a list held
  from an earlier run keeps its members, a reader on another thread during a run sees the maneuvers executed so far,
  and a stopped run leaves those executed up to the stop (C2 of lot L4). It holds the definitions, whose values are those of their last run: the stable values of a run are its
  records, `PropagationSolution.Maneuvers`. Until the fix of
  [#794](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/794) (decision 44, after lot L5), a
  stopped run's list also holds an attitude chained before the stop whose activation the run never reached. Migration:
  a binary break only (recompile); index the list for the order of execution.
- **Breaking: `SpacecraftSummary` is sealed, built from the records of the run** (lot L5a, R09 of #668, decision 59,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): its constructor is internal (`Scenario.Simulate` builds it from the solution of each
  spacecraft), `Maneuvers` is an `IReadOnlyList<ExecutedManeuver>` (the definitions, an `IEnumerable<Maneuver>`,
  before), and `FuelConsumption` and `ManeuverWindow` are the sum and the hull of the records, bit for bit those of
  before (the hull computed directly, with the tie-break of `Window.Merge`); its file is `SpacecraftSummary.cs`.
  `ScenarioSummary.SpacecraftSummaries` is an `IReadOnlyList<SpacecraftSummary>` in scenario order (an
  `IReadOnlyCollection` of a set before). Migration: `summary.Maneuvers[i].Definition` for the maneuver, and the record's
  own `DeltaV`, `FuelBurned` and windows for the values of the run; index `SpacecraftSummaries`.
- **Breaking: finite and in-range values for `Spacecraft`, `FuelTank`, `Engine` and `Payload`**
  ([#800](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/800), lot L5b, decision 75 of #668,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23, under **Fixed**): both `Spacecraft` constructors throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`
  naming the parameter for a `mass` not finite or negative (an `ArgumentException` naming no parameter from
  `CelestialItem` before), a `maxOperatingMass` not finite or below the mass, a `sectionalArea` not finite or not above
  0, a `dragCoefficient`, `solarRadiationCoefficient` or `hardBodyRadius` not finite or negative (the parameters named
  as renamed by lot L5b, decision 71); the kernel-backed constructor gains
  these checks, which run before it reads the kernels, as do the NAIF id and the clock (before, a spacecraft without an SPK
  threw `SpiceException` whatever its values). `FuelTank` checks its `capacity` first, finite and above 0, then its
  `initialQuantity`, finite, above 0 and at most the capacity; `Engine` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` naming `isp`
  or `fuelFlow`, not finite or not above 0, and `Payload` naming `mass` (both `ArgumentException` naming no parameter
  before, for 0 or less). Migration: pass finite values in range; a `catch (ArgumentException)` still catches the new
  exception, which derives from it; `Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>` on an engine's or a payload's value or a
  spacecraft's negative mass becomes `Assert.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>`.
- **Breaking: the propagated `Spacecraft` constructor takes the orbit fourth, the maximum operating mass and the clock
  optional** (lot L5b, R10, decisions 70 and 71 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-23): `Spacecraft(int naifId, string name, double mass, OrbitalParameters initialOrbitalParameters, double
  maxOperatingMass = double.MaxValue, Clock clock = null, double sectionalArea = 1.0, double dragCoefficient = 2.2,
  string cosparId = null, double solarRadiationCoefficient = 1.0, Vector3? bodyFront = null, Vector3? bodyRight = null,
  Vector3? bodyUp = null, double hardBodyRadius = 0.0)`, where it was `(naifId, name, mass, maximumOperatingMass, clock,
  initialOrbitalParameters, sectionalArea, dragCoeff, cosparId, solarRadiationCoeff, ...)` with a required clock (a null
  clock threw `ArgumentNullException`). The default clock is `new Clock(name + "_CLK", 65536)`, the resolution of the CK
  the library writes; the defaults give the results of the explicit values they stand for, bit for bit, and the default
  clock the SCLK of the explicit one byte for byte (`SpacecraftConstructionTests`). An old positional call no longer
  compiles: a `double` does not convert to `OrbitalParameters`. Migration: `new Spacecraft(id, name, mass, max, clock,
  orbit, ...)` becomes `new Spacecraft(id, name, mass, orbit, max, clock, ...)`, or `new Spacecraft(id, name, mass,
  orbit)` when the maximum was `double.MaxValue` and the clock `name + "_CLK"` at 65536 ticks per second.
- **Breaking: the parameters `maximumOperatingMass`, `dragCoeff` and `solarRadiationCoeff` of both `Spacecraft`
  constructors are named `maxOperatingMass`, `dragCoefficient` and `solarRadiationCoefficient`** (lot L5b, decision 71 of
  #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23, as the member each sets; `SolarRadiationCoeff` keeps its name until lot L9).
  The kernel-backed constructor keeps its positions and its default clock, `name + "_CLK"` at 256 ticks per second, so
  only a named argument breaks. Migration: rename the named arguments; `ArgumentOutOfRangeException.ParamName` gives the
  new names.
- **Breaking: `Spacecraft.MaximumOperatingMass` is renamed `MaxOperatingMass`** (lot L5b, decision 70 of #668, decided by
  S. Guillet, 2026-11-23), with no forwarder. The value stays informational: checked against the dry mass only, never
  against the fuel and the payloads (L5-37 of #668). Migration: read `MaxOperatingMass`.
- **Breaking: `Opm.ToSpacecraft(int naifId, double maxOperatingMass = double.MaxValue, Clock clock = null, ILocalizable
  observer = null)` raises no maximum** (lot L5b, decision 77 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): the maximum
  operating mass and the clock are optional with the defaults of the propagated constructor (the clock `OBJECT_NAME +
  "_CLK"` at 65536 ticks per second), and a `MASS` above `maxOperatingMass` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` naming
  `maxOperatingMass` from the constructor, where the maximum was raised to the mass without a word; a null clock threw
  `ArgumentNullException` before. The parameter `maximumOperatingMass` is named `maxOperatingMass`. Migration: pass a
  maximum at least the OPM's mass, or none; `maximumOperatingMass:` becomes `maxOperatingMass:`.
- **Breaking: one `Add*Instrument` per shape, which returns the instrument, the NAIF id and the model optional** (lot
  L5b, R10, decisions 72 to 74 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): `CircularInstrument
  AddCircularInstrument(string name, double fieldOfView, in Vector3 boresight, in Vector3 refVector, in Vector3
  orientation = default, int? naifId = null, string model = null)`, and `AddRectangularInstrument` and
  `AddEllipticalInstrument` with `crossAngle` after `fieldOfView`, where the three returned nothing and took `(int naifId,
  string name, string model, double fieldOfView, ...)`, the id, the model and the orientation required (an empty model
  threw `ArgumentException`). The default id is the smallest free NaifId × 1000 − n, n in [1, 999], that is an `int`
  (NAIF IDs Required Reading, "Instruments"), and writes the kernels of the same id given explicitly byte for byte
  (`InstrumentAdditionTests`); when none is left the call throws `InvalidOperationException`. The checks run before the
  instrument is built, in this order: a kernel-backed spacecraft requires `naifId` (`ArgumentNullException`, decision
  73: `gftfov` reads the instrument kernel loaded under it), a duplicate id throws `ArgumentException` naming `naifId`
  ("Instrument already added to spacecraft", naming no parameter, before), and a name of the invariant upper-cased form
  of another instrument's throws `ArgumentException` naming `name` (decision 74: "Cam" and "CAM" both assigned
  `FRAME_<SPACECRAFT>_CAM`, the later kernel winning, and wrote one file on a case-insensitive file system); the value
  checks stay in the constructor. An old positional call no longer compiles (an `int` does not convert to `string`); a
  call that names every argument keeps its meaning. Migration: `sc.AddCircularInstrument(id, name, model, fov, b, r, o)`
  becomes `sc.AddCircularInstrument(name, fov, b, r, o, naifId: id, model: model)`, or `sc.AddCircularInstrument(name,
  fov, b, r)` for the default id and orientation; read the instrument from the return value rather than
  `Instruments`; give two instruments of one spacecraft names that differ by more than their case.
- **Breaking: the constructor of `Instrument` is `private protected`** (lot L5b, decision 72 of #668 with the critic's gap 1
  of L5-32, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): the hierarchy is closed, and `Add*Instrument` builds every instrument under
  its checks. A subclass outside the library built an instrument that no id or name rule covered, that `Instruments` did
