  not list and so the kernel writers never wrote, and that `Equals` (by NAIF id) took for a library instrument of its id;
  the field-of-view search threw `InvalidOperationException` for such an instrument of a shape other than a circle, a
  case that no longer exists. Migration: build the instrument with the `Add*Instrument` of its shape.
- **Breaking: `FuelTank`, `Engine` and `Payload` take their model and serial number last and optional, a tank may
  start empty** (lot L5b, R10 and decision 76 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): `FuelTank(string name, double
  capacity, double initialQuantity, string model = null, string serialNumber = null)`, `Engine(string name, double isp,
  double fuelFlow, FuelTank fuelTank, string model = null, string serialNumber = null)` and `Payload(string name, double
  mass, string serialNumber = null)`, where they were `FuelTank(name, model, serialNumber, capacity, initialQuantity)`
  and `Engine(name, model, serialNumber, isp, fuelFlow, fuelTank)`, each string required (an empty one threw
  `ArgumentException`), and a payload's serial number required. A tank's `initialQuantity` may be 0, an empty tank whose
  first burn throws `InsufficientFuelException` (above 0 before); the model and the serial number reach no kernel. An
  old positional call no longer compiles (a `string` does not convert to `double`). The components built without a model
  or a serial number propagate as those built with them, bit for bit (`ComponentConstructionTests`). Migration: `new
  FuelTank(name, model, serial, capacity, quantity)` becomes `new FuelTank(name, capacity, quantity, model, serial)` or
  `new FuelTank(name, capacity, quantity)`, and `new Engine(name, model, serial, isp, flow, tank)` `new Engine(name, isp,
  flow, tank, model, serial)` or `new Engine(name, isp, flow, tank)`.
- **Breaking: `AddFuelTank`, `AddEngine` and `AddPayload` return their argument and refuse a second component of a name**
  (lot L5b, R10 and decision 76 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): `FuelTank AddFuelTank(FuelTank)`, `Engine
  AddEngine(Engine)` and `Payload AddPayload(Payload)`, which returned nothing (source compatible, a binary break), and
  a second tank, engine or payload of a name on a spacecraft, compared ordinally, throws `ArgumentException` naming the
  parameter; a tank or an engine of a name was accepted before when its model or serial number differed, and a payload
  of a name when its serial number or mass did. `AddFuelTank` checks the name before it attaches the tank, so a refused
  tank stays free for another spacecraft. The payload's rule has no file behind it (a payload name reaches no kernel):
  it is the rule of every component. The messages of `AddEngine`, `AddFuelTank` and of the run's engine check print a
  serial number only when one is given, and the run names an engine of the name of an added one where it named an
  engine equal by value. Migration: give each tank, engine and payload of a spacecraft its own name; `var tank =
  spacecraft.AddFuelTank(new FuelTank(...))`.
- **`Spacecraft.GetTotalISP()` and `GetTotalFuelFlow()` count every engine**
  ([#801](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/801) part 1, lot L5b, decision 60 of
  #668 with L5-20 as amended, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): they counted only the engines whose tank held fuel at
  the start of a run (an initial quantity above 0), and now count every engine of `Engines`, whatever its tank holds. A
  tank refuses a non-finite quantity since #800 (under **Fixed**), so every spacecraft that can be built gives the same
  values, bit for bit (the set of engines enumerated in the order of their addition, as before); the filter left out
  only the engine of a tank of NaN quantity. On a spacecraft that mixes empty and filled tanks the engines on the empty
  tanks count: engines of 300 s at 10 kg/s and 200 s at 30 kg/s give 225 s whatever the second tank holds, where the
  filter gave 300 s with that tank empty, so the fuel cost of an avoidance option (`ConjunctionAssessment`, from the
  specific impulse) rises by about a third in that case. Without an engine `GetTotalISP` stays NaN (0 / 0) and
  `GetTotalFuelFlow` 0. #801 part 2, the avoidance clone lighter than its dry mass, stays open, fixed after lot L5.
- **Breaking: an attitude points the instruments of the spacecraft propagated**
  ([#797](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/797), lot L5b, decision 66 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-23, under **Fixed**): an `InstrumentPointingToAttitude` or a `TriadAttitude` built on an instrument of another spacecraft ran,
  on the spacecraft's own engine, and pointed that instrument's boresight, whose orientation is in the frame of its own
  spacecraft (in the probe of the gap analysis of L5, 11 attitudes recorded and the spacecraft's own boresight 0.577 rad
  from the Moon); the TRIAD instrument forms kept no reference to their instruments. They keep them now, and
  `Spacecraft.SetManeuvers` throws `ArgumentException` (`maneuvers`) for an attitude that points an instrument whose
  `Spacecraft` is not the spacecraft, compared by reference, nothing changed, the propagator constructor and `Propagate`
  `InvalidOperationException` for a chain that holds one, beside the engine check (`ForeignInstrumentTests`, the
  pointing, the TRIAD of one instrument and of two, red before the change). An attitude on the spacecraft's own
  instruments runs as before, bit for bit (the body vectors of the TRIAD forms are those of before). Migration: build the
  attitude on an instrument of the spacecraft it is propagated with.
- **Breaking: a maneuver law reads the body axes of the spacecraft whose plan last held it, through the protected
  `GetBodyAxis(BodyAxis)`** (lot L5b, decisions 46, 48, 69 and 93 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-23): the protected `Maneuver.GetBodyFront()` is replaced by `protected Vector3 GetBodyAxis(BodyAxis axis)`, any
  of the six axes of the new `enum BodyAxis` (under **Added**), an undefined value throwing `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`
  (`axis`); it reads the instance axes of the spacecraft whose plan (`Spacecraft.SetManeuvers`) last held the maneuver,
  which a plan that releases it keeps, and the static axes (`Spacecraft.Front`, ...) before any plan, where
  `GetBodyFront()` and the TRIAD factories read the axes of the spacecraft of the engine's tank, the static ones while
  the tank was on no spacecraft. A run reads the axes it read before, bit for bit: the plan's spacecraft is the
  propagated one, whose engines the run checks (`BodyAxisTests`). A preview of an attitude in no plan (`ComputeStateOrientation`), or a factory's `PrimaryBodyVector` and `SecondaryBodyVector` read before
  its plan, takes the static axes where it took those of the engine's spacecraft: for a spacecraft of custom axes, set
  the plan first. Migration: `GetBodyAxis(BodyAxis.Front)` for `GetBodyFront()` in a user attitude; `spacecraft.SetManeuvers(attitude)`
  before a preview on that spacecraft's axes.
- **Breaking: `Engine` is on `ImpulseManeuver`, and an attitude takes no engine** (lot L5b, decisions 48 and 93 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-23): `Maneuver.Engine` moves to `ImpulseManeuver.Engine`, and the constructors of `Attitude`, `NadirAttitude`,
  `ZenithAttitude`, `ProgradeAttitude`, `RetrogradeAttitude`, `NormalAttitude`, `AntiNormalAttitude`,
  `InstrumentPointingToAttitude`, `TriadAttitude` and its factories `CreateLVLH` and `CreateProgradeWithSunTracking`
  lose their `Engine engine` parameter (an engine was required, null throwing `ArgumentNullException`). An attitude
  burns nothing: it orients the spacecraft whose plan holds it, whose axes it reads (`GetBodyAxis`, above), so a
  spacecraft without a tank or an engine runs a plan of attitudes, where a thrusterless satellite needed a tank and an
  engine for it. `SetManeuvers` and the run check the engine of an impulse only; the execution of an attitude no longer
  sets the next maneuver in standby from its engine's spacecraft (a branch the run never reached: the run advances the
  chain on its attitude timeline), and an impulse executed outside a plan moves no chain. A run with an attitude on the
  spacecraft's own engine is bit for bit that of before. Migration: drop the engine argument of an attitude
  (in the order of its parameters below, `new NadirAttitude(epoch, hold, earth)`); `((ImpulseManeuver)maneuver).Engine`
  for `maneuver.Engine`; a user `Attitude` calls `base(minEpoch, holdDuration, maneuverCenter)`.
- **Breaking: a maneuver given no engine or no centre takes those the run infers** (lot L5b, decisions 61, 63 and 64 of
  #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23, and decision 99, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-24): an impulse whose engine
  is null takes the only engine of the spacecraft (`Engines`, decision 92), and a maneuver whose centre is null the
  observer of the spacecraft's initial orbit when it is a celestial body other than a star, resolved from the values the
  maneuver was given when the propagator is built and at `Propagate`, writing nothing; where the centre cannot be
  inferred (SSB mode: a star or a barycentre), the library's `TriadAttitude` or `InstrumentPointingToAttitude` whose
  targets are all library `CelestialAttitudeTarget`s takes the central body of the run, and every other law (the
  impulses, the orbital-direction attitudes, a user `IAttitudeTarget` or subclass of `CelestialAttitudeTarget`, a user
  `Attitude` subclass, one of `TriadAttitude` or `InstrumentPointingToAttitude` included) requires `maneuverCenter`:
  the propagator constructor and `Propagate` throw `InvalidOperationException`, as for an impulse given no engine on a spacecraft of
  none or several ("pass engine:"). Before, a null engine threw `ArgumentNullException` in the constructor, a null centre
  was accepted by most constructors and threw `NullReferenceException` in the run, the `TriadAttitude` of
  `IAttitudeTarget` targets threw `ArgumentNullException` for it, and a user law about a centre it read received a
  heliocentric state silently in SSB mode. `ImpulseManeuver.Engine` and `ManeuverCenter` return the values given before
  a run and the values the last run used after it, written right after its re-arm, which restores the given ones
  (decision 63; a stopped run keeps the resolved ones, a cancelled token or an `Initialize` that throws changes neither);
  every check before the write and every preview (`ComputeDeltaV`, `ComputeStateOrientation`) read the given values,
  so a maneuver released after a run goes to another spacecraft, an engine added between two runs makes the second
  throw, and a preview of an inferred centre takes the state about its own observer before and after a run alike
  (`ManeuverInferenceTests`, both integrators). The explicit engine and centre give the run of before, bit for bit; a
  plan given its engine and centre and the same plan inferring them give the same run. Migration: none for a maneuver
  given its engine and centre; in SSB mode give `maneuverCenter` to an impulse and to an attitude other than a law of
  celestial targets only; on a spacecraft of several engines give `engine`.
- **Breaking: the impulses take their target first, then the optional `engine`, `minEpoch`, `holdDuration` and
  `maneuverCenter`** (lot L5b, D1 rule 8 and R13 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-23): `ApogeeHeightManeuver(apogeeRadius, engine = null, minEpoch = default, holdDuration = default,
  maneuverCenter = null)`, the same for `PerigeeHeightManeuver(perigeeRadius, …)` and
  `CombinedManeuver(perigeeRadius, inclination, …)`, `PhasingManeuver(trueLongitude, revolutionNumber, engine = null,
  minEpoch = default, maneuverCenter = null)`, and the target-orbit forms `(targetOrbit, engine = null, minEpoch =
  default, holdDuration = default)` of `ApogeeHeightManeuver`, `PerigeeHeightManeuver`, `PlaneAlignmentManeuver`,
  `ApsidalAlignmentManeuver` and `PhasingManeuver(targetOrbit, revolutionNumber, engine = null, minEpoch = default)`
  (no hold for a phasing, decision 51; no centre for a target orbit, whose observer is the centre), where they took
  `(maneuverCenter, minimumEpoch, maneuverHoldDuration, …, engine)` or `(minimumEpoch, maneuverHoldDuration,
  targetOrbit, engine)`, and `PhasingManeuver` `(minimumEpoch, targetOrbit, revolutionNumber, engine)` or
  `(maneuverCenter, minimumEpoch, trueLongitude, revolutionNumber, engine)`, each required; the protected constructors
  of `ImpulseManeuver` follow, `(engine = null, minEpoch = default, holdDuration = default, maneuverCenter = null)` and
  `(targetOrbit, engine = null, minEpoch = default, holdDuration = default)`. A null `engine` and `maneuverCenter` are inferred by the run (above), `minEpoch` defaults to
  default(Time), no minimum (D3), and `holdDuration` to zero, the negative hold refused as before under the name
  `holdDuration`. A target orbit whose observer is not a celestial item (a site) throws `ArgumentException`
  (`targetOrbit`), where it gave a maneuver of no centre. An old positional call no longer compiles in most forms (a
  `CelestialItem` or a `Time` first does not convert to a `double` or to `OrbitalParameters`); a call that binds the same
  types, `(Time, TimeSpan, OrbitalParameters, Engine)`, does not compile either. The runs of a maneuver built with the same
  values are bit for bit those of before (the conformance runner's maneuver cases, which give the centre and the engine,
  unchanged). Migration: `new ApogeeHeightManeuver(center, minimumEpoch, hold, radius, engine)` becomes `new
  ApogeeHeightManeuver(radius, engine, minimumEpoch, hold, center)`, or `new ApogeeHeightManeuver(radius)` on a spacecraft
  of one engine about the centre of its orbit; `new PlaneAlignmentManeuver(minimumEpoch, hold, target, engine)` `new
  PlaneAlignmentManeuver(target, engine, minimumEpoch, hold)`; `new PhasingManeuver(minimumEpoch, target, n, engine)`
  `new PhasingManeuver(target, n, engine, minimumEpoch)`, and `new PhasingManeuver(center, minimumEpoch, lambda, n,
  engine)` `new PhasingManeuver(lambda, n, engine, minimumEpoch, center)`; a user `ImpulseManeuver` calls
  `base(engine, minEpoch, holdDuration, maneuverCenter)`.
- **Breaking: radii checked, an apogee above the surface of its centre and an inclination in [0, π]** (lot L5b, decision
  68 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): a radius of `ApogeeHeightManeuver`, `PerigeeHeightManeuver` or
  `CombinedManeuver` that is not finite or not above 0 throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` naming it (`apogeeRadius`,
  `perigeeRadius`), "a radius from the centre …; for a height h pass R + h"; an apogee radius below the equatorial radius
  of a celestial body centre throws `ArgumentException` in the constructor for a given centre (`apogeeRadius`, or
  `targetOrbit` for the target-orbit form; the radius of a deferred body, `PlanetsAndMoons.EARTH_BODY`, is read there) and
  `InvalidOperationException` from the propagator constructor and `Propagate` for an inferred one; the inclination of
  `CombinedManeuver` not finite or outside [0, π] throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (`inclination`). Before, all were
  accepted: 1000e3 m, an altitude given for an apogee radius, put the apogee 5378 km under the surface and ended in
  `InsufficientFuelException`; an inclination above π threw `ArgumentException` at the burn, and a negative one, which
  `KeplerianElements` accepts in [−π, π], was executed (`CombinedManeuverTest.CheckPreconditions` passed 10.0 rad, of no
  effect on its preconditions, now 0.5 rad). A perigee inside the body stays legal (a deorbit). No maneuver of the
  repository's tests or of the conformance cases is refused (`ImpulseConstructionTests`). Migration: give a radius from
  the centre, R + h for an altitude h; an inclination in [0, π].
- **Breaking: `TargetApogee`, `TargetPerigeeHeight`, `MinimumEpoch` and `ManeuverHoldDuration` are renamed
  `TargetApogeeRadius`, `TargetPerigeeRadius`, `MinEpoch` and `HoldDuration`** (lot L5b, R13 and D2 choice 10 of #668,
  decisions 68 and 70, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): `ApogeeHeightManeuver.TargetApogee`,
  `PerigeeHeightManeuver.TargetPerigeeHeight` and `CombinedManeuver.TargetPerigeeHeight`, radii in metres, and
  `Maneuver.MinimumEpoch` and `Maneuver.ManeuverHoldDuration`, the same values; no forwarder. Migration: the new names.
- **Breaking: the constructors of the impulses check the frame of their target no more** (lot L5b, decision 65 of #668,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): `PlaneAlignmentManeuver`, `ApsidalAlignmentManeuver`, `PhasingManeuver(targetOrbit,
  …)` and the protected `ImpulseManeuver(targetOrbit, …)` threw `ArgumentException` for a target in another frame than
  the initial orbit of the spacecraft of the engine's tank (or ICRF on a TLE or TEME spacecraft), when that tank was on a
  spacecraft (the target-orbit forms of `ApogeeHeightManeuver` and `PerigeeHeightManeuver` never checked it); a weaker
  rule than the propagation's, which took a TEME target on a TLE spacecraft the propagation rejected. The rule is now
  `Spacecraft.SetManeuvers` (`ArgumentException`, `maneuvers`) and the propagation (#685), against the frame the spacecraft
  is propagated in. Migration: none for a target in the frame of the propagation; the error of another frame moves to
  `SetManeuvers`.
- **Breaking: the attitudes take their targets first, then the optional `minEpoch`, `holdDuration` and
  `maneuverCenter`, and the single-vector attitudes an optional `bodyAxis`** (lot L5b, D1 rule 8 and R13 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decision 69, decided by S.
  Guillet, 2026-11-23): `NadirAttitude`, `ZenithAttitude`, `ProgradeAttitude`, `RetrogradeAttitude`, `NormalAttitude` and
  `AntiNormalAttitude` take `(minEpoch = default, holdDuration = default, maneuverCenter = null, bodyAxis =
  BodyAxis.Front)` and expose `BodyAxis`, the axis they point, read on the spacecraft of the plan (`GetBodyAxis`, above);
  the base `Attitude(minEpoch = default, holdDuration = default, maneuverCenter = null)`;
  `InstrumentPointingToAttitude(instrument, target, minEpoch = default, holdDuration = default, maneuverCenter = null)`;
  where they took `(maneuverCenter, minimumEpoch, maneuverHoldDuration)` (`InstrumentPointingToAttitude`:
  `(minimumEpoch, maneuverHoldDuration, instrument, target, aberration)`), each required but the aberration (the engine
  of every attitude went with decisions 48 and 93, above). An undefined `BodyAxis` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`
  naming its parameter. The default axis, the front, is the attitude of before, bit for bit. An old positional call no
  longer compiles (a `CelestialItem` first does not convert to a `Time`). Migration: `new NadirAttitude(center, epoch,
  hold)` becomes `new NadirAttitude(epoch, hold, center)`, or `new NadirAttitude()` from the start of the run about the
  centre of the orbit; `new NadirAttitude(bodyAxis: BodyAxis.Down)` points another axis; a user `Attitude` calls
  `base(minEpoch, holdDuration, maneuverCenter)`.
- **Breaking: `TriadAttitude` has four constructors of `IAttitudeTarget` targets, and its factories follow D1 rule 8**
  (lot L5b, decisions 69 and 70 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): `(BodyAxis, IAttitudeTarget, BodyAxis,
  IAttitudeTarget, …)`, two axes of the spacecraft resolved on the spacecraft of the plan at each use as the
  single-vector attitudes resolve theirs (new; the same or opposite axes throw `ArgumentException`, an undefined one
  `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`); `(Vector3, IAttitudeTarget, Vector3, IAttitudeTarget, …)`, literal body vectors;
  `(Instrument, IAttitudeTarget, IAttitudeTarget, …)`, the boresight and the reference vector of an instrument; and
  `(Instrument, IAttitudeTarget, Instrument, IAttitudeTarget, …)`, the boresights of two instruments; each followed by the
  optional `minEpoch`, `holdDuration`, `maneuverCenter` and `minVectorSeparation`. The constructors of `ILocalizable`
  targets are removed (below): a celestial target is a `CelestialAttitudeTarget`, which carries its correction, geometric
  by default as the removed path computed it, so a TRIAD of the same targets points the same way. Their centre, the
  primary target or a site's body, becomes the rule of every maneuver: the one given, else the one the run infers
  (decisions 61, 62 and 99; the direction depends on the centre through rounding only), and a null centre no longer
  throws `ArgumentNullException` in the `IAttitudeTarget` constructor. `PrimaryTarget` and `SecondaryTarget` are typed
  `IAttitudeTarget`, never null (an `ILocalizable`, null for an orbital direction, before);
  `MinimumVectorSeparation` is renamed `MinVectorSeparation`, its parameter `minVectorSeparation`; `CreateLVLH` is
  renamed `CreateLvlh(minEpoch = default, holdDuration = default, maneuverCenter = null)` (D2's casing of acronyms) and
  `CreateProgradeWithSunTracking(sun, minEpoch = default, holdDuration = default, maneuverCenter = null)` keeps its
  required Sun, first, wrapped in a geometric `CelestialAttitudeTarget` as before (decision 70: a Sun built in the factory
  would read the data provider at the call). Both factories are the `BodyAxis` shape, bit for bit. No forwarder.
  Migration: `new TriadAttitude(minimumEpoch, hold, Spacecraft.Front, moon, Spacecraft.Up, sun)` becomes `new
  TriadAttitude(Spacecraft.Front, new CelestialAttitudeTarget(moon), Spacecraft.Up, new CelestialAttitudeTarget(sun),
  minimumEpoch, hold)`, or `BodyAxis.Front` and `BodyAxis.Up` for the axes of the spacecraft of the plan; `new
  TriadAttitude(center, epoch, hold, Spacecraft.Down, OrbitalDirectionTarget.Nadir, Spacecraft.Front,
  OrbitalDirectionTarget.Prograde)` becomes `new TriadAttitude(Spacecraft.Down, OrbitalDirectionTarget.Nadir,
  Spacecraft.Front, OrbitalDirectionTarget.Prograde, epoch, hold, center)`; `TriadAttitude.CreateLvlh(epoch, hold, center)`
  for `CreateLVLH(center, epoch, hold)`, `CreateProgradeWithSunTracking(sun, epoch, hold, center)` for
  `CreateProgradeWithSunTracking(center, epoch, hold, sun)`; `MinVectorSeparation` for `MinimumVectorSeparation`.
- **Breaking: `InstrumentPointingToAttitude` points at an `IAttitudeTarget`, which carries its correction, and its
  centre is that of every maneuver** (lot L5b, decisions 62 and 67 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23):
  `Target` is an `IAttitudeTarget` (an `ILocalizable` before), so the boresight may point at an orbital direction too, and
  the attitude's own `Aberration`, `Aberration.LT` by default, is removed with its parameter (below): the direction is
  `Target.GetDirection(state)`, a `CelestialAttitudeTarget` corrected as #549 corrected the attitude's (#740), its
  unknown aberration refused by `CelestialAttitudeTarget` (#806). A target given as `new CelestialAttitudeTarget(moon)`
  is geometric, 9.165e-5 rad from the former default for the Moon from a LEO. The centre, the target (or a site's body)
  before, is the one given, else the one the run infers (decision 62), which moves the direction by rounding only: the
  preview (`ComputeStateOrientation`) of the reference tests takes the state about its own observer, the Earth, and
  moves within their tolerances, against `spkcvo_c` the Moon from 1.012e-13 to 1.122e-13 rad at worst (CN+S; 2.1e-13
  allowed), a star against its closed form from 1.573e-16 to 1.138e-16 rad (3.2e-16 allowed), the site unchanged
  (1.140e-12 rad, its centre the Earth before and after), the same on Linux x64, Windows x64 and macOS arm64 (`InstrumentPointingAttitudeTests`, CI of #820); a spacecraft
  target with LT moves by 1.02e-8 rad about the Earth and 1.20e-7 rad about the Sun at 100 m, 4.5e-10 and 1.0e-9 rad at
  10 km, 1.9e-12 and 2.0e-11 rad at 1000 km, geometric by 0 rad about the Earth and 4e-14 to 5e-14 rad about the Sun, the
  light time itself 1.08e-4 rad (the probe of the gap analysis of L5b, which corrects the "3.8e-16 rad geometric, 7.9e-12
  rad with LT" of decision 62, measured on a far target, the Moon). In SSB mode a library `CelestialAttitudeTarget` takes
  the central body of the run when the centre cannot be inferred, any other target requires `maneuverCenter` (decision
  99). Migration: `new InstrumentPointingToAttitude(camera, new CelestialAttitudeTarget(moon, Aberration.LT), epoch, hold)`
  for `new InstrumentPointingToAttitude(epoch, hold, camera, moon)`, `new CelestialAttitudeTarget(moon, aberration)` for
  the `aberration` argument, `new CelestialAttitudeTarget(moon)` for `Aberration.None`.
- **Breaking: the command-line tool takes its objects as positional arguments and everything else as options** (lot L8,
  R29 of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-24: no compatibility with the positional forms of 10.x
  beyond the aliases of `time-converter`). The kernels move from the first positional argument to `-K`, repeatable,
  after the paths of `ASTRO_KERNELS`; the window and the step to `--begin`, `--end` and `--step`, an epoch to `--epoch`,
  the frame and the aberration to `--frame` and `--aberration`, the values of the searches to `--relation`, `--value`,
  `--adjust`, `--system`, `--coordinate`, `--target-shape`, `--front-shape`, `--occultation`, `--target-frame`,
  `--fixed-frame`, `--site` and `--angle`; the type flags (`-s -k -q -t`, `-d -c`, `--to-state-vector`, `--to-keplerian`,
  `--to-equinoctial`) become `--from state|keplerian|equinoctial|tle` and `--as`, an orbit `--orbit` (a TLE
  `--orbit "<line 1>" --orbit "<line 2>"`, without centre, epoch or frame, which it carries), the target epoch and frame
  of the converter `--target-epoch` and `--target-frame`, and the settings of `propagate` (`-r -a -n`, mass, area, Cd and
  bodies) `--srp`, `--drag`, `--degree`, `--mass`, `--area`, `--cd` and `--body`, its directory `--output`. An object is
  an identifier or a name, a negative identifier given bare (`-1000`, which the parser read as options before), and a
  positional argument a command does not take is an input error (10.x read the frame and the aberration there). Migration:
  the old-to-new form of each command in `docs/reference/cli.md`, "Migrating from 10.x", for example
  `ephemeris k 301 399 B E 00:01:00 ICRF LT -k` → `ephemeris 301 399 -K k --begin B --end E --step 1min --aberration LT --as keplerian`.
- **Breaking: `astro propagate` runs with the library's defaults** (lot L8, choice 12 of #668, decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-19): RK7(8) at 1e-9 with outputs every 60 s, a drag coefficient of 2.2 and, with `--drag`, NRLMSISE-00 at nominal
  space weather for the Earth, where it ran Velocity-Verlet at 1 s with outputs every second, Cd 0.3 and the U.S. Standard
  Atmosphere 1976. Its SPK is the library run of those settings on the Earth of the CLI (EGM2008 at degree 10), within
  the rounding of the SPK (4.71e-9 m at most over Linux x64, Windows and macOS arm64; `PropagateTests.Defaults_AreTheLibrarysRun`). After 30 min of a 6800 km orbit with drag and SRP, it ends 4.864 m from
  the 10.x run of the same orbit without drag or SRP. On a run with drag, the coefficient alone multiplies the drag by 7.3. Mars keeps its
  standard atmosphere; `--atmosphere` without `--drag` or for another centre than the Earth, `--drag` about another centre
  than the Earth and Mars, a `--body` that is the centre, a mass or an area of 0 or less and a negative drag coefficient
  are input errors. Migration: `--integrator vv --step 1s --cd 0.3`, with `--atmosphere standard` for a run with `--drag`
  about the Earth, writes the SPK of 10.x byte for byte (measured from a state and from a TLE with drag and SRP at
  `--degree 20`, against main 76e02ed7).
- **Breaking: a step of the command line needs a colon or a unit** (lot L8, R29 of #668): `[d.]hh:mm:ss[.f]` or a number
  and `s`, `min`, `h` or `d`; a bare `60` was 60 days (`TimeSpan.Parse`) and is an input error. Migration: `60s`, `1min` or
  `00:01:00`.
- **Breaking: the command line reads its numbers in invariant culture** (lot L8, #814): a dot as decimal separator, no
  thousands separator, a finite value; a value in another form is an input error. Migration: write the decimals with a dot.
- **Breaking: exit codes and messages of the command line** (lot L8, R29 of #668): 0 for a success and for the help and
  the version, 2 for an argument the command cannot read (an unknown command, option, object, frame, value or unit, a
  missing argument), 3 for the kernels (none, a missing path, a file SPICE refuses), 1 for an error of the library or of
  SPICE; each error is one line on the standard error, its trace with `--verbose`, where Cocona exited 129 for an unknown
  option and for the help, and every exception ended the process with its stack trace and exit code 1; the standard output
  holds the data only, without the banner `IO.Astrodynamics.CLI v11.0.0 experimental` that preceded it, and `--version`
  writes `astro 11.0.0`. Migration: test 2 and 3 where a script tested 129 or 1, and read the data from the first line.
- **Breaking: the command line writes its epochs in the scale of the input** (lot L8, R29 of #668, decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-19): `orientation`, the window searches, `frame-converter` and `orbital-parameters-converter` write UTC labels for
  a `Z` input where they wrote TDB (`ephemeris` already wrote the scale of its window), a converted label the nearest tick of
  the instant, which can sit one tick off it. Migration: `--time-scale tdb`.
- **Breaking: the kernel writers of `Clock`, `SpacecraftFrame`, `Instrument`, `Site` and `SiteFrame` are synchronous**
  (lot L5c, R14 and decision 78 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): `void Clock.Write(FileInfo)`,
  `SpacecraftFrame.Write(FileInfo)`, `Instrument.WriteFrame(FileInfo)`, `Instrument.WriteKernel(FileInfo)` (abstract,
  overridden by the three shapes), `Site.WriteFrame(FileInfo)` and `SiteFrame.Write(FileInfo)` replace the six `Write*Async`
  methods, which returned a `Task` over a few kilobytes of text; the files are the same bytes. Migration:
  `await clock.WriteAsync(f)` → `clock.Write(f)`; `await frame.WriteAsync(f)` → `frame.Write(f)`;
  `await instrument.WriteFrameAsync(f)` → `instrument.WriteFrame(f)`; `await instrument.WriteKernelAsync(f)` →
  `instrument.WriteKernel(f)`; `await site.WriteFrameAsync(f)` → `site.WriteFrame(f)`; `await siteFrame.WriteAsync(f)` →
  `siteFrame.Write(f)`; or, for the kernels of a spacecraft, `spacecraft.WriteKernels(directory)`.
- **Breaking: the constructor `SpacecraftFrame(Spacecraft)` is internal**
  ([#799](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/799)(d), lot L5c, decision 78 of
  #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): a frame built apart from its spacecraft held an empty attitude record, which
  no propagation fills, and its CK writer threw. Migration: `spacecraft.Frame`, the frame the spacecraft builds.
- **Breaking: `SpacecraftFrame.WriteOrientation(FileInfo, Spacecraft)` is internal**
  ([#799](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/799)(d), lot L5c, decision 78 of
  #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): it wrote the attitude record of the frame's spacecraft under the id of the
  spacecraft it was given (measured: the record of one spacecraft written under the id of another, never propagated).
  Migration: `spacecraft.WriteOrientation(file)` or `spacecraft.WriteKernels(directory)`.
- **Breaking: `Spacecraft.WriteEphemeris` of a spacecraft that stores no state throws `InvalidOperationException`**
  ([#799](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/799)(e), lot L5c, decision 81 of
  #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): it threw the `ArgumentException` (`arcs`) of the SPK writer, which blamed the
  file for what the spacecraft lacked; nothing is written. An arc of one state keeps its `ArgumentException` (decisions
  87 and 89). Migration: catch `InvalidOperationException`, or test the stored states first (propagate the spacecraft,
  or give it states with `AddPropagatedStates`).
- **Breaking: `Star.WriteEphemeris` of a star that stores fewer than three states throws `InvalidOperationException`**
  ([#799](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/799)(e), lot L5c, decision 81 of
  #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): it threw the `ArgumentException` (`stateVectors`) of
  `SpiceAPI.WriteEphemeris`, whose native writer writes three states or more; nothing is written. `SpiceAPI.WriteEphemeris`
  and `Site.WriteEphemeris`, whose arguments are at fault, keep theirs. Migration: catch `InvalidOperationException`, or
  propagate the star over three steps or more.
- **Breaking: `CosmographiaExporter.ExportAsync` refuses to replace a previous export SPICE holds**
  ([#799](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/799)(c), lot L5c, decision 103 of
  #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-25): `<Mission>_<Scenario>` loaded with `LoadKernels`, a loaded directory above it
  or inside it, or a file of it that SPICE holds, a meta-kernel's included (decision 102), throws
  `InvalidOperationException` naming it, before anything is deleted or written. Before, the export deleted it under
  SPICE's load: its text kernels stayed in the kernel pool with the old content, and a later unload that read them again
  failed. The export never changes the kernels SPICE holds; a first export, with no `<Mission>_<Scenario>` to replace, is
  written under a loaded directory as before. Migration: `UnloadKernels` the previous export (or the
  meta-kernel that names its files) before the export, and load the new one after it.
- **Breaking: the text kernel writers unload the file they replace** ([#799](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/799)(c),
  lot L5c, decision 103 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-25): `Clock.Write`, `SpacecraftFrame.Write`,
  `Instrument.WriteFrame`, `Instrument.WriteKernel`, `Site.WriteFrame` and `SiteFrame.Write`, as the SPK and CK writers
  since [#706](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/706), first unload a file
  `LoadKernels` loaded as `UnloadKernels` does, then every other load SPICE holds of it (a meta-kernel's, a name whose
  symbolic links resolve through it), write it and leave it unloaded. Before, the file was rewritten under SPICE's load,
  which a later `LoadKernels` skipped as a file already loaded: SPICE read the old content (measured: a frame kernel
  rewritten for another spacecraft still named the first, `TextKernelReplaceTests`). The files are the same bytes; a
  failed unload throws `SpiceException` and leaves the file as it was. Migration: load the file again after the write.
- **Breaking: `CosmographiaExporter.ExportAsync` refuses a name that is not a portable file name**
  ([#799](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/799)(a), lot L5c, decisions 74 and
  105 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23 and 2026-11-25): a spacecraft, instrument, site or star name, or the
  export directory `<Mission>_<Scenario>` the mission and scenario names form, that is empty, holds one of
  `/ \ : * ? " < > |` or a control character, is `.` or `..`, ends with a dot or a space, or is a device name Windows
  reserves (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1 to COM9, LPT1 to LPT9, in any case, alone or before a dot) throws
  `InvalidOperationException` naming the object and the reason, before anything is deleted or written (internal
  `Kernels/PortableFileNames`, beside `TextKernelNames`). Before, a name holding a `/` or a `\` was written into nested
  directories on Linux and macOS, a scenario named `/..` deleted the output directory (#822, under **Fixed**), and a
  reserved name or a trailing dot wrote files Windows cannot open. The constructors do not check it. Migration: rename the
  object (no name of the repository's tests and examples changes).
- **Breaking: `astro propagate` refuses a spacecraft name that is not a portable file name**
  ([#799](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/799)(a), lot L5c, decision 74 of
  #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): the rule of the export, checked before the propagation, exit code 2
  (`Error: name: …`), where the name propagated and was written into nested directories or failed after the propagation.
  Migration: another name.
- **A `TLE` reads no kernel when it is built** (lot L7, R21 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668)): its Earth reads its GM, radii,
  frame and orbit from the data provider at the first member that needs them (`MeanSemiMajorAxis`,
  `ToMeanKeplerianElements`, SGP4), from the provider set at that time, a failed read keeping nothing; so a valid set gives
  its fields, `NoradCatalogId`, `MeanMeanMotion` and `ToOmm` without kernels, and `MeanSemiMajorAxis` throws
  `InvalidOperationException` naming `BODY399_GM` before them, then gives ∛(GM/n²) of the kernel GM once they are loaded,
  bit for bit the value of a TLE built after them (`ColdStartTests.Tle_ReadBeforeItsKernels_ThrowsSpicesError_AndWorksOnceTheyAreLoaded`).
  Before, the constructor read the Earth, and a TLE built before the kernels kept a GM of 0, a semi-major axis of 0 and a
  NaN `MeanMotion()` for its life. `ToString` prints the semi-major axis only when the provider gives the GM, and the mean
  motion. With the kernels loaded nothing moves (`TLETests`, `Sgp4ReferenceTests`, the propagation of a TLE spacecraft).
  Migration: none.
- **`TLE.ToOmm` writes the mean motion of the field** (lot L7, decision 111 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-26):
  `MEAN_MOTION` is the field of line 2 as written, in rev/day; before, √(GM/a³)·86400/2π with a = ∛(GM/n²), which moved it
  on 22 of the 31 sets of `Data/Sgp4Reference` by up to 3 ulp (3.4e-16 relative, e.g. 15.957445309999999 for 15.95744531;
  `TleMeanMotionTests`), so the conformance runner's `tle_to_omm` deltas fall to 0. The occultation step a TLE spacecraft
  infers (decision 106) takes `MeanMeanMotion`, within 2 ulp of the former `MeanMotion()`, under a tick of its period.
  Migration: none.

**Removed**

- **The window searches on the target: `FindWindowsOnDistanceConstraint`, `FindWindowsOnOccultationConstraint` and
  `FindWindowsOnCoordinateConstraint` of `CelestialItem`, `ILocalizable` and `Site`, `Site.FindWindowsOnIlluminationConstraint`,
  `Instrument.FindWindowsInFieldOfViewConstraint`, and the public constructor, `FindWindowsWithCondition` and
  `EvaluateCondition` of `GeometryFinder`, now a static class** (lot L6, R15 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), choice 1 and §7 of the
  re-baseline, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19, no forwarder): the searches are on the observer, their settings one
  options record per kind (`WindowSearchOptions`, `OccultationSearchOptions`, `FieldOfViewSearchOptions`), each on the
  path of the former search of the target with the observer as argument, the same windows but for the two Breaking
  entries above (a site observer's occultation, the labels). The raw searches of `SpiceAPI`, by NAIF identifiers, stay;
  an implementer of `ILocalizable` drops its three searches, which the extensions replace for any `ILocalizable` (the
  library's search, through `GetEphemeris`). Migration:
  - `target.FindWindowsOnDistanceConstraint(window, observer, relation, value, aberration, step)` →
    `observer.FindDistanceWindows(window, target, relation, value, new WindowSearchOptions { Step = step, Aberration = aberration })`;
  - `target.FindWindowsOnCoordinateConstraint(window, observer, frame, system, coordinate, relation, value, adjust, aberration, step)`
    → `observer.FindCoordinateWindows(window, target, frame, system, coordinate, relation, value, new WindowSearchOptions
    { Step = step, Aberration = aberration, AdjustValue = adjust })`, `AdjustValue` left null but for `AbsoluteMin` and
    `AbsoluteMax` (with another relation, or on `gfdist_c`, it throws `ArgumentException`; the former searches ignored
    it); the visibility of a spacecraft from a site, its declination in `site.Frame`, is
    `site.FindHorizontalWindows(window, spacecraft, HorizontalCoordinate.Elevation, relation, mask, options)`, bit for bit;
  - `target.FindWindowsOnOccultationConstraint(window, observer, targetShape, front, frontShape, type, aberration, step[, options])`
    and `site.FindWindowsOnOccultationConstraint(window, target, …)` → `observer.FindOccultationWindows(window, target,
    front, new OccultationSearchOptions { Step = step, Aberration = aberration, TargetShape = targetShape, FrontShape =
    frontShape, OccultationType = type, FrontFrame = …, TargetFrame = … })` (a null shape an ellipsoid for a body with
    radii, a point otherwise; the step inferred for a propagated or TLE spacecraft about the front body, decision 106),
    `ConvergenceTolerance` left null on CSPICE's `gfoclt_c` path, where it throws `ArgumentException` (`options`) while
    the former search ignored it;
  - `site.FindWindowsOnIlluminationConstraint(window, angle, relation, value, adjust, aberration, step, source[, method])`
    → `site.FindIlluminationWindows(window, angle, relation, value, source, new WindowSearchOptions { Step = step,
    Aberration = aberration, AdjustValue = adjust })`, `AdjustValue` left null but for `AbsoluteMin` and `AbsoluteMax`, as
    for the coordinates, the method ELLIPSOID, the only one (`SpiceAPI.FindWindowsOnIlluminationConstraint` keeps
    its `method`, and the emission and phase angles with an observer);
  - `instrument.FindWindowsInFieldOfViewConstraint(window, spacecraft, target, targetFrame, targetShape, aberration, step)`
    → `instrument.FindFieldOfViewWindows(window, target, new FieldOfViewSearchOptions { Step = step, Aberration =
    aberration, TargetShape = targetShape, TargetFrame = targetFrame })`, the observer the instrument's spacecraft;
  - `new GeometryFinder().FindWindowsWithCondition(window, quantity, relation, value, step)` →
    `GeometryFinder.FindWindows(window, quantity, relation, value, new WindowSearchOptions { Step = step })`, a
    `Func<Time, double>` or a `Func<Time, bool>`; `EvaluateCondition`, which no search used, has no replacement (compare
    the values).
- **`Window.Merge` and `Window.Intersects(Time)`** (lot L6, R16 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-19, no forwarder): renamed outright, so that the names say what they compute (a hull, which spans the gap
  between two disjoint windows, and the membership of an instant). Migration: `w1.Merge(w2)` → `w1.Hull(w2)`, the same
  window bit for bit (or `w1.TryMerge(w2, out var merged)` to merge only windows that share an instant);
  `window.Intersects(time)` → `window.Contains(time)`. `Intersects(Window)` is unchanged.
- **The `ILocalizable` constructors of `TriadAttitude`, `PrimaryAttitudeTarget` and `SecondaryAttitudeTarget`, and
  `InstrumentPointingToAttitude.Aberration`** (lot L5b, decisions 67 and 69 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23):
  the three TRIAD forms of `ILocalizable` targets (literal vectors, one instrument, two instruments), whose targets were
  read back by `PrimaryAttitudeTarget` and `SecondaryAttitudeTarget` beside `PrimaryTarget` and `SecondaryTarget`, and
  the correction of the pointing attitude, which its target now carries. Migration: wrap each target in `new
  CelestialAttitudeTarget(target)` (geometric, as the removed forms computed it) or `new CelestialAttitudeTarget(target,
  aberration)`, and read it back from `PrimaryTarget`, `SecondaryTarget` or `Target` (`CelestialAttitudeTarget.Target`,
  `.Aberration`).
- **The value equality of `FuelTank`, `Engine` and `Payload`: `Equals`, `GetHashCode`, `==`, `!=` and
  `IEquatable<T>`** (lot L5b, decision 76 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-23): they compared the name, the model
  and the serial number (the mass too for a payload), so two tanks of no model compared equal once both were optional,
  and a twin passed for the instance it copied (the library compared its own components by reference since #676). The
  three compare by reference. Migration: compare `Name` (and the other values) where a value comparison was meant;
  `Spacecraft.FuelTanks.Contains(tank)` tells whether a spacecraft holds that instance.
- **`Instrument.PositionInFOV`** (protected), on which `IsInFOV` was built before #515: its reference vector was not made
  perpendicular to the boresight and its corrections were those of `CelestialItem.GetEphemeris`. A subclass of
  `Instrument` that called it no longer compiles. Use `IsInFOV`, the `POINT` condition of CSPICE's `fovtrg` with the
  field and the corrections of the search; the azimuth and the elevation it returned have no replacement
  ([#515](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/515)).
- **`LowThrustManeuver`.** It was never implemented: every member threw `NotImplementedException`. It was marked
  `[Obsolete]` in 10.1.0 (see its Deprecated entry). Finite thrust is planned as a separate feature
  ([#334](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/334), [#536](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/pull/536)).
- **`Quaternion.Zero`**, the identity under another name and an assignable field: use `Quaternion.Identity` (Changed
  above, [#571](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/571)).
- **`Star.PropagationOutput`**, always null: the output directory of an older design that wrote the propagation to
  files, which no code set, while a star keeps its propagated states in memory. It was marked `[Obsolete]` in the
  fourth round of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668) and is removed
  outright in lot L1 (R02, the amendment of D1 of 2026-11-19: no forwarder). Migration: read `IsPropagated` to know
  whether the star holds propagated states, and write them with `WriteEphemeris`, to a file of the caller's choice.
- **`ExceptionBase`** (R03 of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668),
  section A), an `Exception` with the three standard constructors, the base of `InsufficientFuelException` alone, which
  derives from `InvalidOperationException` now (Changed above). Migration: catch `InsufficientFuelException`, or derive
  a caller's own exception from the standard type that fits it.
- **Six exports of the native library that .NET never called** (R03 of #668, section A): `LaunchProxy`,
  `TDBToStringProxy`, `UTCToStringProxy`, `ConvertTDBToUTCProxy`, `ConvertUTCToTDBProxy` and
  `ConvertStateVectorToEquatorialCoordinatesProxy`. No P/Invoke declaration of `SpiceAPI` named them, and two returned
  SPICE's message as their date string; the C++ classes they called stay, with their tests. Only a C++ or other native
  consumer of `IO.Astrodynamics.so`, `.dll` or `.dylib` meets it. Migration: `Launch.FindLaunchWindows`, `Time.ToString`,
  `Time.ToUTC`, `Time.ToTDB` and `StateVector.ToEquatorial` in .NET; the C++ classes `Launch`, `TDB`, `UTC` and
  `StateVector` in C++.
- **`ITimeFrame`, `TimeFrame` and the namespace `TimeSystem.Frames`** (`TDBTimeFrame`, `TDTTimeFrame`, `TAITimeFrame`,
  `UTCTimeFrame`, `GPSTimeFrame`, `LocalTimeFrame`), with `Time.Frame`, `TimeFrame.LeapSecondsFrom` and a caller's own
  `ITimeFrame` (lot L2, R24 of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668)).
  Migration: `TimeScale` and `Time.Scale` (Changed above); TAI − UTC at an instant `t` is
  `t.ToTAI().DateTime - t.ToUTC().DateTime`; a scale of the caller's own has no replacement.
- **Local time: `Time.ToLocal()`, `TimeFrame.LocalFrame` and the offset form of `Time(string)` as a local time** (D3.1
  of #668: a local time is not a scale, its instant depends on the zone and the daylight saving time of the machine, so
  #751's handling of the repeated hour goes with it). Migration: `t.ToUTC().DateTime.ToLocalTime()` for the calendar of
  the machine's zone; `new Time(localDateTime.ToUniversalTime(), TimeScale.UTC)` for the instant of a local calendar.
- **`Time(string)`**: use `Time.Parse` (Changed above).
- **`Time.J2000`**, a `DateTime` (2000-01-01T12:00:00, kind `Unspecified`) among `Time`'s members (section A of R24: not
  retyped, so that `Time.J2000.AddDays(1)` cannot change meaning silently). Migration: `Time.J2000TDB`, or
  `Time.J2000TDB.DateTime` for the calendar.
- **`Time.Create(int, int, double)`**: use `Time.FromDayOfYear` (Changed above).
- **`Matrix.Set(int, int, double)`** (lot L2, R26 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668)): it wrote the terms in place,
  through every copy of the struct; `Matrix` is immutable (Changed above). Migration: `new Matrix(double[,])`,
  `Matrix.Create`, `Matrix.Diagonal` or `Matrix.Identity` to build a matrix, `With` for a copy with one term changed.
- **The operator `*` between two `Vector3`**, the dot product (R26 of #668, section A as amended: no forwarder;
  `System.Numerics.Vector3 * Vector3` is component-wise, so the operator read as a trap). `v1 * v2` no longer compiles,
  so no caller meets another meaning silently. Migration: `v1.Dot(v2)` (Added above), the same expression, bit for bit.
- **The public interop structs of `IO.Astrodynamics.DTO`** (lot L3, R04 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668)): `AzimuthRange`, `CelestialBody`, `EquinoctialElements`,
  `FrameTransformation`, `KeplerianElements`, `Launch`, `Planetodetic`, `Quaternion`, `Site`, `StateOrientation`,
  `StateVector`, `TLEElements`, `Vector3D` and `Window`, the P/Invoke layouts of the native layer, are internal: eleven
  bore the names of domain types, so that a `using IO.Astrodynamics.DTO` made them ambiguous (CS0104), and only
  `GetCelestialBodyInfo` reached one. Migration: `CelestialBodyInfo` for the body information (Changed above); the
  domain types (`IO.Astrodynamics.Math.Vector3`, `Quaternion`, `OrbitalParameters.StateVector`, `TimeSystem.Window`,
  `Coordinates.Planetodetic`, ...) for the others.
- **The ten raw conversions of `SpiceAPI`** (lot L3, R04 of #668, choice 1 as amended by section 7 of the re-baseline,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19: removed from the public API outright, no forwarder): `ConvertTleToStateVector(line1,
  line2, line3, epoch)`, `ConvertStateVectorToConicOrbitalElement(stateVector)` and `(stateVector, gm)`,
  `ConvertEquinoctialElementsToStateVector(elements)`, `ConvertConicElementsToStateVector(elements)`, `(elements, epoch)`
  and `(elements, epoch, gm)`, `Propagate2Bodies(stateVector, dt)`, `(stateVector, gm, dt)` and `(stateVector,
  targetEpoch)`. They twinned the object API through CSPICE; the library keeps them internal, the SPICE references of its
  tests. Migration, the object API, the library's own computation, which agrees with CSPICE to the tolerances of the
  tests, not bit for bit: `new TLE(name, line1, line2).ToStateVector(epoch)` (the same `evsgp4_c`);
  `stateVector.ToKeplerianElements()`; `elements.ToStateVector()` and `elements.ToStateVector(epoch)`;
  `stateVector.AtEpoch(stateVector.Epoch + dt).ToStateVector()` and `stateVector.AtEpoch(targetEpoch).ToStateVector()`,
  which count the TT seconds between the instants about the Earth (#508) where `Propagate2Bodies` counted the difference
  of the labels (the two differ by the change of TDB − TT over the interval, 3.3 ms at most, twice the 1.66 ms
  amplitude of TDB − TT); an explicit GM through an observer of that GM, a
  `CelestialBody` built from custom parameters. See [Two-body calls and element
  conversions](../reference/spice-api.md#two-body-calls-and-element-conversions).
- **The public helpers of the implementation** (lot L3, R04 of #668): `DictionnaryExtension` (a `GetOrAdd` on
  `IDictionary`), `Enumeration` (`GetDescription`, `GetValueFromDescription`), `ArrayBuilder`,
  `Converters.ProfilesConfiguration` (internal members only), `Helpers.Utf8StringWriter`,
  `Propagator.PropagationEphemerisCache` and `Propagator.PropagationFrameOrientationCache` (the force caches a
  propagation builds for itself), and the JSON model of the Cosmographia exporter (`Cosmographia.Model`, 50 types), whose
  files are the exporter's only output. Migration: `ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd` or `CollectionExtensions`;
  `DescriptionAttribute` read by reflection; `new T[n]` filled by the caller; `StringWriter` with an `Encoding`
  override; the exporter's files for the Cosmographia model.
- **The `Equatorial` constructors of two angles** (lot L3, R20 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668), section A of the re-baseline as
  amended by its section 7, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-19: removed outright, no forwarder): `Equatorial(declination,
  rightAscension, epoch)` and `(declination, rightAscension, distance, epoch)`, whose order was the reverse of the name
  of the type's members, so that a swap compiled and gave another direction ((0.853, 0.492, 0.174) for (0.853, 0.150,
  0.500)). `Equatorial(StateVector)` stays. Migration: `new Equatorial(dec, ra, epoch)` →
  `Equatorial.FromRightAscensionDeclination(ra, dec, epoch)`, and with a distance `(ra, dec, distance, epoch)`. See
  [Sites](../reference/sites.md#equatorial).
- **The coordinate conversions taking a flattening and a radius** (R20 of #668, choice 2 of the first annex, the
  design's recommendation as amended by section 7 of the re-baseline): `Planetodetic.ToPlanetocentric(flattening,
  equatorialRadius)`, `Planetocentric.ToPlanetodetic(flattening, equatorialRadius)`,
  `Planetocentric.RadiusFromPlanetocentricLatitude(equatorialRadius, flattening)` and its static form `(latitude,
  equatorialRadius, flattening)`, in two orders, so that a swapped radius compiled (0.00349 m); internal now, the
  conformance runner's custom ellipsoids among their callers. Migration: `ToPlanetocentric(body)`, `ToPlanetodetic(body)`,
  `RadiusFromPlanetocentricLatitude(body)` with the `CelestialBody` of the ellipsoid (the same arithmetic, bit for bit),
  or `body.RadiusFromPlanetocentricLatitude(latitude)`; `ToPlanetocentric(...).ToCartesianCoordinates()` →
  `ToCartesianCoordinates(body)`.
- **`GeopotentialModelParameters.GeopotentialModelPath`** (lot L4, R06 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668)): the `StreamReader` of the model

- **The public constructors of `GeopotentialGravitationalField`** (R06 of #668): `GeopotentialGravitationalField(StreamReader,

**Known limitations**

The open defects a caller can meet at this release, grouped by cause; each line gives the workaround when there is
one. The other open issues (tests, the conformance runner, benchmarks, documentation warnings and feature requests) are
not listed.

- **A star takes no radial velocity** ([#718](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/718)). `Star` moves along `iauStarpm`'s straight line with rv = 0, its distance
  from the catalog parallax: Barnard's star's −110.47 km/s (Gaia DR3) would move it by 64 mas after 10 years, 6.5″ after
  100 and 11.4′ after 1000, more than the straight line corrects (34 mas after 100 years). The radial velocity input
  that #718 recommends would be a new constructor parameter, and the defect fixes of 11.0.0 keep the existing signatures
  (#668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-14): it is left to an additive constructor overload after 11.0.0, in
  [#723](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/723) (decided by S. Guillet,
  2026-11-17; [Stars](../reference/stars.md#limits)).
- **The planetocentric latitude loses digits at the poles** (found in lot L3 of #668, no issue yet, reported to S.
  Guillet). `OrbitalParameters.ToPlanetocentric()` (before 11.0.0 `ToPlanetocentric(Aberration)`) and
  `CelestialItem.SubObserverPoint` take the latitude as asin(z / r), which loses digits where z / r rounds to 1, and
  `ToPlanetodetic()` and the geodetic coordinate searches go through it: 7.6e-12 rad from CSPICE `recgeo_c` 1.75e-5 rad
  from the poles of the Earth, 112 m from the axis, and 5.6e-16 rad below 1.5 rad (`GeodeticOneCallTests`).
  Workaround: atan2(z, √(x² + y²)) of the body-fixed position (`ToFrame(body.Frame).Position`) gives the full precision.
  The same path differs from `reclat_c` and `recgeo_c` on two degenerate positions: at the centre of the body the
  latitude is NaN (asin(0/0)), and the altitude too, where `reclat_c` gives (0, 0, 0) and `recgeo_c` (0, π/2, −b); on
  the polar axis with a negative-zero x (and y), the longitude is ±π (atan2 of signed zeros), where both give 0 (with
  +0, latitude ±π/2 exactly, longitude 0).
- **A boolean quantity in the managed window search**
  ([#678](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/678)). `GeometryFinder.FindWindows` of a `Func<Time, bool>`
  has no margin to search between its samples: a window or a gap shorter than the step can be lost. Use a step shorter
  than every window and gap, or a `double` quantity whose sign is the condition. A `double` quantity's search finds a
  window or a gap between two samples down to the resolution of `localmin`, about 2 √ε h + 2τ/3 for a step h and
  τ = 1 µs (2.5 µs at a 1 min step, 19 µs at 10 min, 41 µs at 22.5 min; #668), and no tangency there (an extreme
  exactly at the value). The occultation and field-of-view searches have the same limit, the bound scaling with
  `OccultationSearchOptions.ConvergenceTolerance` (#668: their documentation said "however short", and the `stepSize`
  of the distance, coordinate and illumination searches of `CelestialItem` and `Site` "every window and gap").
- **The light time of the occultation search with a spacecraft of the kernels**
  ([#828](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/828)). With `LT`, `CN`, `XLT` or
  `XCN` and a spacecraft of the kernels taking part, the library's occultation search and `gfoclt` find the same
  windows with edges up to 6.2e-4 s apart (LRO behind the Moon from DSS-13: 3.7e-4 s with `LT`, 1.2e-4 s with `CN`,
  6.2e-4 s with `XLT`; 5.0e-7 s geometric), though the states agree: the two light-time models differ, and which one is
  right is not established. Since lot L6 the occultation search of a site observer is the library's whatever the site
  (under **Changed**), so its edges move by those amounts from the former `gfoclt` path. Workaround: for `gfoclt`'s
  windows from a site of the kernels, `SpiceAPI.FindWindowsOnOccultationConstraint` with the site's NAIF id
  ([Occultations](../reference/occultations.md#accuracy)).
- **A crossing during a UTC leap second in the library's threshold search**
  ([#830](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/830)). `GeometryFinder`, the
  library's distance, coordinate, horizontal and illumination search, samples and solves in the calendar of the search
  window's start: on a UTC search window that spans a leap second, a crossing during the leap second is labelled at
  00:00:00, up to 1 s from its instant (found by reading the code, not measured). The CSPICE, occultation and
  field-of-view searches keep such an end in TDB. Workaround: search over the window in TDB,
  `new Window(start.ToTDB(), end.ToTDB())` ([Time Systems](../reference/time-and-windows.md#the-windows-of-a-search)).
- **Kernels the library writes** ([#545](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/545),
  [#546](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/546),
  [#655](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/655),
  [#661](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/661),
  [#706](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/706)). `Spacecraft.WriteOrientation`,
  `SpiceAPI.WriteOrientation` and `SpiceAPI.WriteEphemeris` (under `Star.WriteEphemeris` and `Site.WriteEphemeris`),
  and the text kernel writers since decision 103 of #668, leave the kernel they write unloaded: load it after writing. A file they replace is unloaded first under its path and
  the absolute names whose symbolic links resolve through it (#706), but not under a relative name other than its path
  (a meta-kernel's) nor through a hard link, through which SPICE goes on reading the replaced data: unload such a load
  before rewriting the file. `Spacecraft.WriteKernels` loads what it writes, each file by its own path, and refuses a
  directory inside a loaded one and a file SPICE holds, a meta-kernel's included; a load of the directory made while
  its handle lives furnishes nothing for the handle's files and does not take them over, `Dispose` unloading them all
  (load them again after it to keep them), and `IsLoaded` does not follow a user's `UnloadKernels` of them. A
  spacecraft propagated by `TLEPropagator` has no attitude record, so its CK cannot be written (`WriteKernels` refuses
  it too) and its field-of-view searches throw
  ([#682](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/682)); give it its attitude with
  `AddStateOrientationToICRF`, after the run.
  An instrument named `Frame` (any case) on a spacecraft `Sat` writes `FRAME_SAT_FRAME`, the variable of the spacecraft's
  own frame, in its frame kernel, so the kernel loaded last defines `SAT_FRAME`
  ([#812](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/812); `Add*Instrument` checks the names of the instruments among themselves only, decision 74 of #668):
  give no instrument that name; `WriteKernels` loads the instrument frame kernels after the spacecraft's, so the
  instrument's wins there.
  `Spacecraft.WriteEphemeris` refuses an arc of one state with `ArgumentException` (decisions 87 and 89 of #668), which
  `WriteKernels` refuses with `InvalidOperationException` before it writes anything. `WriteKernels` finds a file SPICE
  holds through a meta-kernel under its full path or an absolute name whose symbolic links resolve through it, not under
  a relative name other than its path, as the writers find it; it writes into a new subdirectory of its directory first,
  which a process killed meanwhile leaves, and a later load of the directory loads its files: delete it. Names composed
  across spacecraft ([#825](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/825)): a spacecraft
  `A` with an instrument `B` and a spacecraft `A_B` write the same file `A_B.tf`, and both define the body `A_B`, so
  `WriteKernels` refuses the second while the first handle lives and overwrites the first's instrument frame kernel after
  it; write one spacecraft per directory. `CosmographiaExporter.ExportAsync` writes two spacecraft, sites or stars of one
  name onto the same files, the last one winning
  ([#823](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/823)): give each object its own
  name; and it throws `InvalidOperationException` at the trajectory plot of a spacecraft whose initial orbit is open,
  which has no period ([#824](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/824)), the
  previous export left as it was since #799.
- **A window that leaves a spacecraft's stored states** (lot L7 of
  [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668)). Decision 81 of #668 gives a
  window argument that leaves a body's stored states `InvalidOperationException`, as `GetEphemeris` over a window, the
  managed distance search and, since lot L6, the field-of-view search throw
  ([Spacecraft](../reference/spacecraft.md#the-exceptions-of-the-reads-and-the-writes)), but the `ILocalizable`
  overloads of `ConjunctionAssessment.Analyze` and `AnalyzeAll` still throw `ArgumentException` for such a window, for
  one that meets a gap between the windows given to `AddPropagatedStates` (decision 86) and for a trajectory that does
  not cover the window: lot L7 changes them. Catch `ArgumentException` there until then.
- **Kernel paths of more than 255 characters** ([#673](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/673)). `LoadKernels` and the command line hand SPICE the full path of
  each kernel, so a kernel whose full path is longer than 255 characters cannot be loaded through them
  (`SPICE(FILENAMETOOLONG)`, SPICE's message in the `InvalidOperationException` since #706, nothing on the standard
  output since #727), while `Spacecraft.WriteEphemeris` and the
  text kernel writers still write it: load it through a meta-kernel that names it by a shorter relative path, or write
  it under a shorter directory. Paths are compared ordinally, so on Windows and macOS two spellings that differ in case
  are two entries.
- **Orientations read in CIRS or TIRS, and frames of the library built by name**
  ([#558](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/558)). `SpiceAPI.ReadOrientation` in
  CIRS or TIRS throws: SPICE does not know them (a frame built by those names is routed to `Frame.CIRS` and `Frame.TIRS`
  everywhere else since #656, Fixed above). The frame of a site built from coordinates and that of a managed spacecraft with an attitude
  record are read in J2000 and rotated ([#682](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/682)), and searched in by the library (third review of #690), but a frame built by
  such a name (`new Frame("MYSITE_TOPO")`) still goes to SPICE, as does any frame built by a name SPICE does not know,
  whose CSPICE search throws SPICE's error (no window before the fourth round of #668).
- **Identifiers that are not celestial bodies**
  ([#650](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/650),
  [#651](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/651)). `SpiceAPI.ReadEphemeris` by
  identifiers throws `ArgumentException` for a spacecraft observer: with `Aberration.None`, read with the spacecraft as
  target and negate the state (with LT, CN or +S the negation is not the state `spkezr` gives); so does a site observer
  that no loaded kernel names, and one whose SPK does not cover J2000 TDB, which its `Site` constructor reads, throws
  `InvalidOperationException`, with the same workaround (documented in the fourth round of #668). `new CelestialBody(399013)` and
  `CelestialItem.Create(399013)` of a site identifier build a body DSS-13 of GM 0 and frame DSS-13_TOPO about the Earth
  (they threw or were built with a garbage frame name before
  [#672](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/672), and about the Sun before #651,
  under Changed): build a `Site`.
  `SpiceAPI.ReadEphemeris` from a site identifier labels its state with a `Site` (#672). The commands of the CLI follow
  the same rule and build the same site (its SPICE name), under Changed.
  `MemoryDataProvider` throws `ArgumentException` naming `naifId` for a body it holds no information on, as
  `SpiceDataProvider` for an identifier SPICE does not name
  ([#680](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/680); `KeyNotFoundException` before).
- **Reads past the end of a propagation window**
  ([#626](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/626)). A propagation whose output
  step does not divide its window runs up to half a step past its end (its caches cover that span since #626), so a
  geopotential or drag read there past the coverage of the orientation data throws. Choose an output step that divides
  the window.
- **Impulses at the edges of the stored states**
  ([#638](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/638)). An impulse at the end of the propagation opens a last arc of one state, the state after it ([#575](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/575)),
  which an SPK segment cannot hold: `WriteEphemeris` ends with the arc before it, and SPICE reads the state before the
  impulse at that last epoch where `GetEphemeris` reads the state after it (the documented limitation of 11.0.0,
  decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-18). The state that closes an arc carries its
  impulse's tick, up to half a tick from its instant (about 0.4 mm at 8.6 km/s).
- **Attitudes** ([#592](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/592)). Between output epochs the
  attitude record is the spherical linear interpolation of its samples, not the law: a `NadirAttitude` 1.47e-3 rad off
  nadir at 60 s outputs in LEO and up to 1.04° near the roll singularity, a TRIAD law up to 3.8e-4 rad on a Molniya;
  shorten the output step where it matters. `TriadAttitude` rejects vectors collinear to the rounding of normal components at every separation
  (fourth round of [#668](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/668)), but a
  subnormal component (below about 2.2e-308) rounds by an absolute 4.9e-324: v = (1, 2, 3)·1e-320 and fl(0.7 v) have a
  sine of 1.1e-4 and pass a separation below that, with a roll set by rounding; give body vectors of a normal magnitude.
- **Two stored states a few ticks apart** (found by the review of #598, its issue to be opened). The read of the
  stored states of a propagated spacecraft (`GetEphemeris` from its centre without aberration, through its 8 nearest
  states) is ill-conditioned when two of them are a few ticks apart: the ISS's SGP4 states every 60 s over one hour,
  plus one 11 ticks after the last, given to the public `Spacecraft.AddPropagatedStates`, read up to 4.934e3 m off SGP4
  over the last 90 s (every 15 s; 4.336e3 m at +3570 s), 9.8 m with the extra state 100 µs after the last, 4.6e-4 m
  with it 1 s after, 7.6e-4 m without it (Linux x64, 2026-11-17): each SGP4 state carries the tick rounding of its epoch, about 0.77 mm per tick
  at 7.7 km/s, which the near-coincident pair amplifies. The propagations do not meet it: the stored states drop an
  output closer to an impulse than a tenth of the output step, and `TLEPropagator` a grid point that close to the window
  end (#598, Fixed above). Workaround: give `AddPropagatedStates` states at least a tenth of their spacing apart.
- **TLEs**. A spacecraft propagated numerically from a TLE ([#675](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/675)) integrates about the TLE's Earth, a point mass whose drag, without an atmospheric model,
  is NRLMSISE-00 at nominal space weather ([#674](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/674)), and an Earth with a geopotential or an atmosphere in the bodies throws
  `ArgumentException` (bodies of one identifier must have the same models, [#674](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/674)); give a TEME state on an Earth that
  carries the models
  ([Numerical propagation of a TLE](../reference/tle.md#numerical-propagation-of-a-tle)). CIRS and TIRS, quasi-inertial
  as TEME, are still rejected as initial frames. A TLE cannot be built without the kernels that define the Earth.
- **Runs on one spacecraft** ([#793](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/793), [#794](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/794)). A spacecraft takes one run at a
  time (decision 43 of #668), and nothing checks it yet: two runs on one spacecraft at the same time, through two
  propagators, `Spacecraft.Propagate`, a `TLEPropagator`, a scenario or a batch beside a direct run, interleave with no
  exception, and can charge a burn twice (a tank left at 841.263915 kg against 917.541305 kg in 1 trial of 12 in the gap
  analysis of lot L5); a guard that refuses the second run comes after lot L5 (#793;
  [Thread Safety](../guides/thread-safety.md#one-run-at-a-time-per-spacecraft)). Nor is the plan of a spacecraft
  changed during a run on it (decision 96 of #668, decided by S. Guillet, 2026-11-24): the run reads the plan as it
  goes, so a `SetManeuvers` during it mixes the two plans (the plan [m1, m2] set again during a run of [m1, m2] left
  `ExecutedManeuvers` reading m1, m1 in the second review of lot L5a); the same guard of #793 will make `SetManeuvers` throw
  `InvalidOperationException` while a run holds the spacecraft. A run stopped by its token lists in
  `ExecutedManeuvers` an attitude it scheduled before the stop whose activation it never reached, with its windows set
  and the chain advanced past it (decision 44 of #668, fixed after lot L5 in #794); the records of a run are not
  affected (a stopped run returns none), and the next run re-arms the spacecraft.
- **Inputs that fail in the run** ([#807](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/807), [#810](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/810), [#811](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/811),
  [#813](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/813)). A few inputs pass their constructor and throw only inside the propagation, with an exception that does
  not name them: a `PhasingManeuver` of `revolutionNumber` 0 or of a true longitude that is not finite
  (`ArgumentException`, `seconds`, at the burn, no fuel burned; #810), an `OrbitalDirectionTarget` of a value outside
  `OrbitalDirection`, `(OrbitalDirection)99` (`ArgumentOutOfRangeException` at the first orientation; #811), a spacecraft
  of total mass 0 propagated with drag or solar radiation pressure (`ArgumentOutOfRangeException`, `seconds`; #813),
  and an engine whose burn lasts longer than a `TimeSpan` holds, a fuel flow of 1e-12 kg/s for 10 m/s
  (`OverflowException` after the fuel is burnt, the windows unset and nothing in `ExecutedManeuvers`; #807). Give a
  revolution number of 1 or more and a finite longitude, a defined direction, a mass above 0 with mass-dependent forces
  and an engine whose burns fit in a `TimeSpan` (about 9.2e11 s); no fix is scheduled yet.
- **Monte Carlo runs** ([#795](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/795)). Each run of `MonteCarloPropagator` propagates a spacecraft built from the
  template's dry mass, maximum mass, area and drag and radiation coefficients only: its drag and SRP act on the dry
  mass, without the fuel and payloads, and its tanks, engines, payloads, instruments, body axes, hard-body radius and
  COSPAR id are dropped (a template with a maneuver plan throws since lot L5a, decision 41 of #668). Fixed after lot
  L5 with the long validation; meanwhile give the template the mass to propagate as its dry mass.
- **The mass of an avoidance trial** (second part of [#801](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/801)). The trial spacecraft of an avoidance
  option takes the mass before the burn less the fuel the delta-V needs (Tsiolkovsky), not limited by the fuel on
  board, so it can be lighter than the dry mass, and `AvoidanceOption` does not say that the burn cannot be made; fixed
  after lot L5 (the mass limited by the fuel on board, the shortfall reported).
- **CDM dates** ([#616](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/616)). A date in a
  leap second throws `CdmParseException`.
- **Angles brought into [0, 2π)**
  ([#471](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/471)). Angle normalization takes
  fl(2π) as 2π: each turn added to Ω, ω, ν or M leaves it 2.45e-16 rad low, each turn removed that much high, and
  `SpecialFunctions.NormalizeAngle(-1e-17)` returns 2π (360°, which can appear in an OPM or OMM).
- **The ephemeris time given to CSPICE**
  ([#665](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/665), item 4 of
  [#455](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/455)). CSPICE is
  given the managed one-term TDB as its ephemeris time, within 1.06 µs of the LSK formula SPICE evaluates (1.055 µs at
  the tick, [Time Scales](../reference/time-and-windows.md#time-scales)): a UTC epoch at a coverage bound of a kernel,
  as `str2et` computes it, can be read up to about 1.1 µs outside it and throw SPKINSUFFDATA. Read 2 µs inside the
  bound.
- **The equatorial coordinates of a light-time corrected state in a non-inertial frame.** `ToEquatorial` of such a state
  (ITRF93, MOON_ME) rotates it to ICRF at its epoch
  ([#680](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/680)): 3.05e-6 rad in RA and 1.15e-6 rad in Dec for the Moon from the Earth with LT in MOON_ME; read it in ICRF.
- **Illumination of a site above the ellipsoid**
  ([#654](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/654)). A site from the kernels,
  searched by `gfilum_c` with the normal of `surfnm_c` at the point, and the same site built from its coordinates,
  searched with the geodetic normal, give illumination windows up to 34.0 ms apart at DSS-13, 1070.85 m up (0.110″
  between the normals); `FindDayWindows` and `Launch` follow.
- **SSB mode about the Earth** ([#389](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/389)).
  With the variational equations in the step control (`IncludeInStepControl`) the columns of Y are scaled by |r0|
  relative to the barycentre, about 1.5e11 m, and the step control fails, with or without drag; propagate relative to
  the Earth. (The noise of the Earth's attraction in SSB mode, #544 and #576, is fixed in this release.)
- **Integration accuracy** ([#445](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/445)).
  At 1e-11 the 3 h error of RK7(8) in LEO with drag and SRP spans 0.94
  to 36.2 mm with the placement of the steps around the eclipse. The orientation cache of a propagation is built for
  every central body, whether or not a force rotates, so each of its 60 s points past the
  coverage of the orientation kernel goes through the native read, which printed its SPICE message on standard output
  (123 lines for 2 h, measured before the fix of [#454](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/454); nothing since #727): a point-mass
  propagation there still runs ([#595](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/595)).
- **Force model inputs** ([#674](https://github.com/IO-Aerospace-software-engineering/Astrodynamics/issues/674)). A configured `Nrlmsise00Model` shared by parallel propagations serializes their
  density calls on its lock (4 threads × 200 000 densities: 5.8 s on one instance, 0.9 s on one per thread); the default
  atmosphere of a model-less Earth is one instance per thread, so give each parallel propagation its own configured
  model. A custom `IAtmosphericModel` compares by `Equals`, so two separately built instances on bodies of one NAIF
